urlbar-toolbar.summary: The address bar and toolbar are unusually well thought through for a SwiftUI browser: one pill for both display and edit modes, a real AppKit field editor so drags select text instead of moving the window, per-window balanced button groups, and a shared radius/shadow scale. The damage is concentrated in three places: ⌘L has no owner at all when both the sidebar and the toolbar are hidden (compact mode), clicking the field almost never selects the URL because the re-select hop fires while the mouse button is still down, and the "..." menu's zoom rows bypass SiteZoomController so they neither persist nor agree with the ⌘+ shortcut printed next to them. The rest is smaller: no stop control while a page loads, an "Aura 1.2.3" version pill drawn next to every hovered link, two different security-icon vocabularies between the toolbar and the sidebar pill, and a dead ShareLinkButton.swift.

kept.title: ⌘L and ⇧⌘C do nothing in compact mode: no view owns the shortcut
kept.evidence: ⌘L is owned only by two hidden buttons: `URLBarField.swift:117-123` (`Button("") { startEditing() }.oraShortcut(KeyboardShortcuts.Address.focus)`) and `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:116-126` (same, `.disabled(!toolbarManager.isToolbarHidden)`). `URLBarField` is only ever built by `TopToolbar` (`TopToolbar.swift:73`), which `BrowserView.swift:130` mounts only `if isToolbarRowUp`. `SidebarURLDisplay` is built by `ContainerView.swift:23`, inside `SidebarView`, which `BrowserSplitView.swift:71` renders through `HSplit(...).hide(sidebarManager.hiddenSidebar)`; the vendored `Split.swift:86-92` does `if !hidePrimary { ... }`, i.e. the hidden side is not in the hierarchy at all. `SidebarManager.applyCompactMode` (`SidebarManager.swift:194-201`) sets both `setSidebarHidden(true)` and `toolbar.setHidden(true)`. Nothing else registers `Address.focus`: `OraCommands` has no Open Location item, and `rg` finds `Address.focus` only in those two files. `.copyAddressURL` has the same hole (`URLBarField.swift:164`, `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:132`).
kept.user_impact: In compact mode, or with the sidebar and toolbar both hidden by hand, ⌘L and ⇧⌘C are silently dead until the user hovers a window edge to reveal chrome. This is exactly the "sometimes the launcher shortcut does nothing" class of complaint.
kept.fix: Prefer reusing the machinery that already exists over a new hidden overlay in BrowserView. Add a File menu row in OraCommands.swift next to the other window-scoped items (`Button("Open Location…") { NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .focusAddressBar, object: NSApp.keyWindow) }.oraShortcut(KeyboardShortcuts.Address.focus)`), add `.focusAddressBar` to AppEvents.swift, and add one row to OraRoot's `events` table (OraRoot.swift:372+) with scope `.windowOrKey`: `if toolbarManager.isToolbarHidden && sidebarManager.isSidebarHidden { appState.showLauncher = true; appState.launcherFocusToken += 1 } else { appState.isURLBarEditing = true }`. Then delete both hidden Buttons (URLBarField.swift:117-123, SidebarURLDisplay.swift:117-126); URLBarField already reacts to `appState.isURLBarEditing`, and SidebarURLDisplay needs a small `.onChange(of: appState.isURLBarEditing)` that calls `openLauncher()`. Do the same for `.copyAddressURL` (see urlbar-toolbar-6): post with `NSApp.keyWindow` and route it through the same table so it works with no address surface mounted. This keeps the shortcut discoverable in the menu bar and gets window scoping for free.
kept.verify_reason: Verified end to end. `Address.focus` is registered only at URLBarField.swift:119 and SidebarURLDisplay.swift:118; rg finds no other owner and OraCommands has no Open Location item. TopToolbar is mounted only under `if isToolbarRowUp` (BrowserView.swift:130-133), SidebarURLDisplay only inside ContainerView.swift:23-25 (`toolbarManager.isToolbarHidden && !isFloatingToolbarVisible`) and inside the sidebar pane, which Split.swift drops from the hierarchy when hidden. SidebarManager.applyCompactMode (SidebarManager.swift:194-201) hides both, and `compactHides` defaults to `.both` (SidebarManager.swift:105-106), so plain compact mode kills ⌘L and ⇧⌘C until the user hovers the top edge.

kept.title: Clicking the address bar leaves a caret instead of selecting the URL
kept.evidence: `CustomTextField.mouseDown` focuses the field, then re-selects on one main-queue hop: `DispatchQueue.main.async { ... guard NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons == 0 else { return }; currentEditor()?.selectAll(nil) }` (lines 131-137). That hop runs in the same event pass as the mouse-down, long before the user releases, so `pressedMouseButtons` is still 1 and the selection is skipped. The `selectAll` in `becomeFirstResponder` (line 105) has already been undone by the cell installing the field editor, which is what the comment on line 128 says.
kept.user_impact: A normal click on the address bar drops a caret mid-URL instead of selecting the whole address, so typing a new address appends to the old one. Select-all only happens if the click is released inside a single run-loop turn.
kept.fix: Two corrections to the snippet. `var upMonitor: Any?` must be `var upMonitor: Any? = nil`, or Swift rejects the capture-before-initialization in the closure. And the monitor must not outlive the field: keep it in a stored property on `CustomTextField` and remove it in `deinit` (and before installing a new one), the way `URLBarField` handles `mouseMonitor`. Before writing the fix, confirm the premise by checking whether a click currently leaves a caret; if the selection is already full after a click, delete the dead async block instead.
kept.verify_reason: The code is as described (LauncherTextField.swift:118-138): the branch returns without calling super, so no NSTextView tracking loop runs, the `DispatchQueue.main.async` block drains on the very next run-loop turn, and `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` is still 1 for the ~100 ms the button is held. So that re-select is effectively dead code. I could not confirm from source alone that the cell really leaves a caret (the claim rests on the comment at lines 128-130), which is why this is not high: if that comment is stale, `becomeFirstResponder`'s selectAll (line 105) already holds and the user sees nothing wrong.

kept.title: No stop control: the reload button never becomes a stop button
kept.evidence: `historyGroup` always builds `toolbarButton(.reload, isEnabled: tabManager.activeTab != nil, action: { tabManager.activeTab?.reload() })` (lines 159-164). `BrowserPage.stopLoading()` exists (`BrowserPage.swift:323`) but `rg` finds no caller outside the engine's own teardown, and no Esc handler or menu item stops a load. `Tab.isLoading` is already tracked and consumed by `URLBarField.swift:288`.
kept.user_impact: A page that hangs on a slow resource cannot be stopped from the chrome; the only way out is navigating somewhere else or closing the tab.
kept.fix: The proposed snippet works (`toolbarButton(_:isEnabled:action:)` has a String overload, TopToolbar.swift:209-221) and ToolbarIconTests only counts `ToolbarIcon.allCases`, so an SF Symbol is safe. One caveat: `.reload` is a bundled 16pt Firefox glyph while `xmark` renders at URLBarButton.iconSize (13pt, regular), so pick `xmark` at the same optical weight as the other SF-symbol chrome buttons (gearshape, ellipsis) or the row will visibly jitter between the two states. Reuse the existing `tabManager.activeTab?.browserPage?.stopLoading()` call and give it `.help("Stop Loading")` plus `.accessibilityLabel`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: TopToolbar.swift:159-164 always builds the reload button, `BrowserPage.stopLoading()` (BrowserPage.swift:323) has no caller outside the engine and the paint probe, and there is no Esc or menu path that stops a load. `Tab.isLoading` is already observed by the field's spinner (URLBarField.swift:288-292), so the toggle costs nothing extra.

kept.title: The "..." menu's zoom rows bypass SiteZoomController, so zoom is lost on the next navigation
kept.evidence: `setZoom` writes the web view directly: `webView.pageZoom = transform(webView.pageZoom)` (line 193), driven by rows that step 0.1 and clamp 0.5...3.0 (lines 127, 135, 143). Every other zoom path goes through `SiteZoomController` (`OraRoot.swift:472-475` for ⌘+/⌘-, `SiteInfoMenu.swift:188-201`), which stores the level per registrable domain and steps the `SiteZoom.levels` ladder. `TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:240` calls `SiteZoomController.apply(to:url:)` on every navigation, which re-asserts the stored level.
kept.user_impact: Zoom In from the "..." menu moves by a different amount than the ⌘+ printed on the same row, is never remembered for the site, does not light up the `SiteZoomBadge` in the address pill, and is thrown away on the next page load in that tab.
kept.fix: Delete `setZoom` and point the three rows at the shared controller, the way `SiteInfoMenu.zoomItems` already does: `SiteZoomController.step(1, for: tabManager.activeTab)`, `SiteZoomController.step(-1, for: tabManager.activeTab)`, `SiteZoomController.reset(tabManager.activeTab)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. URLBarMenuButton.setZoom (URLBarMenuButton.swift:191-194) writes `webView.pageZoom` directly with a 0.1 step, while SiteZoomController.step walks the SiteZoom.levels ladder and persists per registrable domain (SiteZoom.swift:76-95), and SiteInfoMenu.zoomItems (SiteInfoMenu.swift:180-202) already does exactly what the fix proposes. Nothing re-reads pageZoom, so the menu's value is lost on the next navigation.

kept.title: Hovering any link draws an "Aura 1.2.3" version pill next to the URL
kept.evidence: `LinkPreview` renders the hovered URL bottom-left and, in the same HStack after a `Spacer`, `Text(getAppVersion())` reading `CFBundleShortVersionString` into a filled pill (lines 7-10, 37-46). `BrowserWebContentView.swift:159-163` mounts it for every non-empty `tab.hoveredLinkURL`. The URL `Text` has `lineLimit(1)`/`truncationMode(.middle)` but no width limit, so a long address grows the row until the version pill is pushed to the far edge.
kept.user_impact: Every link hover during normal browsing flashes a build-number badge across the bottom of the page. No browser does this; it reads as leftover debug chrome and undercuts the custom-designed look.
kept.fix: Same fix, plus one thing the auditor missed: the whole `VStack`/`HStack` fills the web content and the pill's `RoundedRectangle` background is hit-testable over the page, so add `.allowsHitTesting(false)` to the LinkPreview root while you are in the file.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading the file: LinkPreview.swift:7-10 reads CFBundleShortVersionString and lines 37-46 draw it as a filled pill next to the hovered URL, mounted for every hover at BrowserWebContentView.swift:160-163. No browser shows a build number on link hover; this is leftover debug chrome.

kept.title: ⇧⌘C copies from every open window and stacks a toast per window
kept.evidence: The menu posts `NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .copyAddressURL, object: nil)` (line 83), and both consumers subscribe without any window check: `URLBarField.swift:164-171` and `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:132-140` each run `ClipboardUtils.copyWithToast(activeTab.url...)`. Every other window-scoped event in the app posts `object: NSApp.keyWindow` and is filtered by `WindowEventScope.accepts` (`OraRoot.swift:316-333`).
kept.user_impact: With two browser windows open, ⇧⌘C copies whichever window's URLBarField happens to run last, so the clipboard can hold the background window's address, and both windows show a "Link copied" toast.
kept.fix: Fold this into urlbar-toolbar-1's fix: post `object: NSApp.keyWindow` from OraCommands.swift:83 and from the `.copyAddressURL` AppCommand (AppCommand.swift:77), and handle it in OraRoot's `events` table with scope `.windowOrKey` (the sidebar pill lives in an NSHostingView and gets no `\.window`, which is why `.window` alone would drop posts). That leaves one receiver per window and removes the duplicated copy block from both views.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. OraCommands.swift:82-85 posts `.copyAddressURL` with `object: nil`; URLBarField.swift:164-171 has no window guard, and OraRoot's `WindowEventScope` machinery (OraRoot.swift:306-334) exists precisely for this. TabManager and ToastManager are per-window (`OraRoot.swift:36,98`), so with two windows both receivers fire against their own tab and both toast.

kept.title: The URL you are typing is drawn at 70% opacity, against the field's own doc comment
kept.evidence: `textColor: isEditing ? textColor.opacity(0.7) : foregroundColor` (line 215), while the property doc at lines 11-13 says textColor is the "Full-strength colour used for typed text and the caret". The caret is separately set to `textColor.opacity(0.8)` (line 214). `TopToolbar.swift:75-76` passes `theme.foreground` undimmed exactly so this can be full strength.
kept.user_impact: The address text is the one thing being edited and it is the dimmest text in the row, on an 8%-fill pill. Under the editing backdrop's extra dim (`BrowserView.swift:85`) it drops further, which reads as disabled rather than focused.
kept.fix: Either change line 215 to `textColor` and drop the caret's `.opacity(0.8)` on line 214, or leave both and fix the doc comment on lines 11-13 to say the field dims by 0.7 while editing. Do not claim a contrast fix without measuring: `theme.foreground` at 0.7 over the 8% pill fill is already above 4.5:1 in both themes.
kept.verify_reason: The factual half holds: URLBarField.swift:215 dims typed text to 0.7 while the property doc at lines 11-13 promises full strength. The user-impact half is wrong and I am downgrading for it: idle text uses `foregroundColor`, which TopToolbar.swift:75 passes as `theme.foreground.opacity(0.55)`, so the editing text at 0.7 is in fact brighter than the idle text, not the dimmest thing in the row. This is a doc/code mismatch and a mild contrast miss, not a state that reads as disabled.

kept.title: No "not secure" state, and two different security icon vocabularies
kept.evidence: `securitySymbol` returns `shield.lefthalf.filled` for https and plain `globe` for everything else (lines 301-304), so an http page is marked with the same neutral glyph an unknown scheme gets. `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:41-45` uses a third vocabulary for the same state: `shield.slash` for non-https and nothing at all for https. The accessibility label on the button is the constant `Text("Site information")` (`URLBarField.swift:197`) regardless of state, while `SiteInfoMenu` already computes `connectionSummary` ("Connection is not encrypted").
kept.user_impact: An http page is visually indistinguishable from an https one in the toolbar, and the sidebar pill says the opposite thing about the same page. VoiceOver never announces whether the connection is encrypted.
kept.fix: The proposed `scheme == "https" ? shield : exclamationmark.shield` mis-marks pages that are not insecure: `aura://` internal pages and `file://` URLs would both draw a warning. Gate on the scheme set instead: warn only for `http`, keep `globe` for `file`/`aura`/unknown, keep the shield for `https`. Reuse `SiteInfoSummary.connectionSummary` for the accessibility label rather than writing a second string, and note that `editingSymbol` (URLBarField.swift:306-308) already uses `globe` for a typed-URL hint, so freeing `globe` from double duty is part of the win. Apply the same pair in SidebarURLDisplay so the two surfaces stop disagreeing.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed all three vocabularies: URLBarField.swift:301-304 (`shield.lefthalf.filled` / `globe`), SidebarURLDisplay.swift:41-45 (`shield.slash` for non-https, nothing for https), SiteInfoMenu.swift:96-99 (`lock.fill` / `exclamationmark.triangle`). The button's label is the constant `Text("Site information")` (URLBarField.swift:197) even though `SiteInfoSummary.connectionSummary` (SiteInfoMenu.swift:59-61) already has the right words. An http page carrying the same glyph as an unknown scheme is a real security-UX gap.

kept.title: The JavaScript submenu offers "Allow on home" for aura:// pages
kept.evidence: `pageSection` passes the raw URL: `.submenu("JavaScript", icon: "curlybraces", items: JavaScriptSiteMenu.items(for: tabManager.activeTab?.url))` (line 115). `JavaScriptSiteMenu.items` only guards on `url.host` being non-empty (`JavaScriptSiteMenu.swift:11`), and `aura://home` parses with host `home`, which `registrableDomain(from:)` returns unchanged (`Utils.swift:26`). `SiteInfoMenu` has the guard the submenu is missing (`SiteInfoMenu.swift:37`, `guard !url.isOraInternal`), and `SiteZoomController.set` carries the same guard with the same comment (`SiteZoom.swift:92`).
kept.user_impact: On the home, settings or extensions page the menu offers "Allow on home (default)" / "Block on home", and choosing one writes a permanent policy rule for a site that does not exist. `JavaScriptPolicyService.isAllowed` short-circuits internal URLs anyway, so the row can never do anything.
kept.fix: Move the guard into the shared builder so both callers get it, matching the existing wording: in `JavaScriptSiteMenu.items`, `guard let url, !url.isOraInternal, let host = url.host.map(...)` and keep the `[.disabled("No site loaded")]` fallback.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: JavaScriptSiteMenu.items (JavaScriptSiteMenu.swift:9-13) guards only on a non-empty host, `aura://home` parses with host `home`, and URLBarMenuButton.swift:115 hands it the raw URL while SiteInfoMenu goes through `SiteInfoSummary.init?`, which does carry the `!url.isOraInternal` guard (SiteInfoMenu.swift:37). Downgraded from medium: the rows are only reachable two levels into the "..." menu, the written rule is inert because `JavaScriptPolicyService.isAllowed` short-circuits internal URLs, and it is one orphan defaults entry.

kept.title: The site-info button opens a one-row dead menu on about:blank and data: URLs
kept.evidence: The button is disabled for `tab == nil || isEditing || tab?.url.isOraInternal == true` (line 193), with the comment "an empty menu is worse than no button". But `SiteInfoSummary.init?` also returns nil for anything without a registrable domain (`SiteInfoMenu.swift:37-42`, and its own doc says "nil for anything without a site to describe: about:blank, a data URL"), and `SiteInfoMenu.items` then answers `[.disabled("No site loaded")]` (line 91).
kept.user_impact: On about:blank, a data: URL or a freshly opened blank tab the lock is clickable and opens a menu containing one greyed row, which is the exact outcome the code says it is avoiding.
kept.fix: Do not call `SiteInfoMenu.summary(for:tabManager:)` from the `.disabled` modifier: it runs `SiteSpaceRuleService.containerID`, `tabManager.fetchContainers()` (a SwiftData fetch) and three SettingsStore reads on every toolbar render. Test the cheap precondition instead, which is the same one the initialiser fails on: `.disabled(tab == nil || isEditing || tab.map { $0.url.isOraInternal || registrableDomain(from: $0.url) == nil } ?? true)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: URLBarField.swift:193 disables the button only for nil tab, editing, or `isOraInternal`, while `SiteInfoSummary.init?` also returns nil whenever `registrableDomain(from: url)` is nil (SiteInfoMenu.swift:35-42, Utils.swift:40-44), and `SiteInfoMenu.items` then answers a single disabled row (SiteInfoMenu.swift:90-92). Worth noting the auditor undersold it: `file://` URLs have no host either, so opening a local PDF also gets the dead menu. Downgraded to low because about:blank and data: URLs are rare in normal browsing.

kept.title: A 150 ms timer swallows the search for the first characters typed after ⌘L
kept.evidence: `startEditing` sets `suppressInitialSearch = true` (line 370), `setupInlineLauncher` sets it again (line 379) and clears it on a wall-clock delay: `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.15) { suppressInitialSearch = false }` (lines 392-394). Until then `onChange(of: launcherInput)` updates `launcherViewModel.currentText` but returns before `searchHandler(newValue)` (lines 231-236).
kept.user_impact: Press ⌘L, type one or two characters quickly, then pause: the suggestion list never appears, because the only keystrokes that would have triggered a search landed inside the suppression window. The next keystroke fixes it, which reads as the launcher randomly not responding.
kept.fix: The prefilled-value comparison is right but note the edge: `cleanupInlineLauncher` clears `launcherInput` asynchronously (URLBarField.swift:419-425), so reset `prefilledInput` there too, otherwise a later edit that happens to type its way back to the old URL silently skips one search.
kept.verify_reason: The mechanism is real: `suppressInitialSearch` is set in startEditing (URLBarField.swift:370) and again in setupInlineLauncher (line 379), cleared on a 0.15 s wall clock (lines 392-394), and the `onChange` handler returns before `searchHandler` while it is set (lines 231-236). Downgraded from medium because the window is 150 ms from the keypress that opened the field, only search is suppressed (currentText still updates), and the next keystroke recovers; the user has to type and then stop inside that window to notice.

kept.title: A long press released off the back button swallows the next click on it
kept.evidence: `didLongPress` is set by the `LongPressGesture` (lines 51-57) and only cleared inside the `Button` action (lines 39-42). The action fires only when the release lands on the button and is not consumed elsewhere; `AuraMenuHost.handleMouse` consumes any mouse-up whose `eventWindow === menuWindow` (`AuraMenuHost.swift:104-110, 132`), and the presented panel can sit over the button it hangs from.
kept.user_impact: After holding back or forward to open its history menu and releasing away from the button (or over the menu panel), the next single click on that button does nothing; the user clicks twice.
kept.fix: The timestamp version works. Compare against `URLBarButton.longPressDuration` rather than a fresh literal: `guard Date().timeIntervalSince(lastLongPress) > Self.longPressDuration else { return }`, so one constant governs both ends.
kept.verify_reason: The stale-flag path is real: `didLongPress` (URLBarButton.swift:35) is cleared only inside the Button action (lines 39-42), which needs a release inside the button's bounds. The common case is safe (the implicit grab delivers the mouseUp to the browser window and the pointer is still over the button), but the press-hold-drag-into-the-menu-and-release gesture leaves the flag set, and `AuraMenuHost.handleMouse` only sees events whose window is the menu panel (AuraMenuHost.swift:104-110), so nothing else clears it. Low: costs one extra click, no state loss.

kept.title: Address-bar event monitors leak if the toolbar hides mid-edit
kept.evidence: `clickAwayMonitor` is installed in `.onChange(of: isEditing, initial: true)` and removed only by the same `onChange` when editing ends (lines 127-145); `mouseMonitor` is removed only from `cleanupInlineLauncher` (lines 415-418), which also runs off `onChange(of: isEditing)`. Neither has an `.onDisappear`. `BrowserView.swift:130` unmounts `TopToolbar` whenever `isToolbarRowUp` goes false, and `FloatingTopToolbar` does exactly that when the reveal times out (`BrowserView.swift:325`, `GlobalMouseTrackingArea.scheduleHide`).
kept.user_impact: Hiding the toolbar (⌥⌘T, compact mode, or a hover reveal that hides) while the address bar is focused leaves an app-wide `.leftMouseDown`/`.rightMouseDown` monitor running for the rest of the session, retaining the dead view's `appState` and running a hit test on every click in every window.
kept.fix: Same teardown, but state the real trigger in the comment (window closed or the row toggled away mid-edit, not a hover timeout), and guard it against the normal path: `.onDisappear` runs after `onChange` has already nil'd the monitors on a clean dismiss, so the `if let` checks are what keep it idempotent.
kept.verify_reason: There is genuinely no `.onDisappear` in URLBarField (grep confirms only the two comments at lines 106 and 411), and both monitors are torn down solely from `.onChange(of: isEditing)`. The auditor's main trigger is wrong though: `FloatingTopToolbar.isHeld` includes `appState.isURLBarEditing` (BrowserView.swift:299-301), so a hover reveal cannot time out mid-edit. The reachable leaks are ⌥⌘T / compact-mode toggles taken while the field is focused, and closing the window mid-edit, where the local monitor and its captured `appState` outlive the window.

kept.title: Window control buttons are tap gestures with no label, no keyboard access and no reduce-motion-safe feedback
kept.evidence: `WindowControlButton` is an `Image` with `.onTapGesture { performAction() }` (lines 63-85). There is no `Button`, no `.accessibilityLabel`, no `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)`, no `.help`, and no press state; every other chrome control in the area uses `Button` + `.buttonStyle(.interactive(...))` + label + help (e.g. `TopToolbar.swift:286-290`). Used by `SidebarHeader.swift:23`, `HistoryPanelView.swift:66`, `DownloadsHistoryView.swift:38`, `FilesPanelView.swift:37`.
kept.user_impact: VoiceOver reads the close/minimize/zoom controls as unlabelled images with no action, keyboard users cannot reach them, and there is no pressed feedback, so a click that misses registers as nothing.
kept.fix: Keep the hover art exactly as it is: the three images already encode hover and no-focus states, so wrap in `Button { performAction() } label: { ... }.buttonStyle(.plain)` and do not add `.interactive`, which would paint a second highlight behind the asset. Add `.help`/`.accessibilityLabel` per type.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: WindowControlButton is an `Image` with `.onTapGesture` (WindowControls.swift:63-85), no Button, no label, no traits, no pressed state, while every other chrome control in the area goes through `URLBarButton` with `.buttonStyle(.interactive(...))` plus a label. Low rather than medium: close, minimize and zoom all have menu-bar equivalents (⌘W, ⌘M, ⌃⌘F), so nothing is unreachable, and macOS's own traffic lights are not keyboard targets either.

kept.title: Copy feedback says two different things and ignores reduce motion
kept.evidence: The copy button runs `ClipboardUtils.triggerCopy`, which animates `CopiedURLOverlay`'s `Text("Copied Current URL")` (`CopiedURLOverlay.swift:11`), while ⇧⌘C on the same URL runs `copyWithToast` with the message "Link copied" (`ClipboardUtils.swift:40`). `triggerCopy` also drives its state with bare `withAnimation { }` (lines 26-35), i.e. SwiftUI's default spring, while every view in this area animates through `AnimationSettings.easeOut(...)`, which is what honours the app's reduce-motion preference (`AnimationSettings.swift:18-24`).
kept.user_impact: The same action reports itself two different ways with two different phrasings, and the inline version keeps animating with reduce motion turned on.
kept.fix: Change the overlay copy to `Text("Link copied")` to match the toast, and swap the two bare `withAnimation { }` calls in `triggerCopy` for `withAnimation(AnimationSettings.easeOut(0.15))`.
kept.verify_reason: Both halves check out: CopiedURLOverlay.swift:11 says "Copied Current URL" while ClipboardUtils.copyWithToast defaults to "Link copied" (ClipboardUtils.swift:40), and `triggerCopy` uses bare `withAnimation` twice (lines 26 and 31) where AnimationSettings.easeOut is what zeroes duration under reduce motion (AnimationSettings.swift:18-24).

kept.title: ShareLinkButton.swift is dead code
kept.evidence: `rg -n "ShareLinkButton"` across the repo returns only the declaration itself (line 4). Sharing is reached through `URLBarMenuButton`'s "Share link" row and `TopToolbar.shareCurrentPage` (`TopToolbar.swift:188-193, 320-327`), which use their own `AuraMenuAnchorView` anchor. The file also carries its own private `ShareSourceView` anchor duplicating that helper, and a `// Nothing to update` comment.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime; it is 47 lines of duplicate anchor plumbing that reads as a live component and will be copied the next time someone needs a share button.
kept.fix: Delete `aura/Features/Browser/Components/ShareLinkButton.swift` and its Xcode project reference.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: `rg ShareLinkButton` outside the project file returns only the declaration at ShareLinkButton.swift:4; sharing runs through URLBarMenuButton's row and TopToolbar.shareCurrentPage. The pbxproj carries three references (build file, file ref, group membership) that all have to go with it.

kept.title: URLBarField documents and carries a floating URL bar that no longer exists
kept.evidence: The type doc says "Address field shared by the top toolbar and the floating URL bar" (lines 4-5), but `TopToolbar.swift:73` is the only construction site. The flip-up machinery that exists for that second bar (`suggestionsFlipUp`, lines 85-89, with the comment "A floating URL bar near the bottom of the window would drop its list off-screen") can never fire from a 38pt row pinned to the top of the window. `URLBarMenuButton`'s doc has the same stale claim (line 6), and `onTab: {}` (line 209) silently drops Tab completion that the launcher's own field implements.
kept.user_impact: None visible; it misdescribes the architecture for anyone touching the suggestion overlay and keeps unreachable geometry alive.
kept.fix: Only fix the two doc comments, and reword the one on lines 84-86 to name the real trigger (a window too short to fit 160pt of list below the field). Leave `suggestionsFlipUp` and `suggestionsSpace.above` alone. Drop the `onTab` suggestion as written: the launcher's Tab does search-engine alias completion (LauncherView.swift:26-36), not suggestion walking, so mapping it to `moveFocusedElement(.down)` would make the two fields behave differently, which is the opposite of the point. Either mirror the alias completion or leave `onTab: {}`.
kept.verify_reason: The stale doc claim is right (URLBarField.swift:4-5 and URLBarMenuButton.swift:6 both mention a floating URL bar; TopToolbar.swift:73 is the only construction site of either). The "can never fire" claim about the flip is wrong: `suggestionsFlipUp` triggers whenever `space.below < 160`, which a short window produces even with the field pinned to the top, so that geometry is a live small-window guard, not dead code.

kept.title: Hardcoded ⌘Y in the menu and a literal divider colour in the toolbar
kept.evidence: `AuraMenuItem.item("Show All History", icon: "clock", shortcut: "⌘Y")` (line 163) hardcodes a chord that `KeyboardShortcuts.History.show` owns and the user can rebind in settings (`KeyboardShortcuts.swift:236-243`); every neighbouring row passes the definition (`shortcut: KeyboardShortcuts.App.preferences`, line 150). Separately, `TopToolbar.swift:98-100` paints its group separator with `Rectangle().fill(theme.foreground.opacity(0.2))` instead of `theme.border`, which is what every other chrome hairline uses.
kept.user_impact: Rebinding Show History leaves the menu advertising the old chord, and the toolbar's one divider is a different grey from every other 1pt line in the window.
kept.fix: Apply only the shortcut change (`shortcut: KeyboardShortcuts.History.show` at URLBarMenuButton.swift:163) and drop TopToolbar.swift from files_to_touch. Leave the separator as `theme.foreground.opacity(0.2)`; swapping it to `theme.border` would break it away from the glass-adaptive foreground the rest of the row uses.
kept.verify_reason: The ⌘Y half is confirmed: URLBarMenuButton.swift:163 hardcodes the chord while `KeyboardShortcuts.History.show` exists (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:237) and is user-rebindable, and the neighbouring rows pass definitions. The divider half I could not support: the toolbar row is drawn under `auraGlassChromeForeground()` and its separator deliberately keys off the same `theme.foreground` as every icon in the row, and I found no app-wide convention of `theme.border` for vertical group separators.

kept.title: ⌘Y, the "..." menu's panels and ⌘G act on every open window at once
kept.evidence: BrowserView subscribes to `.findNext`, `.findPrevious`, `.toggleSidebar`, `.toggleSidebarPosition`, `.toggleCompactMode`, `.showHistoryPanel` and `.showDownloadsPanel` with plain `.onReceive` and no window check (BrowserView.swift:215-241). The posters do scope: OraCommands.swift:71,76 send `NSApp.keyWindow`, OraCommands.swift:311 sends `NSApp.keyWindow`, URLBarMenuButton.swift:84,164 send `hostWindow`, and OraCommands.swift:110,131 send nil. Every other window-scoped event in the app is filtered through `WindowEventScope.accepts` in OraRoot's routing table (OraRoot.swift:306-334, 372+), and BrowserView does not even read `@Environment(\.window)`.
kept.user_impact: With two browser windows open, ⌘Y opens the history panel in both, the "..." menu's Downloads row opens the panel in both, ⌘G steps the find match in the background window's tab as well, and Toggle Sidebar / Toggle Compact Mode flip every window at once. The background window silently changes layout behind the one being used.
kept.fix: Add `@Environment(\.window) private var window` to BrowserView and gate the seven handlers with the rule the app already owns: `guard WindowEventScope.window.accepts(note, window: window) else { return }` (use `.windowOrKey` for the two the sidebar posts with a nil window). While there, post `object: NSApp.keyWindow` from OraCommands.swift:110 and :131 so `.toggleSidebar` and `.toggleSidebarPosition` carry a sender at all.

kept.title: A second ⌘L does nothing, and the address field can never be re-focused from the keyboard
kept.evidence: `startEditing` opens with `guard !isEditing else { return }` (URLBarField.swift:369), and URLBarField constructs `LauncherTextField` without `focusToken` (URLBarField.swift:205-222), so it stays 0 forever. `LauncherTextField.focusToken`'s own doc (LauncherTextField.swift:20-23) says the launcher bumps it on every ⌘T precisely so "a panel that lost the caret gets it back", and LauncherView passes `appState.launcherFocusToken` (LauncherView.swift:201), incremented in OraRoot.swift:385. The address field has no equivalent: `updateNSView` only re-asks for first responder when `isEditing != focused` changes or the token moves (LauncherTextField.swift:189-204), and with `appState.isURLBarEditing` already true and the token frozen, nothing re-asks.
kept.user_impact: Pressing ⌘L while the address bar is already in edit mode is a complete no-op, where Safari and Chrome re-select the whole URL. Worse, any state where `isURLBarEditing` is true but the field lost first responder (a panel or extension popup took focus, an AppKit responder shuffle) cannot be recovered with the keyboard at all: the shortcut returns immediately and the user has to reach for the mouse. That is the second half of the owner's complaint, the field being open with the caret nowhere.
kept.fix: Mirror the launcher. Add `@State private var focusToken = 0` to URLBarField, pass `focusToken: focusToken` into `LauncherTextField`, and change `startEditing` to bump it and select all instead of bailing: replace the guard with `focusToken += 1; guard !isEditing else { return }` so a repeat ⌘L re-asserts first responder, and let the existing `becomeFirstResponder` select-all do the rest.

settings.summary: The settings shell is genuinely well built: one gutter scale, one card, a hand-made search field, a persisted section that survives renames, and doc comments that mostly explain why. The rot is at the leaves. Search Engines and Spaces read like the oldest code in the app (stock push buttons, "Name:" label columns, Title Case labels, destructive clears with no confirmation, a rename that silently drops the default), the shortcut rebinding UI captures keys without swallowing them so ⌘W closes the tab you are configuring, and the passwords page ships a one-option picker with three unreachable branches behind it. Nothing here loses browsing data except the unconfirmed Clear History in Spaces, but a demanding user hits the mixed stock-and-custom chrome within one scroll.

kept.title: Rebinding a shortcut also fires the key it captures, and accepts Escape or a bare letter as a binding
kept.evidence: The capture overlay uses `KeyCaptureView(onKeyDown: { event in handleKeyCapture(event) })`. That init (KeyCaptureView.swift:6-11) wraps the closure as `{ event in onKeyDown(event); return event }`, so the local monitor returns the event and the app still performs it. The sibling init `onKeyDownResult` (line 13) is the one that can return nil and swallow. `handleKeyCapture` then accepts anything `KeyChord(fromEvent:)` builds, and `KeyChord.init?(fromEvent:)` (aura/Core/Domain/Keyboard.swift:66-78) only fails when there is no character at all: modifier flags are optional and `kVK_Escape` is in `namedKeys`. Pressing Escape to back out records Escape as the shortcut; pressing ⌘W while capturing records ⌘W and closes the settings tab underneath the capture; a plain "a" becomes a menu key equivalent with no modifier.
kept.user_impact: Trying to rebind a command performs the old command instead (⌘W closes the tab, ⌘Q asks to quit), there is no keyboard way to cancel, and a stray keystroke can bind a bare letter that then fires the command on every press of that letter.
kept.fix: Switch the overlay to the swallowing init and filter the event: `KeyCaptureView(onKeyDownResult: { event in handleKeyCapture(event); return nil })`. In `handleKeyCapture`, before setting: `if event.keyCode == UInt16(kVK_Escape) { cancelEditing(); return }` and `guard !event.modifierFlags.intersection([.command, .option, .control]).isEmpty else { return }` with a comment that a menu key equivalent without a modifier fires on every plain keystroke. `Carbon.HIToolbox` is already the import `Keyboard.swift` uses for `kVK_Escape`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading both files. ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:63 uses KeyCaptureView(onKeyDown:), and KeyCaptureView.swift:6-11 wraps that closure to return the event, so the local monitor passes it on and the app performs the key it just captured. KeyChord.init?(fromEvent:) (Keyboard.swift:66-78) only fails when charactersIgnoringModifiers is empty and kVK_Escape is in namedKeys (line 59), so Escape and a bare letter both bind. handleKeyCapture (line 86-93) adds no filter.

kept.title: Clear Cache, Clear Cookies and Clear History in Spaces run with no confirmation
kept.evidence: `clearButton("Clear Cache") { PrivacyService.clearCache(container) ... }`, `clearButton("Clear Cookies")` and `clearButton("Clear History") { historyManager.clearContainerHistory(container) }` all act on the first press. The same destructive work one section over goes through the shared dialog: `PrivacySettingsView.confirmClear()` (PrivacySettingsView.swift:273-284) calls `dialogManager.confirm(title: "Clear browsing data?", …, variant: .destructive)`, and `PermissionsSettingsView.clearSiteData(for:)` (line 180) does the same for a single host.
kept.user_impact: A misclick on a page of ordinary pickers signs the user out of every site in that space or deletes that space's history with no undo.
kept.fix: Route the three buttons through the confirm the page can already reach. Add `@Environment(DialogManager.self) private var dialogManager` and wrap the action: `dialogManager.confirm(title: "Clear \(what) for \"\(container.name)\"?", message: …, iconImage: Image(systemName: "trash"), confirmLabel: "Clear", variant: .destructive, onConfirm: action)` inside `clearButton`, so all three inherit it from one place.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. SpacesSettingsView.swift:180-196 wires the three clearButton calls straight to PrivacyService.clearCache/clearCookies and historyManager.clearContainerHistory; the toast at the end is the only feedback. The precedent the finding cites is real: PrivacySettingsView.swift:276 and PermissionsSettingsView.swift:180 both route the same work through dialogManager.confirm(..., variant: .destructive), and DialogManager.confirm has exactly that signature (DialogManager.swift:49-58). SpacesSettingsView has no dialogManager today, so the environment property has to be added.

kept.title: Renaming a custom search engine silently drops it as the default
kept.evidence: Defaults are stored by name: `settings.globalDefaultSearchEngine = engine.name` (line 159) and per space `settings.setDefaultSearchEngineId($0, …)` with `Text(engine.name).tag(Optional(engine.name))` (SpacesSettingsView.swift:66). `SearchEngineService.getDefaultSearchEngine` matches `searchEngines.first { $0.name == globalDefaultId }` and falls back to Google when nothing matches (SearchEngineService.swift:262-268). `saveEdit()` writes the renamed engine through `updateCustomSearchEngine` and never touches either stored default; `onDelete` (line 152) does remember to clear the global one, so the omission is only on the rename path.
kept.user_impact: Fix a typo in a custom engine's name and every search silently goes to Google again, and any space pinned to that engine falls back too, with no message anywhere.
kept.fix: Carrying the global default is the one-liner the finding describes. The per-space ids need setDefaultSearchEngineId over every container, which SearchEngineSettingsView has no container list for; simpler and equally correct is to key defaults by engine.id instead of name, but that is a migration. Ship the global carry, and leave a ponytail marker naming the per-space case as the upgrade trigger.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. Defaults are stored by engine name (SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:159, SpacesSettingsView.swift:66) and resolved by name with a silent Google fallback (SearchEngineService.swift:253-269). saveEdit() (line 430-460) writes the renamed engine through updateCustomSearchEngine on both branches and never carries the stored default, while onDelete at line 145-150 does clear it. Downgraded from high: it only bites a custom engine that was set as default and then renamed, not normal browsing.

kept.title: The appearance selector does not restyle itself when the choice does not change the colour scheme
kept.evidence: `class AppearanceManager: ObservableObject { @AppStorage("ui.app.appearance") var appearance: AppAppearance = .system { didSet { updateAppearance() } } }`. `@AppStorage` only drives redraws through `DynamicProperty` inside a `View`; in an `ObservableObject` it never sends `objectWillChange`. `LookAndFeelSettingsView` (line 7, 12) and `OnboardingSteps` bind `$appearanceManager.appearance` into `AppearanceSelector`, whose highlight is `let isSelected = selection == opt.appearance` (AppearanceSelector.swift:33-44). The only thing that redraws the card today is the environment `colorScheme` flipping.
kept.user_impact: On a Mac already in light mode, picking Light while Auto is selected (or the reverse) leaves the highlight and the semibold label on the old card, so the setting looks like it did nothing.
kept.fix: Smaller than the rewrite proposed: keep @AppStorage and add the missing notification, `@AppStorage("ui.app.appearance") var appearance: AppAppearance = .system { willSet { objectWillChange.send() } didSet { updateAppearance() } }`. Same key, no init, no UserDefaults plumbing to get wrong.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. AppearanceManager (AppearanceManager.swift:15-21) is an ObservableObject whose only stored property is @AppStorage, which sends no objectWillChange, and nothing else in the app reads that key (only OraRoot.swift:440 writes it). LookAndFeelSettingsView:12 and OnboardingSteps:285 bind it into AppearanceSelector, whose highlight is a pure function of the binding, so the card only redraws when the effective colorScheme flips.

kept.title: aura://settings/extensions persists a selection that leaves the sidebar with no row highlighted
kept.evidence: `.onChange(of: initialTab, initial: true) { … selectionRawValue = newValue.rawValue }` writes whatever the URL named into the persisted key. `BrowserWebContentView.swift:117` builds the page as `SettingsContentView(initialTab: tab.url.oraSettingsSection)`, and `URL.oraSettingsSection` (URL+Ora.swift:66-71) happily resolves `extensions`. The notification path reroutes that section to the store (OraRoot.swift:557-563), but a typed address does not. `dividedGroups` (line 275-289) has no `.extensions` entry, so `List(selection:)` matches nothing, and `detailView`'s `.extensions` branch is reached with the comment "Only reachable from a selection an older build saved".
kept.user_impact: Typing aura://settings/extensions once leaves Settings opening on a bare stub page with nothing selected in the sidebar on every later visit, until another section is clicked.
kept.fix: Do not silently swallow the deep link. In the onChange, `guard newValue != .extensions else { ExtensionsSettingsView.openStore(); return }` so a typed aura://settings/extensions lands on aura://extensions like every other entry point (OraRoot.swift:561-568 does exactly this for the notification path), and nothing unshowable is persisted.
kept.verify_reason: The mechanism is confirmed: onChange at line 325-328 persists any initialTab including .extensions, dividedGroups (line 265-279) omits .extensions, so List(selection:) highlights nothing, and the selection survives in the "settings.selectedTab" default. Downgraded to low and the evidence corrected on one point: the detail pane is not a bare stub, ExtensionsSettingsView renders a real summary card with three buttons, so the only defect is the unhighlighted sidebar plus the sticky selection, reachable only by typing that URL by hand and undone by one click.

kept.title: Settings search finds no import, export, backup or camera and microphone setting
kept.evidence: `searchKeywords` is the whole index and `matches(query:)` only looks at it plus the title. `.browsing` holds `SettingsBackupCard` (BrowsingSettingsView.swift:45, "Settings file", Export/Import Settings) but lists no "settings file", "backup", "import" or "export". `.passwords` holds `PasswordExportCard` ("Export passwords") and lists none of those words. `.bookmarks` holds `BookmarkPortabilityCard` ("Import and export", "Import from Safari…") and lists neither. `.permissions` renders a "Camera and microphone" card (PermissionsSettingsView.swift:44) and its keywords are only javascript, pinned sites, site data and cookies.
kept.user_impact: Someone moving to a new Mac types "export" or "backup" and gets "No settings match that", although three sections have an export in them; "camera" and "microphone" find nothing either.
kept.fix: Extend the three lists in step with the cards, as the doc comment on `searchKeywords` already instructs: add "settings file", "backup", "import settings", "export settings" to `.browsing`; "export passwords", "csv" to `.passwords`; "import", "export", "safari", "html" to `.bookmarks`; "camera", "microphone", "site permissions" to `.permissions`. `SettingsSectionsTests.searchFindsASectionByWhatItHoldsNotJustItsTitle` is where an `#expect(hits("export").contains(.browsing))` row belongs.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed against the cards. matches(query:) (line 253-257) only searches title plus searchKeywords, and none of the four lists carries the words. SettingsBackupCard sits in BrowsingSettingsView.swift:45 with an Export/Import Settings pair (DataPortabilityViews.swift:341-372), PasswordExportCard is on Passwords (DataPortabilityViews.swift:237-254, "Export passwords", CSV), BookmarkPortabilityCard is on Bookmarks (line 114-144, "Import and export", "Import from Safari…"), and PermissionsSettingsView.swift:44 renders the "Camera and microphone" card. So "export", "backup", "import", "camera" and "microphone" all return "No settings match that".

kept.title: Rebinding a shortcut onto a chord another command already owns is accepted silently
kept.evidence: `handleKeyCapture` calls `shortcutManager.setCustomShortcut(for:event:)` with no check, and `CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.setCustomShortcut` (line 36-41) just stores the chord. The codebase already names the failure and owns the helper: `KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.pin` (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:49-51) says "two menu items sharing a key equivalent means AppKit picks one by menu order", and `ExtensionCommands.collidesWithBuiltIn` (ExtensionCommands.swift:92) is `KeyboardShortcuts.allShortcuts.contains { $0.currentChord == chord }`.
kept.user_impact: Binding a command to a chord another command holds leaves two menu items on one key; AppKit fires whichever comes first in the menu and the row in Settings shows the chord as though it took.
kept.fix: Same shape, but compute the chord once and reuse it for the store call so the event is not parsed twice: `guard let chord = KeyChord(fromEvent: event) else { return }`, then the clash lookup, then setCustomShortcut. Note the collision check must skip the row being edited, which the finding already says.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. handleKeyCapture (ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:86-93) stores whatever KeyChord builds, CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.setCustomShortcut (line 36-41) just writes it, and no caller checks. The helper the fix wants exists and is used the same way for extension commands: ExtensionCommands.collidesWithBuiltIn is KeyboardShortcuts.allShortcuts.contains { $0.currentChord == chord } (ExtensionCommands.swift:92-94).

kept.title: Stock AppKit push buttons and text fields sit next to the app's own OraButton and OraInput
kept.evidence: Within one scroll of Settings: `Button(showingAddForm ? "Cancel" : "Add Custom Engine")`, `Button("Save")`, `Button("Set as Default")`, `Button("Edit")`, `Button("Delete", role: .destructive)` are all stock; `DownloadsSettingsView.swift:20` `Button("Choose…")`; `ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:46-54` three stock buttons; `SpacesSettingsView.swift:201` `.buttonStyle(.bordered)`; `ContainersSettingsView.swift:47` `Button("New Container", systemImage: "plus")`. The same pages render `OraButton` for About's "Show the welcome tour again" (AboutSettingsView.swift:46) and for every button in `SettingsBackupCard` and `PasswordExportCard`. Text fields disagree three ways as well: the nav search field is hand-built (SettingsContentView.swift:366-395), the home page field is `.textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder)` (BrowsingSettingsView.swift:62), and the engine form uses the bare default with hand-rolled "Name:" labels and a red error `Text` (SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:42-60) although `OraInput` takes `label`, `hint` and `error`.
kept.user_impact: The Arc/Zen-style chrome breaks the moment a settings card is opened: grey system push buttons and three different field looks on one page read as an unfinished preferences window.
kept.fix: Replace the stock `Button`s in these sections with `OraButton(label:variant:size:action:)` (`.secondary` for neutral, `.destructive` for Delete, `size: .sm` to match About and the portability cards), and the engine form's fields with `OraInput(text:placeholder:label:error:)`, which removes the "Name:"/"URL:" label column and the manual error `Text` at the same time.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading each cited line: stock Buttons at SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:28, 76, 251, 404, 408, 412; DownloadsSettingsView.swift:20 and 22; ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:46-54; SpacesSettingsView.swift:201 (.buttonStyle(.bordered)); ContainersSettingsView.swift:47; LanguagesSettingsView.swift:44. Against them OraButton appears in Settings only at AboutSettingsView.swift:46 and in the three portability cards. The three field looks are real too: hand-built nav field (SettingsContentView.swift:356-385), .roundedBorder at BrowsingSettingsView.swift:62, bare TextFields with a "Name:" label column at SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:42-60. OraButton(label:variant:size:...) and OraInput(text:placeholder:label:hint:error:) both take the arguments the fix uses.

kept.title: The password manager picker has exactly one option and three dead branches behind it
kept.evidence: `PasswordManagerProviderRegistry.providers` holds one live descriptor and two commented-out ones (PasswordManagerProviderRegistry.swift:42-66), so the `Picker("", selection: $settings.passwordManagerProvider)` can only ever show "Aura Passwords". Everything keyed off it is unreachable: `if !selectedProvider.isAvailable { Text("\(title) is not yet integrated.") }` (line 71-75), the `else` half of `vaultCard` with "integration coming soon" (line 92-97), the `usesBuiltInVault` and `usesBuiltInOverlay` guards on four toggles, and the `theme.warning` branch on the summary. The registry also still carries the fork's names: `case ora` and `let vaultStoredInOra: Bool`.
kept.user_impact: A menu that cannot be changed, and a promise of 1Password and Bitwarden support that does not exist, on the page that handles the user's credentials.
kept.fix: Drop SettingsStore.passwordManagerProvider from files_to_touch unless the enum is being removed with it: leaving the stored key alone costs nothing and avoids a migration on a page that holds credentials. Deleting the picker, the commented-out descriptors and the dead branches in the two view files is the whole win.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. PasswordManagerProviderRegistry.swift:42-67 has one live descriptor and two commented-out ones, so the Picker at PasswordsSettingsView.swift:34-39 has a single row. Every branch keyed off the descriptor is unreachable: isAvailable at line 44 and 70-74, the else half of vaultCard at line 90-97, and the usesBuiltInVault/usesBuiltInOverlay disables at 53-64. The fork names are still there: `case ora` and `vaultStoredInOra`.

kept.title: The Privacy page stats the filesystem four times per redraw, and the comment claims it does it once
kept.evidence: `private var blockingPlan: BundledExtensions.BlockingPlan { BundledExtensions.plan(for: BundledExtensions.blockingInputs()) }` is a computed property with a doc comment reading "asked once per body". One render of `blockingCard` reaches it four times: `blockerSummary` → `activeBlockerName`, the button title `"Open \(activeBlockerName) dashboard"`, `.disabled(uBlockDashboardURL == nil)`, and `waitingMessage`. `BundledExtensions.blockingInputs()` (BundledExtensions.swift:306-325) scans `manager.installedExtensions` and calls `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: folder.path)` on the main actor each time.
kept.user_impact: Four synchronous disk stats on the main thread every time anything on the Privacy page changes, which is every toggle and every keystroke that redraws it.
kept.fix: Same restructure, but the honest framing for the commit is the comment, not perf. If passing the plan through five members reads worse than the duplication, the smaller fix is to make the comment true by deleting the word "once".
kept.verify_reason: The redundancy and the false comment are real: blockingPlan (PrivacySettingsView.swift:110-112) is computed, and blockingCard reaches it through blockerSummary, the button title, uBlockDashboardURL and waitingMessage. Downgraded from medium: blockingInputs() (BundledExtensions.swift:306-325) short-circuits the fileExists once the extension row is present, and a single stat is microseconds, so calling it a main-thread stall overstates it. What is actually wrong is a doc comment that says "asked once per body" while the body asks four times.

kept.title: Deleting a custom search engine takes no confirmation
kept.evidence: `Button("Delete", role: .destructive) { onDelete() }` removes the engine on the first press through `settings.removeCustomSearchEngine(withId:)`; nothing is undoable and the name, URL and aliases the user typed are gone. Every other destructive action in Settings asks first through `dialogManager.confirm` (PrivacySettingsView.swift:276, PermissionsSettingsView.swift:180, ContainersSettingsView.swift:74).
kept.user_impact: One stray click on a row that also carries Edit and Set as Default deletes a hand-entered search engine with no way back.
kept.fix: Pass a `DialogManager` into the row (`@Environment(DialogManager.self) private var dialogManager`) and wrap the call the way `ContainersSettingsView.confirmDelete` does: title `"Delete \"\(engine.name)\"?"`, message naming that the shortcut stops working, `confirmLabel: "Delete"`, `variant: .destructive`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:412-414 calls onDelete() straight through to settings.removeCustomSearchEngine(withId:) (line 145-150), and the row carries Set as Default and Edit right next to it. ContainersSettingsView.confirmDelete (line 72-81) is the exact pattern to copy, and DialogManager is already in the settings environment (PrivacySettingsView.swift:15 resolves it in the same tab).

kept.title: Button labels switch between Title Case and sentence case inside the same card
kept.evidence: Title Case: "Clear Cache", "Clear Cookies", "Clear History" (SpacesSettingsView.swift:180-196), "Use Global Default" (line 60, 86), "Add Custom Engine", "Set as Default", "AI Chat Engine", "Search Engine Name" (SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:28, 44, 72, 252), "Reset to Default" (ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:136), "Set as Default" (BrowsingSettingsView.swift:19), "New Container" (ContainersSettingsView.swift:47), "Export Settings…"/"Import Settings…" (DataPortabilityViews.swift:353, 360). Sentence case in the same pages: "Clear browsing data…", "Install from file…", "Check for updates", "Show the welcome tour again", "Import HTML…", "Open Language & Region…". The copy is en-GB throughout ("Accent colour", "honour", "Licence and credits") except SettingsContentView.swift:89, "autofill behavior".
kept.user_impact: Two capitalisation conventions and two spelling conventions inside one window, which is the first thing a demanding user reads as unfinished.
kept.fix: Sentence case everywhere except proper nouns, matching the majority: "Clear cache", "Clear cookies", "Clear history", "Use global default", "Add custom engine", "Set as default", "AI chat engine", "Reset to default", "New container", "Export settings…", "Import settings…", and "autofill behaviour" in the passwords subtitle.
kept.verify_reason: Every cited string checks out: Title Case at SpacesSettingsView.swift:180/187/194, 60 and 86, SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:28/44/72/252, ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:136, BrowsingSettingsView.swift:19, ContainersSettingsView.swift:47, DataPortabilityViews.swift:353/360; sentence case in the same pages at PrivacySettingsView.swift:261, ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:51/54, AboutSettingsView.swift:46. The en-GB/en-US split is real: "Accent colour", "Licence and credits", "honour" against "autofill behavior" at SettingsContentView.swift:86. Cosmetic by the severity rubric, so low.

kept.title: The Spaces page ignores the settings layout: full-bleed cards, radio group cookies, no page gutter cap
kept.evidence: Every other section is `SettingsSection`, which caps content at `SettingsMetrics.contentMaxWidth` 960 and left-aligns it "because a toggle row stretched across a 1400pt window puts its control a screen away from its label" (SettingsSection.swift:11-13). Spaces rolls its own `ScrollView` with `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` and no cap, and has to re-read `@AppStorage("a11y.alwaysShowScrollBars")` by hand (line 17, 165). Its cookie picker is `.pickerStyle(.radioGroup)` (line 272) while the identical setting in Privacy is `.pickerStyle(.menu)` (PrivacySettingsView.swift:241).
kept.user_impact: Widen the window and the Spaces cards stretch to the full width while every other section stops at 960; the same cookie setting looks like two different controls depending on which page you reach it from.
kept.fix: Apply the same cap to the detail column, `.frame(maxWidth: SettingsMetrics.contentMaxWidth, alignment: .leading)` on the inner `VStack` before the outer `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)`, and switch the cookie picker to `.pickerStyle(.menu)` to match Privacy.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. SettingsSection caps its content at SettingsMetrics.contentMaxWidth 960 and says why (SettingsSection.swift:11-13, 34); SpacesSettingsView's own ScrollView ends at .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading) (line 161) with no cap and re-declares @AppStorage("a11y.alwaysShowScrollBars") by hand (line 17). The cookie picker really is .radioGroup at line 272 while the same setting is .pickerStyle(.menu) at PrivacySettingsView.swift:241.

kept.title: Comments describe a standalone Settings window and an explicit source list, neither of which exists
kept.evidence: `SettingsContentView` has exactly one call site, `BrowserWebContentView.swift:117`; there is no `Settings` scene or settings `Window` anywhere in the target. Yet: "Stands in for the window mode navigation title, which a tab cannot show" (line 439), "One set of numbers for every settings page, window and embedded tab alike" (SettingsSection.swift:3), "Settings can be a tab or its own window" (PrivacySettingsView.swift:153) guarding a `WindowFactory.openWindow` fallback that cannot be reached, "from the standalone settings window, the key window is not one" (ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:77-79), "shared with the standalone Passwords window" (PasswordsSettingsView.swift:79). Separately, LookAndFeelSettingsView.swift:33 justifies two structs in one file with "it shares that file because the app target lists its sources explicitly", but project.yml declares `sources: - path: aura`, a directory glob that picks up new files on its own.
kept.user_impact: The next person to touch this area works from a mental model of a window mode that was removed, and keeps dead fallbacks alive because a comment says they are needed.
kept.fix: Drop PasswordsSettingsView.swift from files_to_touch, its comment is true. Keep the `guard host != nil else { WindowFactory.openWindow(with: url) }` fallback in openUBlockDashboard: focusedAdapter() returns nil whenever no browser window is registered and on macOS below 15.4 (ExtensionWindowAdapter.swift:75-84, the call is under #available), and deleting it turns the button into a silent no-op in that case. Fix the comment above it instead.
kept.verify_reason: Mostly confirmed, with two corrections. There is no Settings scene or window: SettingsContentView has one call site (BrowserWebContentView.swift:117), so the comments at SettingsContentView.swift:439, SettingsSection.swift:3, PrivacySettingsView.swift:153 and ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:77-79 are stale, and project.yml:27-30 is a directory glob, so the LookAndFeelSettingsView.swift:33 sources sentence is wrong too. But PasswordsSettingsView.swift:79 is accurate: openPasswordsWindow and PasswordsWindowController exist (PasswordsWindow.swift:6-12) and are called from three places, so that comment is not a leftover.

kept.title: Custom engine URL validation passes an address with no scheme
kept.evidence: `isValidURL` is `newEngineURL.contains("{query}") && URL(string: newEngineURL.replacingOccurrences(of: "{query}", with: "test")) != nil`, and `URL(string:)` accepts relative strings, so "google.com/search?q={query}" or "exmaple/{query}" both validate and the Save button enables. `CustomSearchEngineRow.isValidEditURL` (line 273) repeats the same two lines. The error text under the field promises more than the check does: "URL must contain {query} and be a valid URL".
kept.user_impact: A search engine saved without https:// looks accepted and then does nothing when it is used from the launcher.
kept.fix: Require a web scheme in the shared check and hoist it out of the two views: `static func isValidTemplate(_ template: String) -> Bool { guard template.contains("{query}"), let url = URL(string: template.replacingOccurrences(of: "{query}", with: "test")), let scheme = url.scheme?.lowercased() else { return false }; return ["http", "https"].contains(scheme) }`, and have both `isValidURL` and `isValidEditURL` call it.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. isValidURL (line 15-19) and the duplicated isValidEditURL (line 272-275) both test only for {query} plus URL(string:) != nil, which accepts scheme-less relative strings, and the error copy under the field claims a validity check it does not perform.

kept.title: Switching sections leaves the settings tab's address pointing at the old one
kept.evidence: The selection binding writes only `selectionRawValue`; nothing writes back to `tab.url`. `TabManager.openSettingsTab` sets `existing.url = URL.oraSettings(section:)` on the way in (TabManager.swift:494-496), so a tab opened at aura://settings/downloads keeps showing that address after the user clicks through to Privacy. `everySectionHasAWorkingDeepLink` in SettingsSectionsTests proves the URL round-trips, so the address bar is the only half that is missing.
kept.user_impact: The address bar lies about which settings page is open, so copying the URL or reloading the tab lands somewhere else than the screen shows.
kept.fix: Passing the whole Tab into SettingsContentView widens its inputs for one line of work. Pass a closure instead, `SettingsContentView(initialTab:onSectionChange:)` called from BrowserWebContentView.swift:117 as `{ section in tab.url = .oraSettings(section: section); tab.urlString = tab.url.absoluteString }`, so the settings page still knows nothing about tabs. Guard against re-entering the initialTab onChange by only firing on a user selection, which is where the binding setter already sits.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed that nothing writes back: the selection binding (SettingsContentView.swift:294-299) sets only selectionRawValue, and TabManager.openSettingsTab (TabManager.swift:493-499) is the only thing that sets tab.url/urlString for a settings tab. So the address stays on whatever section opened the tab.

kept.title: Rebinding a keyboard shortcut does not reach the menus until the app is relaunched
kept.evidence: Every menu item takes its key equivalent from KeyboardShortcutDefinition.keyboardShortcut, which reads CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.shared through currentChord (Keyboard.swift:105-118). OraCommands declares no @StateObject/@ObservedObject for that manager; its only dynamic properties are six @AppStorage keys ('AppAppearance', 'ui.sidebar.hidden', 'ui.sidebar.position', 'ui.toolbar.hidden', 'ui.toolbar.showfullurl', 'ui.compact.enabled', 'ui.bookmarksBar.visible'). A rebind writes customShortcuts on the manager and 'settings.customKeyboardShortcuts' in defaults (CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.swift:36-41, SettingsStore.swift:205), none of which any of those wrappers observe, so the Commands body is not invalidated. Nothing else rebuilds the menu either: there is no NSMenu or mainMenu construction anywhere in the target.
kept.user_impact: The user rebinds a command in Settings, the chip in the row shows the new chord, and the old chord keeps firing while the new one does nothing, for the rest of the session.
kept.fix: Have the commands observe the store that owns the bindings: `@StateObject private var shortcuts = CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.shared` in OraCommands, with a comment that the property exists so a rebind invalidates the menu, since every keyEquivalent below reads through currentChord. The @Published customShortcuts then drives the rebuild.

kept.title: The View menu's Appearance picker reads a defaults key nothing else writes
kept.evidence: OraCommands.swift:4 is `@AppStorage("AppAppearance") private var appearanceRaw`, and the picker at line 90-99 shows that value while its setter writes the key and posts .setAppearance. The handler (OraRoot.swift:436-441) then sets AppearanceManager.shared.appearance, which persists under 'ui.app.appearance' (AppearanceManager.swift:17). grep over the whole target finds "AppAppearance" as a defaults key only at OraCommands.swift:4, so the Settings section and the onboarding step write one key and the menu reads another.
kept.user_impact: Pick Dark in Settings and the View menu still shows the tick next to System; pick Dark from the menu, relaunch, and the menu's tick and the actual appearance can disagree, because only the menu's own copy was updated in one direction.
kept.fix: Delete the appearanceRaw wrapper and drive the picker from the single owner: `@StateObject private var appearanceManager = AppearanceManager.shared`, selection `$appearanceManager.appearance`, keeping the .setAppearance post inside an onChange or the binding setter for the windows that listen. Depends on settings-4, the manager has to publish for the menu to redraw.

slop-sweep.summary: The prose in this repo is unusually good for a Swift codebase, and there is no TODO/FIXME debt, one stray print(), and almost no dead types, so the sweep turned up fewer cheap hits than expected. What it did turn up is worse than cosmetic: a File menu with two import buttons that do nothing, six shortcuts that appear rebindable in Settings but that nothing in the app reads, a one-option Picker in Passwords sitting on top of fifteen lines of commented-out code, and a stock NSAlert "About" box that calls the product "Aura Browser" and dates it 2025. Underneath that sits the unfinished Ora rename: the whole App layer, the design-system components and every script injected into every page the user visits still carry ora identifiers, and the shipped docs (HANDOFF-MACOS.md, PERFORMANCE.md, AUDIT.md) are lab notebooks that name the owner's Mac, an Apple team ID and files that no longer exist.

kept.title: File > Import Data offers Safari and Chrome buttons that do nothing
kept.evidence: `Menu("Import Data")` mounts three buttons; two have commented-out bodies: `Button("Safari") { // importSafari() }` (98-100) and `Button("Chrome") { // importChrome() }` (101-103). `ImportDataButton()` is mounted in the real File menu at aura/App/OraCommands.swift:44. Working bookmark import lives elsewhere entirely, in `BookmarkImportAction.run` (aura/Features/Importer/Views/DataPortabilityViews.swift:169) reached from Settings > Bookmarks and from onboarding.
kept.user_impact: A user picks File > Import Data > Chrome, the menu dismisses, and nothing happens at all. No toast, no panel, no error. Chrome and Safari are the two browsers people are most likely to be arriving from.
kept.fix: Do not call BookmarkImportAction from the menu. Menu items in this file already work by posting to the key window, so follow that: replace the whole ImportDataButton mount at OraCommands.swift:44 with `Button("Import Data…") { NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .openSettingsTab, object: nil, userInfo: ["tab": SettingsTab.bookmarks.rawValue]) }`, the same shape as "Show All Bookmarks" at OraCommands.swift:290-296, and delete ImportDataButton.swift. If the Arc import is worth keeping, it has to move to a view that lives inside a window (a row on BookmarkPortabilityCard in DataPortabilityViews.swift) or be driven by a new notification handled in OraRoot where the managers exist; leaving it in Commands cannot work. files_to_touch becomes aura/App/OraCommands.swift, aura/Features/Importer/Views/ImportDataButton.swift (delete) and, if Arc is kept, aura/Features/Importer/Views/DataPortabilityViews.swift plus project.yml regeneration.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: ImportDataButton.swift:97-103 mounts Safari and Chrome buttons with commented-out bodies, and it is mounted only at OraCommands.swift:44. But the auditor understated it and its fix will not work. OraApp.swift injects every manager inside OraRoot (OraRoot.swift:171-187); nothing is injected into the .commands scene (OraApp.swift:174 has no .environment). So @Environment(TabManager.self) etc. are nil in the menu and importArc() returns at its own guard: all three items are dead, Arc included. BookmarkImportAction.run needs a BookmarkStore and a DialogManager, which are equally absent from the menu environment, so calling it from there would be dead too.

kept.title: Six shortcuts are listed in Settings but nothing in the app reads them
kept.evidence: `allShortcuts` (374-410) feeds `itemsByCategory` (416), the only source for `ShortcutsSettingsView` (aura/Features/Settings/Sections/ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:11). Grepping `KeyboardShortcuts.Window.close`, `.Window.fullscreen`, `.App.quit`, `.App.hide`, `.Tabs.moveRight`, `.Tabs.moveLeft` across aura/ and auraTests/ returns zero call sites outside the declarations. Meanwhile OraCommands hardcodes the chords those definitions describe: `.keyboardShortcut("w", modifiers: .command)` at line 57 for Close Window and `.keyboardShortcut(",", modifiers: .command)` at line 337 for Settings, ignoring `App.preferences` which is in the list.
kept.user_impact: Settings > Shortcuts shows Close Window, Fullscreen, Quit, Hide, Move Tab Right and Move Tab Left as rebindable rows. Rebinding any of them changes the displayed chord and does nothing else; the old key still works and the new one does nothing. Same for Preferences.
kept.fix: Same shape, one correction: App.preferences must stay in allShortcuts (three call sites read it); only swap the literal `,` at OraCommands.swift:337 for KeyboardShortcuts.App.preferences.keyboardShortcut. For Window.close, either delete the definition and keep the hardcoded ⌘W, or point OraCommands.swift:57 at it and accept the ⇧⌘W default, but do not ship both. Adding the six retired ids to CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.retiredShortcutIDs also needs the KeyboardPolishTests.swift:132 expectation extended.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by grep: Window.close, Window.fullscreen, App.quit, App.hide, Tabs.moveRight and Tabs.moveLeft have no reference anywhere outside their declaration and allShortcuts (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:374-410), and allShortcuts is the only feed for ShortcutsSettingsView. Worse than stated for Window.close: its defaultChord is ⇧⌘W (line 180-185) while OraCommands.swift:57 hardcodes ⌘W, so Settings shows the wrong chord even before anyone rebinds. Downgraded from high: the rows only mislead a user who visits Settings > Shortcuts and rebinds; nothing breaks or loses data. App.preferences is NOT dead (AppCommand.swift:111, URLBarMenuButton.swift:150, TopToolbar.swift:183 all read it), it is only the menu item at OraCommands.swift:337 that hardcodes its chord, so the rebind changes three displayed chords and not the menu's.

kept.title: Five menu commands hardcode their chords and bypass rebinding entirely
kept.evidence: `Save Page As…` uses `.keyboardShortcut("s", modifiers: [.command, .shift])` (176), `Reader` uses `"r", [.command, .option]` (188), `View Source` uses `"u", [.command, .option]` (194), `Clear Cookies & Reload` uses `"r", [.command, .option, .shift]` (222). None has a `KeyboardShortcutDefinition`. Separately `Window.toggleCompactMode` has a definition (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:168) and is used at OraCommands.swift:125 but is absent from `allShortcuts`, so it never reaches Settings. README.md:74 claims "Every shortcut is rebindable in Settings" and README.md:76 advertises ⌥⌘R and ⌥⌘U by name.
kept.user_impact: Reader mode, view source, save page, clear cookies and compact mode cannot be rebound, and compact mode does not even appear in the shortcuts list. Anyone whose muscle memory or keyboard layout collides with ⌥⌘R has no way out, and the README promises otherwise.
kept.fix: Fix stands. Note the comment at OraCommands.swift:174-175 explains why Save Page is not on ⌘S; keep that comment on the new definition rather than dropping it, and give the definitions a category string that already exists in itemsByCategory ("Navigation" for clearCookiesAndReload, a new "Page" category for the other three) so Settings does not grow a one-row section per command.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: hardcoded chords at OraCommands.swift:176 (⇧⌘S), 188 (⌥⌘R), 194 (⌥⌘U) and 222 (⌥⇧⌘R), none of which has a KeyboardShortcutDefinition. Window.toggleCompactMode is defined (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:168) and used at OraCommands.swift:125, AppCommand.swift:108 and OnboardingSteps.swift:446 yet is absent from allShortcuts, so Settings never lists it while onboarding teaches it. README.md:63 does claim "Every shortcut is rebindable in Settings" and README.md:65-66 names ⌥⌘R and ⌥⌘U.

kept.title: About Aura is a stock NSAlert naming the product wrong and dated 2025
kept.evidence: `showAboutWindow()` builds `NSAlert()` with `messageText = "Aura Browser"` and `informativeText` ending `© 2025 Aura Browser`, then `runModal()`. Everywhere else the product is "Aura" (Info.plist, README, `AboutSettingsView` line 30 `Text("Aura")`). A designed About surface already exists: `AboutSettingsView` (aura/Features/Settings/Sections/AboutSettingsView.swift) with the app icon, version, GitHub link, update button and third-party notices.
kept.user_impact: The App menu's About item throws a grey system modal with a hardcoded 2025 copyright and a product name used nowhere else, in a browser whose whole point is custom chrome. It also duplicates a nicer panel that is one click away in Settings.
kept.fix: Fix stands. getAppVersion() has no other caller, so it goes with showAboutWindow(); check the About section actually scrolls into view when opened by tab id, otherwise the user lands on a page whose update button is what they wanted anyway.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at OraCommands.swift:342-357: NSAlert with messageText "Aura Browser" and "© 2025 Aura Browser", run modally from the App menu, while AboutSettingsView.swift:30-33 already draws the icon, "Aura" and versionString, and SettingsTab.about exists (SettingsContentView.swift:18). The bookmarks item at OraCommands.swift:290-296 proves the notification route works from Commands.

kept.title: Passwords settings shows a menu Picker with exactly one option, over 15 lines of commented-out code
kept.evidence: `providers` holds one descriptor, `.ora` / "Aura Passwords"; lines 51-65 are the 1Password and Bitwarden descriptors commented out. The enum still declares `case onePassword` and `case bitwarden` (lines 5-6) that no descriptor matches, so `descriptor(for:)` falls through to `providers[0]`. `PasswordsSettingsView.swift:34-40` renders `Picker("", selection: $settings.passwordManagerProvider)` over that one-element array with `.pickerStyle(.menu)`.
kept.user_impact: Settings > Passwords shows a stock pop-up button labelled "Aura Passwords" whose menu contains only "Aura Passwords". Clicking it does nothing. It reads as an unfinished feature in the one settings page where users are most suspicious.
kept.fix: Do not delete the two enum cases without checking SettingsStore's decode path: passwordManagerProvider is persisted by rawValue, and a stored "onePassword" from an earlier build must still decode to something rather than trapping. Keep the enum as-is, delete only the commented block, and replace the Picker with `Text(selectedProvider.title)` in the trailing VStack. The vaultStoredInOra rename is fine but belongs in the Ora rename pass (slop-sweep-11), not here.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PasswordManagerProviderRegistry.swift:42-67 holds one descriptor with lines 51-66 commented out, the enum at lines 3-6 still declares onePassword and bitwarden with no descriptor, and PasswordsSettingsView.swift:34-40 renders a .menu Picker over that one-element array. Downgraded to low: it is one stock pop-up on one settings page, not something a user meets in a normal session.

kept.title: Three modal dialogs use 11/14 pt radii instead of the AuraRadius scale the other dialogs use
kept.evidence: `DialogView.swift:59-63` sets the inner card to `AuraRadius.row` (10) and the outer shell to `AuraRadius.pane` (13) with a 3pt inset and `lineWidth: 1`; `DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:64,72` matches. `NewContainerButton.swift:101,103,109`, `EditContainerModal.swift:32,34,40` and `BookmarkEditDialog.swift:110,117` use literal `11` and `14` with the same 3pt inset and `lineWidth: 0.5`. A fourth scale, `ContainerConstants.UI.cornerRadius = 10`, duplicates `AuraRadius.row` and is used by `ContainerForm.swift:32,45,63,64`.
