kept.user_impact: New Space, Edit Space and Edit Bookmark are 1pt rounder than every other dialog and their hairline is half as heavy. Open one next to a confirm dialog and the corners visibly disagree.
kept.fix: The radius is the smaller half of the mismatch and the auditor missed the bigger one: all three dialogs also hand-roll `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 20, y: 8)` (NewContainerButton.swift:108, EditContainerModal.swift:40, BookmarkEditDialog.swift:118) against AuraShadow's 0.12/6/2. Swap those three for `.auraFloatingShadow()` in the same edit, which is what Theme.swift:38-42 exists for.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: DialogView.swift:59-67 uses AuraRadius.row, AuraRadius.pane, lineWidth 1 and .auraFloatingShadow(); NewContainerButton.swift:100-108, EditContainerModal.swift:31-40 and BookmarkEditDialog.swift:110-118 all use literal 11/14 with lineWidth 0.5. ContainerConstants.swift:30 does duplicate AuraRadius.row at 10.

kept.title: The network error page mixes stock AppKit buttons with OraButton in the same stack
kept.evidence: `Button("Try Again").buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large)` (47-51) and `Button("Go Back").buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large)` (53-59) sit directly above `OraButton(label: "Continue Anyway", variant: .ghost, size: .sm, …)` (64-70). These are the only two `.borderedProminent`/`.bordered` uses in the whole app outside `SpacesSettingsView.swift:201`. The comments at 17, 23, 29, 36 and 45 ("// Error icon", "// Error title", "// Action buttons") restate the line under them.
kept.user_impact: Every failed page load, which is the moment the browser most needs to look intentional, shows two glossy system-blue AppKit buttons above one custom ghost button. It is the most stock-looking screen in the product.
kept.fix: The proposed call will not compile: OraButtonVariant has no `.primary` (OraButton.swift:3-9 declares default, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive) and OraButton's default size is .md, not large. Use `OraButton(label: "Try Again", size: .lg, action: onRetry)` and `OraButton(label: "Go Back", variant: .secondary, size: .lg, action: goBack)`. SpacesSettingsView.swift:201 applies .bordered to a whole VStack of clearButton rows, so converting it means rewriting clearButton itself as an OraButton with variant .destructive; that is a separate edit, not a same-line swap.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: StatusPageView.swift:47-59 are the app's only .borderedProminent/.bordered uses outside SpacesSettingsView.swift:201, and OraButton sits directly beneath them at lines 64-70. The view is live (BrowserWebContentView.swift:123). The narrating comments at 17, 23, 29, 36 and 45 are real.

kept.title: Every page Aura loads gets ora-branded script names and window globals
kept.evidence: User scripts are registered as `"ora-bridge"` (13), `"ora-navigation"` (19), `"ora-context-menu"` (27), `"ora-password-manager"` (37) and, in BrowserPrivacyService, `"ora-global-privacy-control"`. They define `window.__oraContextMenuInstalled` (63), `window.__oraBridge` (108, 136, 231) and `window.__oraMedia` (314, plus six call sites in MediaController.swift:147-183). password-manager.js writes `element.dataset.oraPasswordFieldId = \`ora-password-${random}\`` (38) and queries `[data-ora-password-field-id]` (376, 379), so the attribute lands in the live DOM of every login form. Newer code in the same repo already uses `__aura`: `__auraShim`, `__auraFrames`, `__auraClipboardInstalled`, `__auraManifest`.
kept.user_impact: Anyone who opens Inspect Element on a page, or any site that enumerates injected attributes, sees a browser called Ora. It is the most public leftover of the fork and it contradicts the `__aura*` prefix the rest of the injected code already uses.
kept.fix: Same rename, wider list. files_to_touch must add aura/Features/Browser/Views/BrowserView.swift (ora-sb-shield) and aura/Features/Passwords/Services/PasswordAutofillCoordinator.swift:88 (window.__oraPasswordManager), and the pass must cover BrowserPrivacyService.swift:95-98 and 135-136. Rename the Swift and JS sides in one commit: PasswordAutofillCoordinator and password-manager.js must agree on the global name or autofill silently stops working, and AuditRegressionTests.swift:150,183-205 is what catches it.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed and broader than reported. Beyond the five script names and the three globals, page-visible Ora leftovers include window.__oraPasswordManagerInstalled and window.__oraPasswordManager (password-manager.js:2,5,408; read back at PasswordAutofillCoordinator.swift:88), element.dataset.oraPasswordFieldId / [data-ora-password-field-id] (password-manager.js:34-40,376-380), the element id 'ora-sb-shield' injected into the live DOM (BrowserView.swift:21,42,45), window.__oraFingerprintingProtectionInstalled and the spoofed device ids 'ora-' + kind (BrowserPrivacyService.swift:95-98,135-136), and element._oraHighlightTimer / _oraOriginalBackground (password-manager.js:357-366). The fingerprinting deviceId strings are the sharpest one: the anti-fingerprinting code hands every site a device id that names the fork.

kept.title: HANDOFF-MACOS.md ships the owner's machine paths, an Apple team ID and instructions for deleted files
kept.evidence: Line 13 tells the reader to run xcodegen because "AuraPaintKeepAlive.swift is new"; no such file exists in the repo. Lines 85-90 give an A/B table over `AURA_FG_PRIORITY` and `AURA_PAINT_KEEPALIVE`, which line 133 then says "are deleted" (grep confirms neither exists in any Swift or Objective-C source). Line 26 documents `AuraSetAlwaysForegroundPriority`, which does not exist either. The header names branch `feature/extensions`. Run notes carry `Aniko's Mac` (line 116), `/tmp/aura-backup-115241` (line 130), `~/Library/Application Support/Aura-backups/2026-08-26-pre-extensions-run` (line 150) and the Apple team ID `8TZ464JNCL` (line 146). scripts/paint-probe.html:13,21 still probes the removed `__auraKeepAlive` marker.
kept.user_impact: A public repo document instructs contributors to build with environment variables that no longer exist and to look for a file that was never committed, and it publishes the maintainer's home directory layout and Apple developer team ID.
kept.fix: Fix stands, with one addition: line 12's xcodegen instruction and the Track 2 table are the only actively wrong parts, so cut those first. Do not delete the run notes wholesale without moving the still-useful paint-probe serving instructions (line 130) into scripts/ or UBLOCK-ORIGIN.md; they are the only record of how that fixture is driven.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: no AuraPaintKeepAlive.swift in the tree, and AURA_FG_PRIORITY, AURA_PAINT_KEEPALIVE, AuraSetAlwaysForegroundPriority and __auraKeepAlive appear in no Swift, Objective-C or project file; the only surviving hit is scripts/paint-probe.html:13,21. Team id 8TZ464JNCL and the personal paths are at HANDOFF-MACOS.md:122,128,130,144. Downgraded to low: the document itself says at line 133 that both levers are deleted, so a contributor reading it in order is contradicted rather than misled into a broken build, and a team id is a public identifier, not a secret.

kept.title: Ellipsis style is inconsistent across user-facing strings, three ways in one app
kept.evidence: Three spellings coexist: the literal character in OraCommands.swift ("Save Page As…" 176, "Add Bookmark…" 280, "Settings…" 336) and DataPortabilityViews.swift ("Import HTML…" 129, "Export…" 152); the escape `\u{2026}` in OraCommands.swift:31, HomePageView.swift:130 and OnboardingSteps.swift:211,214; and three ASCII periods in `placeholder: "Search files..."` (DownloadsHistoryView.swift:78), `"Search history..."` (HistoryPanelView.swift:105), `label: isAuthenticating ? "Unlocking..."` (PasswordVaultView.swift:199) and `"eg. work, streaming, finance..."` (ContainerForm.swift:90, which also spells "eg." instead of "e.g.").
kept.user_impact: Search fields and the password unlock button show three dots at a different width and baseline from every menu item's proper ellipsis. Side by side in the same window it looks unproofed.
kept.fix: Change only the four "..." strings to … and "eg." to "e.g."; leave the \u{2026} escapes alone unless the same commit converts them everywhere, since they are already correct on screen. files_to_touch shrinks to DownloadsHistoryView.swift, HistoryPanelView.swift, PasswordVaultView.swift and ContainerForm.swift.
kept.verify_reason: The three spellings exist as described, but only one of them is user-visible: \u{2026} and the literal … render identically, so the OraCommands/HomePageView/OnboardingSteps escapes are a source-style nit with no pixel consequence. The real defects are the four ASCII cases (DownloadsHistoryView.swift:78, HistoryPanelView.swift:105, PasswordVaultView.swift:199, ContainerForm.swift:90) plus "eg." for "e.g.". Downgraded to low accordingly.

kept.title: The App layer, design-system components and internal-URL helpers are still named Ora
kept.evidence: Ora-named files: OraApp.swift, OraRoot.swift, OraCommands.swift, OraBrowserScripts.swift, OraButton.swift, OraIcon.swift, OraInput.swift, URL+Ora.swift, auraTests/OraInternalURLTests.swift. Ora-named types and members by reference count: OraButton (41), OraInternal (30), OraInput (20), OraShape (17), OraRoot (16), OraIcons (16), OraContainer (8), plus `oraInternalURL` (Utils.swift:80), `URL.isOraInternal`, `URL.canonicalOraInternal`, `URL.oraHome`, `URL.oraSettings()`, `ToastIcon.ora` (ToastModel.swift:68), the modifiers `.oraShortcut`, `.oraShortcutHelp`, `OraWindowDragGesture`, and `BrowserPageConfiguration.oraUserAgent`. Assets: `OraColorLogo.imageset` (whose file is already named aura-color-logo.png), `ora-logo-plain.imageset`, and `appearance-system.imageset/Ora Browser System.png`.
kept.user_impact: No runtime symptom, but every contributor and every stack trace reads the wrong product name, and `Image("OraColorLogo")` at OraRoot.swift:544 is the app's own logo asset. It is the loudest remaining signal that this is an unfinished rename.
kept.fix: Do the injected-script rename (slop-sweep-8) first and on its own: it is the half with page-visible effect and its own test coverage. Then this rename as one mechanical commit with no behaviour change in it. Note project.yml globs on `path: aura`, so file moves need `xcodegen` but no project.yml edit; drop project.yml from files_to_touch and add aura/Assets/Catalogs/Assets.xcassets/appearance-system.imageset/Ora Browser System.png as a git mv.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: the nine Ora-named files exist, the types and members are as listed, and the app's own logo is Image("OraColorLogo") (OraRoot.swift:551, OnboardingSteps.swift:143). Downgraded to low: zero runtime effect, and the exclusions the auditor names (PasswordManagerProviderKind.ora, LegacyDataMigrator.legacyFolderName = "Ora", the GPL notice in AboutSettingsView.swift:102) are correctly identified as must-not-touch.

kept.title: Onboarding shames the user for declining ad blocking
kept.evidence: The two choices on the ad-blocking screen are `title: "Yes, block them"` (421) and `title: "No, I collect banner ads"` (426). The subtitles underneath are both straight and informative ("Pages exactly as served. Settings › Privacy turns blocking back on any time.").
kept.user_impact: A first-run screen makes a joke at the expense of anyone who picks the non-default, which is a pattern people recognise from consent dialogs they resent. It is also the only piece of snark in an otherwise plain, confident voice.
kept.fix: `title: "No, show pages as served"`, matching the subtitle already there.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at OnboardingSteps.swift:426: "No, I collect banner ads" next to the straight subtitle "Pages exactly as served." It is the only joke in the onboarding copy. Downgraded to low: it is a taste call on one first-run row, not a defect.

kept.title: Grammar error in the new-space explainer users see before creating their first space
kept.evidence: `Text("Spaces are an isolated profiles with their own history, passwords, configs, etc.")`. "an isolated profiles" is ungrammatical, and "configs, etc." is developer shorthand nowhere else in the product's copy. Compare the same concept written well in ContainersSettingsView: "Containers keep cookies and logins separate."
kept.user_impact: The sentence explaining Aura's headline feature, shown in the dialog that creates a space, does not parse.
kept.fix: The same explainer should also be checked in EditContainerModal, which shares ContainerForm but draws its own header; if it repeats the sentence, fix both in one edit.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed verbatim at NewContainerButton.swift:75: "Spaces are an isolated profiles with their own history, passwords, configs, etc." Ungrammatical copy in the dialog that creates the product's headline feature.

kept.title: Workstream numbers and paired begin/end MARK fences left over from a task plan
kept.evidence: `// MARK: - Open local files (workstream 7)` (29) closed by `// MARK: - End open local files` (40); `// MARK: - Page tools (workstream 6)` (169) closed by `// MARK: - End page tools` (196); `// MARK: Hard reload (workstream 8)` (204) closed by `// MARK: End hard reload` (217); `// MARK: Per-site zoom` (140) closed by `// MARK: End per-site zoom` (157). kept.verify_reason: Confirmed, with the OraRoot line numbers off by two: the comments are at OraRoot.swift:525 and 538, not 523 and 536. The four End MARKs (OraCommands.swift:40, 157, 196, 217) and three (workstream N) tags in OraCommands are exactly as described.

kept.title: One print() in shipped code, where CONTRIBUTING mandates AuraLog
kept.evidence: `print("Failed to compile privacy rule list \(identifier): \(error.localizedDescription)")` inside the `compileContentRuleList` completion. It is the only `print(` in aura/ and auraWebBundle/. CONTRIBUTING.md line 38 says "Use `AuraLog` for diagnostics", and `AuraLog` exists at aura/Core/Utilities/AuraLog.swift.
kept.user_impact: A content-blocker compile failure goes to stdout, which is invisible in a shipped app and absent from `log stream`, so the one signal that filtering silently stopped working is lost in Release.
kept.fix: There is no existing AuraLog logger in this file, so the fix is two lines: add `private static let log = AuraLog.category("Privacy")` next to the other statics and call `Self.log.error("content rule list \(identifier, privacy: .public) failed to compile: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: BrowserPrivacyService.swift:578 is the only print( in aura/ and auraWebBundle/, and CONTRIBUTING.md:37 mandates AuraLog. One correction to the evidence: the SwiftLint rule no_print_statements (.swiftlint.yml:76-80) is severity warning, not an error, which is why this line survives.

kept.title: Two view files with zero references
kept.evidence: `struct ShareLinkButton` (ShareLinkButton.swift:4) and `struct PlayerIconButtonStyle` (PlayerIconButtonStyle.swift:3) each match exactly once across aura/, auraTests/ and auraUITests/: their own declaration. A scan of all 647 declared types in aura/ found no other unreferenced ones. `ShareLinkButton` also drags in a private `ShareSourceView: NSViewRepresentable`.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime. Two files, ~70 lines, that a contributor has to read and decide about.
kept.fix: project.yml globs on `path: aura`, so deleting the two files plus `xcodegen` is the whole change; no project.yml edit.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: each type matches exactly once across aura, auraTests and auraUITests, its own declaration (47 and 30 lines respectively).

kept.title: Joke emoji as data-model defaults, one of them reachable from the Arc importer
kept.evidence: `emoji: String = "💩"` in the `TabContainer` initialiser (TabContainer.swift:37) and in the versioned schema copy (AuraSchema.swift:46). The real production default is `ContainerConstants.defaultEmoji = "•"`, passed by `TabManager.createContainer` (TabManager.swift:304), so 💩 is only reachable through a caller that omits the argument. `ImportDataButton.swift:22` is a live path with its own joke default: `emoji: space.emoji ?? "💀"`.
kept.user_impact: Import an Arc space that has no emoji and the sidebar shows a skull. The 💩 default is dormant but sits in a `@Model` initialiser and in the migration schema, one omitted argument away from being written to disk.
kept.fix: Change TabContainer.swift:37 to ContainerConstants.defaultEmoji and the Arc fallback with it. Leave AuraSchema.swift:46 alone or change it in a separate commit: it is a frozen versioned migration schema, and touching that file for cosmetics invites a migration diff nobody wanted.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: 💩 at TabContainer.swift:37 and AuraSchema.swift:46, 💀 at ImportDataButton.swift:22, with the only TabContainer( call site (TabManager.swift:308) always passing ContainerConstants.defaultEmoji. The stated user impact does not currently happen: the Arc importer is reachable only from the File menu, which has no environment, so importArc() returns before it can ever write a skull (see slop-sweep-1). It is real slop in a @Model initialiser, not a live bug.

kept.title: The paint probe's doc comment is a dated lab notebook, not an explanation
kept.evidence: Forty-two lines of `///` before `extension AuraWebBundle`, of which roughly half narrate the investigation rather than the code: "Measured on macOS 26 beta (build 26A5416b), 2026-08-22, through the gated test …: verdict `painted`, while the same run logged `Failed to acquire RBS assertion` …" (28-33) and "Told apart on macOS 27 (Xcode 27.0 beta 27A5218g), 2026-08-25: it is the second. Pages on the bundle pool went blank for the user while the snapshot probe kept saying `painted` …" (35-46). The same three passes are already written up in HANDOFF-MACOS.md and UBLOCK-ORIGIN.md.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime. A reader has to work out which of two superseded OS-beta findings still describes the code in front of them, and the dates rot with every OS release.
kept.fix: Keep more than proposed: the sentence explaining why the host window keeps a point on screen must survive, because it is the only thing standing between a future reader and "why are there two floating windows at launch". Cut only the 2026-08-22 verdict paragraph and the dated framing of the 2026-08-25 one.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: 42 lines of /// at AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:7-47, of which lines 25-46 are two dated OS-beta narratives. The middle paragraph does carry live design rationale (frames outrank the snapshot; the window keeps one point on screen or rAF never ticks), which the auditor's fix correctly preserves.

kept.title: ROADMAP and AUDIT contradict the shipped code and each other
kept.evidence: ROADMAP.md:28 lists under "Near term": "Full uBlock Origin reliability: automatic paint-health checks for the compatibility mode it requires". That check shipped: `AuraWebBundle.PaintProbe` (aura/Core/BrowserEngine/AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift) runs at launch and is covered by `FullUBlockOriginTests`, and HANDOFF-MACOS.md:133 records the root cause as fixed in `AuraWebBundleSupport.m`. ROADMAP.md:44 reads "_Last updated: August 2026_" while the repo is at v1.2.3 dated 7 September 2026. AUDIT.md:24 claims "316 application source files and 63 Swift test files"; the actual counts are 310 and 67.
kept.user_impact: The roadmap advertises as upcoming a feature that already ships and is two OS betas old, and the audit's own inventory numbers do not match the tree it describes.
kept.fix: Do not move the bullet. Trim it to its unshipped half, "Request-level blocking that does not need the compatibility mode", and let README's feature list carry the paint check. Then bump ROADMAP.md:44 to September 2026 and correct AUDIT.md:24 to 310 and 62.
kept.verify_reason: Half refuted, half worse. The ROADMAP bullet is compound: "automatic paint-health checks ... AND groundwork for request-level blocking that does not need that mode at all". Only the first clause shipped, so moving the bullet to "Available today" would be wrong. The AUDIT.md counts are wrong even against their own baseline: at commit 73f9b86 the tree holds 310 app Swift files and 62 test files, not 316 and 63. The date line at ROADMAP.md:44 says August 2026 against an AUDIT.md dated 7 September 2026.

kept.title: PERFORMANCE.md names the owner's personal machine as the target
kept.evidence: "The target machine is the user's M5 Pro MacBook on macOS 27; CI hardware and OS are recorded separately and cannot predict its launch time." The surrounding document is otherwise written for contributors, and README.md:114 links it as public project documentation.
kept.user_impact: A public performance document sets its acceptance target against one maintainer's laptop, which tells a contributor nothing actionable and reads as an internal note left in by accident.
kept.fix: Replace with the hardware class rather than the person: "CI hardware and OS are recorded per run and do not predict Apple Silicon laptop launch times; measure on the machine you are optimising for."
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed verbatim at PERFORMANCE.md:140, in a file README links as public documentation, and the surrounding table (lines 145-158) is written for anyone reading a CI run.

kept.title: Trailing space baked into a launcher row label
kept.evidence: `Text("Switch to tab ")` followed by an `Image(systemName: "arrow.right")` inside `HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 8)`. The HStack already supplies 8pt of spacing, so the trailing space adds a second, font-dependent gap on top of it.
kept.user_impact: The arrow chip on an open-tab row sits further from its label than the spacing value says, and the gap changes width with the system font.
kept.fix: Drop the trailing space: `Text("Switch to tab")`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:103: Text("Switch to tab ") inside an HStack(spacing: 8). The gap claim is softer than stated, since text layout often trims trailing whitespace at the end of a line, so the visible effect may be nil; the string is still wrong and the fix costs one character.

kept.title: Commented-out cursor block carried in vendored SplitView code
kept.evidence: Lines 89-101 are an upstream `.onHover` implementation commented out in full, including its `NSCursor.pop()` / `push()` body and an iOS caveat, immediately above the live `.cursor(...)` modifier that replaced it (102-104). Aura is macOS-only, so the iOS branch it discusses cannot apply.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime. Thirteen lines of dead upstream code in a file the repo has already localised (`Vendor/SplitView/LICENSE` is retained separately in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
kept.fix: Delete lines 89-101 including the "Perhaps should consider some kind of custom hoverEffect" lead-in at 89-90, which is upstream musing about iOS and equally dead in a macOS-only app.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at Splitter.swift:89-101, a fully commented .onHover including its iOS caveat, directly above the live .cursor modifier at 102-104. The vendored-code objection does not hold: this directory has already been reformatted by the repo's SwiftFormat gate (ba6a603) and renamed (2c7403c), so divergence from upstream is accepted policy here.

kept.title: Every item in File > Import Data is dead, Arc included, because Commands get no environment
kept.evidence: importArc() opens with `guard let tabManager, let historyManager, let downloadManager else { return }` (line 12). Those come from @Environment(TabManager.self) etc. (lines 4-8). The managers are injected inside the window content only, at OraRoot.swift:171-187; OraApp.swift:174 attaches `.commands { OraCommands() }` with no `.environment` on the scene, and OraApp.swift has no environment modifier at all. ImportDataButton's single mount is OraCommands.swift:44, inside those commands. So all three optionals are nil at click time and the guard returns. The file's own comment at lines 5-6 notices the menu "sits outside any window's environment" and then relies on that environment anyway.
kept.user_impact: File > Import Data > Arc dismisses the menu and does nothing, exactly like the two commented-out siblings. Every route into the Arc importer is dead, so the feature README and onboarding imply is unreachable.
kept.fix: Menu items in OraCommands work by posting to NSApp.keyWindow. Either drop the Arc row and point the File menu at Settings > Bookmarks with the same notification "Show All Bookmarks" uses (OraCommands.swift:290-296), or post a new `.importArcData` notification and handle it in OraRoot alongside the other window-scoped handlers, where tabManager, historyManager and downloadManager are real.

kept.title: Import-settings confirmation dialog copy does not parse
kept.evidence: `message: "Settings the file names are overwritten. Everything it does not " + "name stays as it is."` in SettingsBackupCard.confirmImport(), shown by dialogManager.confirm with title "Import settings?" and confirm label "Choose File…".
kept.user_impact: The one sentence telling a user what an import will overwrite reads as a fragment. It is the last thing shown before settings are replaced.
kept.fix: `message: "Settings named in the file are overwritten. Everything it does not name stays as it is."`

kept.title: Download toasts read as run-on sentences and toast punctuation is inconsistent
kept.evidence: `"Download failed \(download.fileName)"` (line 174) and `"Download cancelled \(fileName)"` (line 198) render as "Download failed report.pdf". The success case at line 161 reads correctly ("Downloaded report.pdf"). Across the app, toasts also split on trailing periods: "Settings exported." and "Exported 12 bookmarks." (DataPortabilityViews.swift:385,205) against "Cookies cleared", "Cache cleared", "Browsing data cleared" and "Pinned URL set to the current page" (SpacesSettingsView.swift:183,191,198, PrivacySettingsView.swift:292, TabManager.swift:724).
kept.user_impact: A failed download shows a sentence with a word missing, and consecutive toasts in one session disagree about whether they end in a full stop.
kept.fix: `"Download failed: \(download.fileName)"` and `"Download cancelled: \(fileName)"`, then pick one punctuation rule for toasts (no trailing period, matching the majority) and drop the periods from the four DataPortabilityViews success toasts.

kept.title: User-facing copy mixes British and American spelling and two menu-path separators
kept.evidence: Onboarding says "Favourites sit at the very top of the sidebar" (line 365) and "favourites on top" (line 452), while the sidebar itself says "Drop here to add to favorites" (EmptyFavTabItem.swift:20), "Remove from Favorites" (FavTabItem.swift:110, TabItem.swift:216) and "Add Selected Tab to Favorites" (SidebarView.swift:116-117). Settings pairs "Accent colour" (LookAndFeelSettingsView.swift:23) with "autofill behavior" (SettingsContentView.swift:89). Menu paths are written "Settings › Privacy" almost everywhere (OnboardingSteps.swift:427, SearchEngineSettingsView.swift:133) but "Settings > Privacy > Extension request blocking" at ExtensionCompatibility.swift:60.
kept.user_impact: Onboarding teaches a word the sidebar then spells differently, and one settings description uses American spelling next to a British header on the adjacent page.
kept.fix: Pick one locale, British to match the majority of the shipped copy, and align: favourites/Favourites in the four sidebar strings, "behaviour" in SettingsContentView.swift:89, and "›" in ExtensionCompatibility.swift:60. SettingsContentView.searchKeywords already lists both spellings, so search keeps working either way.

kept.title: AuraLog's doc comment claims a lint gate that is only a warning
kept.evidence: "Use this instead of `print`: the unified log keeps release builds observable and SwiftLint's `no_print_statements` rule fails the build on the alternative." The rule at .swiftlint.yml:76-80 is `severity: warning`. BrowserPrivacyService.swift:578 is the standing proof, a print( that ships.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime. A contributor trusts a gate that does not exist, which is how the one print in the tree got there.
kept.fix: Either make the claim true by setting `severity: error` on no_print_statements in .swiftlint.yml (after fixing line 578), or reword the comment to "SwiftLint warns on the alternative". The first is the smaller diff and the one the comment already promises.

panels.summary: The sidebar panels (history, downloads, files) are the most finished part of this area: consistent 38pt headers, real empty and no-results states, date grouping shared between two panels, hover styling that never reflows a row. The seams show at the edges. The history panel's Clear button deletes a whole space's history with no confirmation while every other destructive path in the app asks first, File > Import Data ships two menu items that do nothing and a third that always fails silently against the sandbox, and the password vault plus the extension store are the two surfaces still wearing stock AppKit widgets. Underneath that, none of the list rows are buttons, so history, downloads and bookmarks are unreachable by keyboard or VoiceOver, and the three panels carry three copies of the same header and footer that have already started to drift.

kept.title: History panel "Clear" wipes the range with no confirmation, and ignores the active search
kept.evidence: The header button calls `clearRange` directly: `Button(action: clearRange)` (line 78), and `clearRange()` (line 283) is `historyManager.delete(range: range, in: containerId)` followed by `reload()`. `HistoryManager.delete(range:in:)` fetches every row in the range and deletes it with no undo. Every other destructive action in the app goes through `dialogManager.confirm` first: `PrivacySettingsView.swift:276` for clearing browsing data, `ContainersSettingsView.swift:73` for deleting a container, `BookmarksBar.swift:246` for deleting a folder. The button is also shown whenever `!items.isEmpty`, i.e. while a search is active, and its tooltip then still reads "Clear all history in this space" while the visible list is the search result: the delete ignores `searchText` entirely and removes rows the user cannot see.
kept.user_impact: One stray click on a 60pt button in the panel header permanently deletes a whole space's browsing history. With a search typed in, the list shows three rows and clicking Clear deletes thousands.
kept.fix: Fix stands. Two notes: DialogManager.confirm's signature is (title:message:icon:iconImage:confirmLabel:variant:onConfirm:onCancel:isQuitConfirmation:), so pass onConfirm as a labelled argument or trailing closure exactly as BookmarksBar.confirmDelete does. Rather than hiding the Clear button during a search (which removes the only way to clear from a searched panel), keep it and make it honest: when !searchText.isEmpty, title it 'Clear all history in this space?' with message 'Your search will be cleared too.' — or simply gate the button on searchText.isEmpty; either is acceptable, but the confirm is the load-bearing half.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at HistoryPanelView.swift:78 (Button(action: clearRange)) and :283-287 (delete(range:in:) then reload). HistoryManager.delete(range:in:) (HistoryManager.swift:226-240) fetches and deletes every row with no undo, and clearRange never looks at searchText, while the tooltip on :92 still says 'Clear all history in this space'. Every other destructive path in the app confirms first (BookmarksBar.swift:247, ContainersSettingsView.swift:74, PrivacySettingsView.swift:276). DialogManager is injected into the browser window (OraRoot.swift:186-188), so the panel can reach it.

kept.title: File > Import Data: Safari and Chrome do nothing, Arc reads a path the sandbox cannot see
kept.evidence: `Menu("Import Data")` (line 94) is mounted live in the File menu (`aura/App/OraCommands.swift:44`). `Button("Safari") { // importSafari() }` (98-100) and `Button("Chrome") { // importChrome() }` (101-103) have commented-out bodies, so they are enabled menu items that do nothing at all. The Arc item calls `importArc()`, which calls `getRoot()` (`Importer.swift:150`), reading `NSString(string: "~/Library/Application Support/Arc/StorableSidebar.json").expandingTildeInPath`. `aura/Info/aura.entitlements` sets `com.apple.security.app-sandbox` with only `files.user-selected.read-write` and `files.downloads.read-write`, so the tilde expands to the app's container and the read always fails; the only reaction is `logger.error` (Importer.swift:158). `DataPortabilityPanels` in the same feature documents this exact trap and provides `realHomeDirectory` plus an `NSOpenPanel` path for it.
kept.user_impact: Three menu items under File > Import Data. Two are inert on click, the third fails silently every time with no message, no toast and no panel. A user importing from another browser concludes the browser is broken.
kept.fix: Fix stands. Add that the Arc item is dead for the environment reason as well, so no amount of sandbox work would revive it in place. If Importer.swift is deleted, delete its Arc JSON model types with it (Root/TopAppsObject/CleanSpace/CleanTab and inspectItems are only used by importArc); confirm with `grep -rn 'inspectItems\|getRoot(' aura` before removing.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. ImportDataButton.swift:98-103 has two empty Button bodies with commented-out calls, mounted live at OraCommands.swift:44. Stronger than the auditor states: OraApp.swift:174 attaches the commands with `.commands { OraCommands() }` and injects no environment, so the optional @Environment values in ImportDataButton (lines 4-8) are all nil and importArc() returns at its first guard — the Arc item is inert too, before the sandbox ever matters. The sandbox point also holds (aura.entitlements has app-sandbox with only user-selected and downloads access; Importer.swift:150-152 reads an expanded tilde path and only logger.error's on failure). grep shows ImportDataButton is referenced from OraCommands.swift only.

kept.title: Password vault is the only surface still using stock AppKit widgets and a system alert
kept.evidence: `TextField("Search saved passwords", text: $searchText).textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder)` (77-78) where History (`HistoryPanelView.swift:100`), Downloads (`DownloadsHistoryView.swift:75`) and the bookmark manager (`BookmarksSettingsView.swift:82`) all use `OraInput(... leadingIcon: "magnifyingglass")`. `Button("Lock", action: lockVault)` (147) is a stock bezel button next to an `OraButton` on the lock screen (line 205) in the same view. `Picker(...).pickerStyle(.menu)` (line 158-164) is the only stock popup in the panels. Line 108 is the only `.alert(` in the whole app (`grep -rn '\.alert(' aura` returns one hit) while every other destructive confirmation uses `dialogManager.confirm`.
kept.user_impact: The Passwords window looks like a different app: a grey rounded search box, a system popup button and a macOS alert sheet sitting inside Aura's flat chrome.
kept.fix: Keep the styling swaps (OraInput, OraButton, and the AuraMenuAnchorView/presentAuraMenu pattern for the space picker). Do NOT replace the .alert with dialogManager.confirm as written: PasswordsWindowView (PasswordsWindow.swift:86-103) is a separate window that neither injects DialogManager nor applies .dialogs(manager:) — only OraRoot.swift:186-188 does — so a non-optional @Environment(DialogManager.self) traps there and even an optional one would present into a window with no dialog host. Either leave the .alert as the one system confirmation, or first inject dialogManager and .dialogs(manager:) into PasswordsWindowView, which is a bigger change than this finding warrants.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PasswordVaultView.swift:77-78 .roundedBorder TextField, :147 stock Button("Lock"), :158-164 .pickerStyle(.menu), :108 the only .alert( in the app (grep confirms one hit). Every sibling panel uses OraInput/OraButton. The proposed dialogManager replacement, however, is unsafe.

kept.title: Panel rows are tap gestures, not buttons: no VoiceOver label, no keyboard activation
kept.evidence: Every list row in the panels opens through `.contentShape(Rectangle())` + `.onTapGesture(perform: onOpen)` on a bare `HStack`: `HistoryPanelRow.swift:56-57`, `DownloadHistoryRow.swift:92` (`.onTapGesture(perform: activate)`), `BookmarksSettingsView.swift:207` (`.onTapGesture(perform: onOpen)`). `grep -rn accessibility` across History, Downloads, Bookmarks, Extensions, Passwords, Containers and Importer returns four hits in total, all in Files and the bookmarks bar. A tap gesture publishes no `.isButton` trait and no accessibility action, so VoiceOver reads the row as an unlabelled group and cannot open it, and the row is not in the tab order.
kept.user_impact: History, downloads and bookmarks are unreachable with the keyboard or VoiceOver: the rows announce as loose text and pressing Return does nothing.
kept.fix: Fix stands, with one correction: .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) on a row that contains buttons collapses those buttons away, so add the row's own .accessibilityLabel (as OpenedFileRow.swift:72 does) plus .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton) and .accessibilityAction(named:) for the hover actions, rather than .combine. Pair the existing .opacity(isHovered ? 1 : 0) with .accessibilityHidden(!isHovered) on the hover buttons.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. HistoryPanelRow.swift:56-57, DownloadHistoryRow.swift:84-92 and BookmarksSettingsView.swift:200-207 all activate through .contentShape(Rectangle()) + .onTapGesture on a bare HStack with no .isButton trait and no accessibility action. grep across History/Downloads/Bookmarks/Extensions/Passwords/Containers/Importer/Files returns 4 accessibility hits, all in Files and BookmarksBar, matching the claim. The hover action buttons are also always laid out at opacity 0 (HistoryPanelRow.swift:41-43), so VoiceOver announces controls the sighted user cannot see.

kept.title: Bookmark dialogs use literal corner radii and their own shadow, against the Theme rule
kept.evidence: `BookmarkDialogCard` ends with `.cornerRadius(11)` (110), `ConditionallyConcentricRectangle(cornerRadius: 11).stroke(theme.border, lineWidth: 0.5)` (112-113), `.cornerRadius(14)` (117) and `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 20, y: 8)` (118). `Theme.swift:22-27` says "Every surface picks one of these; a literal radius anywhere else is a bug" (button 6, row 10, pane 13), and `Theme.swift:30-41` defines `auraFloatingShadow()` as "The one shadow a floating Aura surface may carry" at radius 6, y 2, opacity 0.12. kept.title: History panel search runs a SwiftData fetch on the main thread on every keystroke
kept.evidence: `.onChange(of: searchText) { _, _ in reload() }` (line 54) and `reload()` (261) call `historyManager.page(matching:range:in:offset:limit:)` synchronously. That predicate is `history.urlString.localizedStandardContains(trimmed) || history.title.localizedStandardContains(trimmed)` (`HistoryManager.swift:196-199`), which SQLite cannot index, so every character types a full unindexed scan of the space's history on the main actor. The two other debounced searches in the codebase show the intended pattern: `ExtensionStoreModel.scheduleSearch` (250 ms `Task.sleep`) and `LauncherViewModel`'s `Debouncer(delay: 0.2)`.
kept.user_impact: Typing in the history search field stutters once the table has a few thousand visits; each keystroke blocks the chrome for the length of a table scan.
kept.fix: Fix stands as written (Task-based 200 ms debounce mirroring ExtensionStoreModel.scheduleSearch). Also cancel the task in the range/containerId handlers so a stale keystroke reload cannot land after an immediate one.
kept.verify_reason: Code confirmed: HistoryPanelView.swift:54 reloads on every keystroke and reload() (:261-276) calls historyManager.page synchronously on the main actor with a localizedStandardContains predicate (HistoryManager.swift:196-203). The user impact is overstated, though: the descriptor carries fetchLimit = limit + 1 = 51 (HistoryManager.swift:210), so SQLite stops after 51 matches; only a query with few or no matches degrades into a full scan of the space. Worth debouncing, not a visible stutter for most users.

kept.title: "Move to Trash" removes the download row even when trashing the file failed
kept.evidence: `func moveToTrash(_ download: Download)` is `if download.status == .completed, let url = download.destinationURL { try? FileManager.default.trashItem(at: url, resultingItemURL: nil) }` then `deleteDownload(download)` (573-577). The `try?` discards the error, and the row is deleted unconditionally. The menu item that calls it is labelled "Move to Trash" (`DownloadHistoryRow.swift:157`).
kept.user_impact: When the file has been moved, renamed or sits on a volume with no Trash, the row vanishes as if it worked and the file stays on disk with no way back to it from Aura.
kept.fix: Don't return on every error, or a download whose file the user already deleted can never be cleared from the list by this item. Only keep the row when the file is still there: `if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) { do { try FileManager.default.trashItem(at: url, resultingItemURL: nil) } catch { ToastManager.shared.show("Could not move \(download.fileName) to the Trash: \(error.localizedDescription)", type: .error); return } }` before deleteDownload(download). ToastManager.show(_:type:icon:duration:) matches (ToastManager.swift:17-22).
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at DownloadManager.swift:572-577: try? swallows the error and deleteDownload runs unconditionally, behind a menu item labelled 'Move to Trash' (DownloadHistoryRow.swift:149-154). Real but rare (moved file, no-Trash volume), hence low rather than medium.

kept.title: History panel never refreshes while it is open: new visits and outside deletions do not appear
kept.evidence: `items` is plain @State filled by `reload()` (HistoryPanelView.swift:261-276), and the only triggers are `.onAppear(perform: reload)` (:53) and `.onChange` of searchText, range and containerId (:54-56). HistoryManager is @Observable but exposes no observable property the panel reads — `record(...)` (HistoryManager.swift:72-130) and `delete(_:)` (:219-222) only touch the ModelContext, and there is no notification either (`grep -rn 'Notification.Name' aura/Features/History` returns nothing). The sidebar panel stays mounted while browsing: clicking a row calls `open(_:inNewTab:)` (:262-276), which loads in the active tab with the panel still on screen.
kept.user_impact: With the History panel open, clicking a row and then browsing on adds nothing to the list, and pages visited in another window never show up. The panel silently shows a snapshot from whenever it was opened, so the user thinks history stopped recording until they collapse and reopen it.
kept.fix: Give the manager one observed revision counter and let the panel watch it. In HistoryManager add `private(set) var revision = 0`, bump it in `record` right after the `try? modelContext.save()` (HistoryManager.swift:129), in `delete(_:)` and in `delete(range:in:)`; in HistoryPanelView add `.onChange(of: historyManager.revision) { _, _ in reload() }` next to the existing handlers. Cheaper than a @Query and it reuses the reload path that already exists.

kept.title: Downloads groups by rolling dates while History groups by calendar boundaries, so a 20-day-old file reads "Last Month"
kept.evidence: DownloadsHistoryView.groupByDate builds its buckets by subtracting from today: `startOf1MonthAgo = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: -1, to: startOfToday)` (:201) labelled "Last Month" (:215), plus "2 Weeks Ago", "3 Months Ago", "6 Months Ago", "Last Year" (:214-220). HistoryGrouping.buckets (HistoryGrouping.swift:21-40) uses calendar boundaries and a different label set: Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, This Month, Last Month, Older. Its doc comment (HistoryGrouping.swift:6-8) claims it uses "the ordered-bucket table Aura's downloads panel already uses, so the two panels group and order the same way", which is not true of either the bounds or the labels. Consequence of the rolling bounds: a download from 20 days ago clears startOf1MonthAgo but not startOf2WeeksAgo, so it is filed under "Last Month" even when it happened this month.
kept.user_impact: The two panels sit in the same sidebar slot and swap, and their date headings disagree; a file downloaded three weeks ago is headed "Last Month" while a page visited the same day is headed "This Month".
kept.fix: Delete the private bucket table in DownloadsHistoryView.groupByDate and call HistoryGrouping.buckets(now:) instead, keeping the local grouping loop (`buckets.first { date >= $0.start }`) over `download.completedAt ?? download.createdAt`. One bucket table, both panels, and the HistoryGrouping comment becomes true. Drop the now-unused startOf2WeeksAgo/3/6-month/1-year lets.

perf.summary: The hot paths have clearly been worked on once already (debounced launcher search, coalesced session writes, cached user scripts, bounded favicon caches), but the remaining costs sit exactly where a user feels them: the first page load carries a launch-time paint probe that spawns a second web process and two floating windows, every relaunch re-runs full favicon discovery for every restored tab and downloads each site's HTML as an image, and every launcher or address-bar keystroke rebuilds the whole suggestion list plus a window-sized mask bitmap. None of this is architectural; each finding is a few lines in one or two files. The launch path also spends 110 ms of hard-coded asyncAfter sleep before the restored tab's load even starts, which is a straight subtraction from the 0.95 s median PERFORMANCE.md reports.

kept.title: Paint probe runs during the first page load, costing an extra web process and two floating windows
kept.evidence: `BrowserPage.init` calls `ExtensionManager.shared.attach(to:)` (BrowserPage.swift:139), which calls `start()` (ExtensionManager.swift:195) → `WebRequestBroker.prepare()` (ExtensionManager.swift:253) → `Task { await AuraWebBundle.probe() }` (WebRequestBroker.swift:177). `probe` guards only on `isEnabled` (AuraWebBundle.swift:161), and `extensionRequestBlocking` defaults to true (`defaults.object(forKey:) as? Bool ?? true`, SettingsStore.swift:442). It then runs `PaintProbe.run(pool:)`, which builds two `WKWebView`s — one on a brand new `WKProcessPool()` for the control (AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:236) — hosts each in a borderless `.floating` `NSWindow` ordered front with `orderFrontRegardless()` (AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:315-337), waits `settle` = 2 s plus `waitUntilTicking` up to 1.5 s, and on `.inconclusive` runs the whole thing a second time (AuraWebBundle.swift:179). Both fixture pages run an unthrottled `requestAnimationFrame` loop the whole time (framesScript, line 77).
kept.user_impact: Opening the first web page spawns a third WebContent process and two always-on-top windows that paint a rAF loop for 2 to 4 seconds while the user's own page is loading. A third-party window manager sees two new NSWindows appear and re-tiles the browser window off screen.
kept.fix: Two corrections to the proposed fix. (1) Do not move the probe into OraRoot.scheduleDeferredWork: that runs per window (OraRoot.swift:246), so a second window would start a second probe, while WebRequestBroker.prepare() is already one-shot behind ExtensionManager.start()'s hasStarted guard. Keep it where it is and just delay it: `Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2)); await AuraWebBundle.probe() }` in WebRequestBroker.prepare(). Smaller diff, keeps the single-run guarantee, and by then ordinary traffic has usually satisfied stage one so no probe pages get built at all. (2) Do not shrink contentRect to one point. screenSample requires `image.width > 1, image.height > 1` (AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:352) and screenVerdict compares fixture share against the control, so a 1pt window makes the screen stage permanently inconclusive, which AuraWebBundle.swift:186-190 now reads as broken and switches request blocking off. Keep the 320x200 frame and the one-point-on-screen placement, change only the class: NSPanel(contentRect: view.frame, styleMask: [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel], backing: .buffered, defer: false) with isFloatingPanel = true and isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true, so the window reads as a utility panel (AXFloatingWindow) rather than a document window to a tiling manager. files_to_touch becomes WebRequestBroker.swift and AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift only.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed end to end. BrowserPage.swift:146 calls ExtensionManager.attach(to:) inside init; attach calls start() (ExtensionManager.swift:246), which calls WebRequestBroker.prepare() (ExtensionManager.swift:251), which fires Task { await AuraWebBundle.probe() } (WebRequestBroker.swift:177). probe guards only on isEnabled, and extensionRequestBlocking defaults true (SettingsStore.swift:442, file is aura/Core/Utilities/SettingsStore.swift, not Core/Services). PaintProbe.run builds two WKWebViews, one on a brand-new WKProcessPool for the control (AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:236), each hosted in a borderless .floating NSWindow ordered front with orderFrontRegardless (hostWindow, lines 313-337), settles 2 s, and AuraWebBundle.swift:179 re-runs the whole thing on .inconclusive. Both fixtures run an unthrottled rAF loop (framesScript, line 77). On a cold launch answersMessages also builds a third throwaway web view first (AuraWebBundle.swift:201-206) because didHearFromBundle is still false. The two floating windows appearing during the first page load is exactly the reported symptom.

kept.title: Every relaunch resets each tab's favicon to the site root, re-runs full icon discovery and downloads the homepage HTML as an image
kept.evidence: `FaviconService.faviconURL(for:)` returns `sourceURLCache[normalizedDomain] ?? canonicalURL(for:)`, and `canonicalURL` is `URL(string: "https://\(domain)")`, the site's homepage (FaviconService.swift:132-167). `sourceURLCache` is in-memory only, so it is empty at launch. `setFavicon()` then reads `guard self.favicon != faviconURL || !fileExists(saveURL)` (Tab.swift:151): the persisted `favicon` holds the real icon URL from the last run, `faviconURL` is now the homepage, so the guard passes and line 152 does `self.favicon = faviconURL`, overwriting a good icon URL with the page URL and kicking off `downloadAndSaveFavicon`, which finds no `originalBytes` and re-runs the whole `FaviconFinder` discovery plus up to three candidate downloads (FaviconService.swift:261-292). Meanwhile the sidebar row renders `AsyncImage(url: favicon)` (TabItem.swift:53) against that homepage URL. `HistoryManager.record` carries the same comment for the same bug it already fixed there: "storing the page itself made every reader fetch the HTML as an image" (HistoryManager.swift:118-121). `setFavicon()` is called on every `.finished` navigation and every SPA URL message (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:218, 563).
kept.user_impact: Cold launch with a dozen restored tabs fires a dozen full favicon rediscoveries plus a dozen homepage HTML downloads that can never decode as images, on a connection the user wants for the page in front of them. Sidebar icons also fall back to the globe glyph after every relaunch until discovery finishes.
kept.fix: The proposed guard regresses cross-domain navigation. TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:215-217 documents why setFavicon is called unconditionally: gating on the file or on `favicon == nil` left the previous site's icon on the tab after a cross-domain move, and `faviconLocalFile == nil || !fileExists` is true-free for exactly that case. Key the skip on the domain instead, and stop writing the guess at all: add `@Transient var faviconDomain: String?` next to the other transients (Tab.swift:29-40), then in setFavicon replace lines 151-152 with `guard faviconDomain != domain || !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: saveURL.path) else { return }` / `faviconDomain = domain`, and drop `self.favicon = faviconURL`. The completion at line 156 stays the one writer of a resolved URL, but its `self.favicon == faviconURL` re-check has to become `self.faviconDomain == domain`. Same guess is written at tab creation (TabManager.swift:566 and TabManager+Spaces.swift:57 pass `FaviconService.shared.faviconURL(for:)` straight into `Tab.favicon`); those two call sites have to pass nil for the fix to hold, see the missed finding. Do not delete the AsyncImage branch from FavIcon in the same change: LocalFavIcon only ever loads from `.onAppear` on its globe branch (TabItem.swift:25), so with AsyncImage gone a row whose faviconLocalFile arrives while it is mounted keeps the globe. If the branch is to go, LocalFavIcon needs `.task(id: faviconLocalFile)` first.
kept.verify_reason: The mechanism is real: favicon is persisted (Tab.swift:20), sourceURLCache is in-memory only (FaviconService.swift:59), faviconURL(for:) falls back to canonicalURL = https://domain (FaviconService.swift:132-134,165-167), so after a relaunch the guard at Tab.swift:151 always passes and line 152 overwrites the resolved icon URL with the site root. Two parts of the evidence are wrong, which is why this is medium and not high. (a) downloadAndSaveFavicon ignores the URL it is handed (`faviconURL _: URL`, FaviconService.swift:294-307) and goes through sharedPayload(for: domain), which is deduped per domain by payloadTasks and by originalBytes, so there is no homepage-HTML download in the service and no per-tab rediscovery, only one per domain per session. (b) setFavicon only runs from a finished navigation or an SPA URL message (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:218, 565), so a restored session does not fire a dozen of these at launch; only tabs that actually load do. What is genuinely user-visible is downstream: recordHistory runs immediately after setFavicon in the same .finished block (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:219) and reads tab.favicon, so the first visit to a domain in a session writes the site root into History.faviconURL, and the launcher then renders that through AsyncImage (LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:66-72 -> TabItem.swift:54), fetching page HTML as an image per row.

kept.title: Launcher suggestions get a fresh UUID per keystroke, so every row's view tree and favicon request is rebuilt on each character
kept.evidence: `LauncherSuggestion` declares `let id = UUID()` (line 10) and `runLocalSearch` constructs a completely new array on every debounced keystroke (LauncherViewModel.swift:113-126). `LauncherSuggestionsView` iterates `ForEach(suggestions)` using that identity (LauncherSuggestionsView.swift:13), so SwiftUI treats every row as new: `LauncherSuggestionItem.icon` rebuilds `FavIcon`, which restarts `AsyncImage(url:)` (TabItem.swift:53) and re-runs `LocalFavIcon.loadFavicon`'s `DispatchQueue.global` hop (TabItem.swift:29-40) for up to six history rows plus six tab rows. Identical rows across two keystrokes share no identity at all.
kept.user_impact: Typing in the launcher or the address bar tears down and rebuilds the entire result list on every character, restarting a URLSession image load per row per keystroke. The icons visibly blink between characters and rows cannot animate in or out.
kept.fix: The proposed contentKey is not unique and would give ForEach duplicate ids. aiSuggestions builds four rows through createAISuggestion(engineName:query:), all with `title: query` and `url: nil` (LauncherViewModel.swift:212-215), and they reach the list through `trailing`, which merge() appends without passing through dedupeByURL (LauncherResultScoring.swift:217-227) — so all four would collapse onto the key "aiChat|<query>". Two open tabs on the same address collide the same way, since mixOpenTabs appends leftover tabs after dedupe (LauncherResultScoring.swift:200-202). Either put `name` in the key (`"\(type)|\(name ?? "")|\(url?.absoluteString ?? title)"`) or, simpler and collision-proof, use positional identity at both call sites: `ForEach(suggestions.indices, id: \.self) { index in ... suggestions[index] ... }`. Rows keep their view across keystrokes and AsyncImage only reloads when the url it is handed actually changes. files_to_touch must include aura/Features/Browser/URLBar/URLBarField.swift:318 — the address bar renders the same rows and has the same churn.
kept.verify_reason: Identity churn is real: `let id = UUID()` (LauncherSuggestion.swift:10), runLocalSearch rebuilds the whole array per debounced keystroke (LauncherViewModel.swift:113-125), and both list views iterate with the default Identifiable id (LauncherSuggestionsView.swift:13 and, missed by the auditor, URLBarField.swift:318). So every row is torn down and rebuilt, restarting AsyncImage (TabItem.swift:54) and LocalFavIcon's global-queue decode (TabItem.swift:29-40) per row per keystroke. Downgraded from high because the cost is a URLCache-backed reload plus a placeholder flash rather than a stall, and it only bites rows that carry a faviconURL.

kept.title: Address-bar editing backdrop redraws a full-window mask bitmap on every keystroke
kept.evidence: `EffectView.holes` has `didSet { if holes != oldValue { rebuildMask() } }` (lines 17-19), and `rebuildMask` allocates `NSImage(size: bounds.size, flipped: true)` and fills the whole rect through a `CGContext` (lines 42-54). The holes come from `BrowserView.editingHoles`, built from `appState.urlFieldFrame` and `appState.urlSuggestionsFrame` (BrowserView.swift:64-67) and handed to a window-spanning `BlurEffectView` (BrowserView.swift:81-84). `urlSuggestionsFrame` is written from an `onGeometryChange` on the suggestions overlay (URLBarField.swift:105-110), whose height changes whenever the number of suggestion rows changes, which is most keystrokes. The sibling `Color.black.opacity(0.12).mask(cutout...)` re-paths the same rects at the same time (BrowserView.swift:85-86).
kept.user_impact: Each character typed in the address bar allocates and rasterises a window-sized bitmap (about 10 MB at 1440x900 @2x) on the main thread before the frame can composite, which reads as the field lagging the keyboard.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. holes didSet rebuilds immediately (BlurEffectView.swift:17-19), rebuildMask draws a bounds-sized NSImage through a CGContext (lines 34-56), the holes come from appState.urlFieldFrame + urlSuggestionsFrame (BrowserView.swift:64-68) fed to a window-spanning BlurEffectView (BrowserView.swift:81-84), and urlSuggestionsFrame is written from an onGeometryChange on the suggestions overlay (URLBarField.swift:105-110) whose height moves whenever the row count moves. addressEditingBlur defaults true (SettingsStore.swift:445), so this is the default path. Not quite every keystroke though — the frame only changes when the list height changes, and NSImage(size:flipped:) defers the draw to first use — so medium rather than high.

kept.title: 110 ms of hard-coded sleep sits between first appearance and the restored tab's first byte
kept.evidence: `BrowserView.onAppear` is the only thing that builds the active tab's web view at launch (`TabManager.initializeActiveContainerAndTab` sets `activeTab` without calling `restoreTransientState`, TabManager.swift:283-296), and it does so behind `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.1)` (BrowserView.swift:270). `restoreTransientState` then defers the load again: `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.01) { self.startRestoredLoad(...) }` with the comment "Load after a short delay to ensure layout" (Tab.swift:306-310).
kept.user_impact: Every cold launch waits 110 ms doing nothing before the restored page's network request is issued, roughly 11% of the 0.95 s median launch PERFORMANCE.md records, and it is dead time rather than work.
kept.fix: Do not call restoreTransientState synchronously from onAppear. Building the WKWebView, its configuration, the user scripts and the extension controller is the most expensive main-thread block on the launch path (BrowserPage.swift:120-175), and running it inside the first onAppear pushes it in front of the first frame — the launch metric PERFORMANCE.md records is XCTApplicationLaunchMetric(waitUntilResponsive:), so this would trade 100 ms of dead time for a worse measured number. Use the pattern OraRoot already uses for deferred launch work (OraRoot.swift:247): `DispatchQueue.main.async { tab.restoreTransientState(...) }`. The inner hop in Tab.swift:306-310 can go entirely — call startRestoredLoad and set isWebViewReady inline. Doing that also makes perf-12's dead branch self-evidently dead, since isWebViewReady is then true before onChange runs.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. initializeActiveContainerAndTab sets activeTab without restoring (TabManager.swift:283-296), BrowserView.onAppear is the only builder at launch and waits 0.1 s (BrowserView.swift:269-277), and restoreTransientState defers the load another 0.01 s (Tab.swift:306-310). BrowserPage.load already parks the request when the page is not ready (BrowserPage.swift:253-258) and startRestoredLoad has its own sessionRestoreTimeout fallback (TabSession.swift:220-231), so the layout justification in the comment does not hold.

kept.title: Launcher history search materialises 200 rows per keystroke to show six
kept.evidence: `HistoryManager.search` sets `descriptor.fetchLimit = 200` (line 165) and returns full `History` objects. Its only caller is `LauncherViewModel.runLocalSearch` (LauncherViewModel.swift:113-116), which passes the result to `historySuggestions`, and that does `histories.prefix(6)` (LauncherViewModel.swift:395). The fetch runs on the main actor inside the 40 ms debounce window (LauncherViewModel.swift:71-81), so a burst of typing pays it repeatedly.
kept.user_impact: Each keystroke faults 200 SwiftData objects into the main-thread context to display six rows, and the surplus 194 stay registered in the window's `ModelContext` for the rest of the session.
kept.fix: Since prefix(6) runs before dedupeByURL and mixOpenTabs, the surplus rows do not feed either, so 24 is more headroom than the caller can use. `descriptor.fetchLimit = 12` covers the six rows with slack for a future change; anything larger is dead weight. Leave the comment above the descriptor accurate: it currently claims the bound is what keeps the table out of memory.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed but overstated. fetchLimit is 200 (HistoryManager.swift:165), the only caller is runLocalSearch (LauncherViewModel.swift:113-116), and historySuggestions takes `histories.prefix(6)` (LauncherViewModel.swift:395) before any dedupe or merge, so the other 194 rows can never influence the result. Real waste, but it is a bounded, sorted, predicate-filtered fetch behind a 40 ms debounce (LauncherViewModel.swift:16), not something the user feels; the lasting cost is the objects staying registered in the window context.

kept.title: Tab switcher captures full-resolution page snapshots for 200pt previews and keeps them all in memory
kept.evidence: `takeSnapshot` uses `BrowserSnapshotConfiguration(rect: nil, afterScreenUpdates: false)` (line 289) with no `snapshotWidth`, even though `BrowserSnapshotConfiguration` exposes one and documents it as "Downscales the result" (BrowserEngineTypes.swift:97). The previews draw at `previewWidth: 200` / `previewHeight: 125` (lines 24-25). Every result is retained in `@State private var tabSnapshots: [Tab: TabSnapshot]` (line 16) for up to `SettingsStore.shared.maxRecentTabs` tabs, default 5 (SettingsStore.swift:461). The surrounding `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInteractive).async` (line 288) immediately hops back with `DispatchQueue.main.async` (line 292) and does no work off the main thread.
kept.user_impact: Holding ⌃Tab retains five full-window bitmaps (about 10 MB each at 1440x900 @2x) to draw 200pt thumbnails, and each capture forces the web process to render at full resolution.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:289 builds BrowserSnapshotConfiguration(rect: nil, afterScreenUpdates: false) with snapshotWidth left nil, while BrowserPage only sets WKSnapshotConfiguration.snapshotWidth when it is present (BrowserPage.swift:344-345), so WebKit returns a full-resolution bitmap; previews are 200x125 (lines 24-25), results are held in @State tabSnapshots for up to maxRecentTabs tabs (default 5, SettingsStore.swift:461). The global(qos:.userInteractive) block at line 288 only builds a struct before hopping back to main at line 292, so it does nothing.

kept.title: WebKit warm-up spins up the wrong WebContent service when request blocking is on, which is the default
kept.evidence: `warmUp()` builds `WKWebView(frame: .zero)` with no configuration (line 61), so it uses the default process pool and launches `com.apple.WebKit.WebContent`. Real pages get `AuraWebBundle.apply(to: webConfiguration)` (BrowserPage.swift:71), which points the configuration at the injected-bundle pool; that pool makes WebKit launch `com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.Development` instead, as documented in AuraWebBundle.swift:9-13. `extensionRequestBlocking` defaults to true (SettingsStore.swift:442), so the default configuration warms a service the first real page never uses.
kept.user_impact: The stated benefit of the warm-up, "a window that opens onto the start page pays for the whole stack inside the first ⌘T keystroke", does not land for the default configuration: the first tab still pays for a cold Development WebContent launch.
kept.fix: Warming through AuraWebBundle.apply also forces the lazy `processPool` static into existence at launch, which installs the injected-bundle message handler (AuraWebBundle.swift:88-111) earlier than today. That is a behaviour change worth naming in the comment, and it interacts well with perf-1: the warm-up page makes the bundle speak, so a deferred probe usually settles at stage one without building any pages.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading. warmUp builds WKWebView(frame: .zero) with no configuration (BrowserEngine.swift:61), so it uses the default pool, while every real page runs AuraWebBundle.apply(to: webConfiguration) in BrowserPage.init and gets the injected-bundle pool when isEnabled (AuraWebBundle.swift:129-132), which moves pages to com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.Development (documented at AuraWebBundle.swift:9-13). extensionRequestBlocking defaults true (SettingsStore.swift:442). Held at medium rather than higher because the Networking and GPU services the warm-up also starts are shared across pools, so only the WebContent launch is wasted.

kept.title: Compact-mode hover tracking evaluates every mouse move twice
kept.evidence: `WindowMouseMonitor.Monitor.init` installs both a full-window `MouseCatcherView` whose `mouseMoved` calls `broadcast()` (lines 207, 255-258) and an `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: [.mouseMoved])` that also calls `broadcast()` (lines 213-216). The catcher's tracking area is what makes the window post `.mouseMoved` over the `WKWebView` in the first place (comment at lines 168-175), so both fire for the same event. Each `broadcast()` reads `NSEvent.mouseLocation` and runs every listener's `evaluate`, which recomputes `hotRect` via `window.convertToScreen(content.convert(...))` (lines 120-129).
kept.user_impact: While the toolbar or sidebar is hidden, moving the pointer runs the edge-reveal test twice per event on the main thread, doubling a cost already paid at mouse-report rate.
kept.fix: Do not delete the local monitor. The comment at lines 168-175 says the catcher and acceptsMouseMovedEvents are both there because a WKWebView under the pointer can silence a window's moves; removing one of two deliberately redundant sources to save a coordinate conversion risks the chrome not revealing at all, which is a far worse bug than the one being fixed. Drop the duplicate instead, in Monitor: keep `private var lastLocation: NSPoint?` and start broadcast() with `let location = NSEvent.mouseLocation; guard location != lastLocation else { return }; lastLocation = location` — the catcher and the monitor report the same event at the same point, and a real move always changes the point.
kept.verify_reason: The double evaluation is real: the catcher's mouseMoved calls broadcast (GlobalMouseTrackingArea.swift:207, 255-258) and the local monitor calls it again for the same event (lines 213-216). Downgraded to low because the per-event work is a couple of coordinate conversions per listener (lines 120-129), listeners number two or three, and mouse-move events top out around 100/s, so this is not something a user perceives.

kept.title: Tab.loadingProgress is written on every navigation phase and read nowhere
kept.evidence: `@Transient @Published var loadingProgress: Double = 10.0` (Tab.swift:39). Grepping `loadingProgress` across `aura/` returns only four writes, all in `TabBrowserPageDelegate` (lines 185, 192, 202, 229). Nothing reads it. Line 229 exists purely to zero it, and it is scheduled through a retained `progressResetWorkItem` plus `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3.0)` on every finished navigation (lines 74, 227-232). The load state views actually show comes from `tab.isLoading` (URLBarField.swift:288, SidebarURLDisplay.swift:35).
kept.user_impact: Dead `@Published` state fires Combine change notifications on every navigation phase and keeps a 3-second work item alive per navigation for a value nobody renders.
kept.fix: Delete the property and its four writers, plus `progressResetWorkItem` (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:74) and the `asyncAfter` block at lines 227-232. Everything that shows load state already reads `isLoading`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed dead: `loadingProgress` (Tab.swift:39) has four writers, all in TabBrowserPageDelegate (185, 192, 202, 229), and no readers anywhere in aura/ or auraTests/. progressResetWorkItem exists only to zero it. Downgraded to low because nothing observes Tab through Combine — no view in the repo declares @ObservedObject over a Tab, SwiftUI tracks Tab through the @Model/Observation macro instead — so the @Published writes notify nobody and the cost is one retained DispatchWorkItem per navigation, not a re-render storm.

kept.title: Tab maintenance timer runs a full store sweep every minute per window, awake or idle
kept.evidence: `startCleanupTimer` installs `Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 60.0, repeats: true)` in `TabManager.init` (line 792) with no stop condition, one per browser window, running whether or not the app is frontmost. Each tick runs `runTabMaintenance` (TabManager+Hibernation.swift:373-383): `fetchContainers()`, four passes over every tab, then a second `fetchContainers()` at line 382 and `sessionStore.prune`, which does an unbounded `modelContext.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TabSession>())` (TabSessionStore.swift:137). The timer body also wraps its work in a redundant `DispatchQueue.main.async` inside a handler that already runs on the main run loop (TabManager.swift:793).
kept.user_impact: An idle Aura in the background wakes the main thread once a minute per open window for two full container fetches and a session-table scan, which shows up as CPU wake-ups on battery.
kept.fix: Name the trade in the guard's comment: the skip also postpones captureActiveSession, and that one exists as crash insurance for the front tab's scroll position (TabManager+Hibernation.swift:385-387). It is still the right call while the app is in the background, since nothing the user does can move that offset, but the comment should say so rather than only talking about ageing.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. The 60 s repeating timer is installed unconditionally in init with no stop condition (TabManager.swift:791-796), one per window, and each tick runs runTabMaintenance: fetchContainers, four passes over every tab, a second fetchContainers, and sessionStore.prune, which does an unbounded fetch of every TabSession row (TabManager+Hibernation.swift:373-383, TabSessionStore.swift:137). captureActiveSession also fires a JS round trip into the web process every minute (TabSession.swift:189-208), so the idle wake reaches the content process too. The inner DispatchQueue.main.async at line 793 is redundant: the timer is scheduled on the main run loop from a main-actor init.

kept.title: Every tab switch schedules a restoreTransientState that activateTab has already done
kept.evidence: `TabManager.activateTab` builds the web view synchronously when `!tab.isWebViewReady` (TabManager.swift:775-782), but `isWebViewReady` is only set true inside the 0.01 s hop in `restoreTransientState` (Tab.swift:307-310). So when `BrowserView.onChange(of: tabManager.activeTab)` runs one turn later and tests `!tab.isWebViewReady` (line 254), the flag is still false and it schedules a second `restoreTransientState`, which returns immediately at `if browserPage != nil { return }` (Tab.swift:279).
kept.user_impact: A dead work item per tab switch, and a second reader of a flag whose meaning is "the load has started" rather than "the page exists", which is what makes the branch look correct.
kept.fix: Sequence this after perf-5: if the 0.01 s hop in restoreTransientState goes away, isWebViewReady is already true when onChange runs and the branch stops firing on its own, which makes deleting BrowserView.swift:254-263 obviously safe rather than an argument about ordering.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. The only non-nil writers of activeTab are activateTab (TabManager.swift:770) and initializeActiveContainerAndTab (line 292, which predates the view and so never triggers onChange), and activateTab already builds the page at lines 775-782. isWebViewReady flips true only inside the 0.01 s hop (Tab.swift:307-310), so BrowserView.swift:254 always sees false and always schedules a call that returns at Tab.swift:279.

kept.title: NSPageView logs at default level on every space switch and data-source update
kept.evidence: `updateNSViewController` emits two `logger.log` calls with interpolated counts whenever the page list or the selection changes (lines 78-86), and `updateDataSource` / `updateSelectedIndex` each log again (lines 155, 159). `logger.log` is `OSLogType.default`, which is persisted to the on-disk unified log rather than only held in memory. `pageObjects` here is the sidebar's `containers` array (SidebarView.swift:291-295), so this fires on every space switch and every container mutation.
kept.user_impact: Switching spaces writes four persisted log lines about internal view-controller state that only mean something while debugging this one file.
kept.fix: Change the four calls to `logger.debug(...)`, which stays memory-only in a Release build, or delete them. The `identifierFor: unexpected object type` line (178) is the only one that reports a real fault and should become `logger.error`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. Four logger.log calls at OSLogType.default (NSPageView.swift:78, 84, 155, 159) fire whenever pageObjects or the selection changes, and pageObjects is the sidebar's containers array (SidebarView.swift:291-295), so a space switch persists four lines to the on-disk log about view-controller internals. Line 178 uses logger.log for a genuine type fault.

kept.title: Tab search with an empty query fetches every tab in the store, unfiltered and unbounded
kept.evidence: When `trimmedText` is empty the predicate is `#Predicate { _ in true }` (line 28) with no container filter, and the descriptor carries no `fetchLimit` (line 41), so it materialises every `Tab` row across every space and then scores and sorts all of them (lines 44-52). The non-empty branch does scope to `activeContainerId` (line 37). `TabManager.search` is public API (TabManager.swift:187); `LauncherViewModel` guards against empty text before reaching it, but nothing in the service does.
kept.user_impact: Any caller that passes an empty or whitespace query loads the whole tab table into the window's context and sorts it, on the main thread.
kept.fix: Do not add a bare fetchLimit. The descriptor has no sortBy, so a limit would hand back an arbitrary 20 rows and the recency ranking in combinedScore (TabSearchingService.swift:60-70) would silently pick from the wrong candidates. Either scope the predicate only — `predicate = #Predicate { $0.container.id == activeContainerId }` and leave it unbounded, matching what the non-empty branch already does — or pair the limit with `sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.lastAccessedAt, order: .reverse)]`, which is the key the scorer actually ranks on.
kept.verify_reason: The code reads as described — `#Predicate { _ in true }` with no container scope and no fetchLimit (TabSearchingService.swift:28, 41) — but it is not reachable today: the only caller is LauncherViewModel.swift:117, and searchHandler returns early on empty text (LauncherViewModel.swift:56-62). So this is defensive hardening of a public entry point (TabManager.swift:187-197), not something a user hits, hence low.

kept.title: Every new tab is seeded with the site's homepage URL as its favicon, so the sidebar downloads the page HTML as an image
kept.evidence: `openTab` builds the Tab with `favicon: host.flatMap { FaviconService.shared.faviconURL(for: $0) }` (TabManager.swift:566), and `TabManager+Spaces.swift:57` does the same for a space-scoped open. Until that domain has been resolved once this session, `faviconURL(for:)` returns `canonicalURL(for:)` = `https://<domain>` (FaviconService.swift:132-134, 165-167), the page itself. The sidebar row then renders `FavIcon`, whose first branch is `AsyncImage(url: favicon)` as soon as `isWebViewReady` is true (TabItem.swift:52-54), so URLSession fetches the site's homepage HTML and hands it to an image decoder that cannot read it. HistoryManager already carries the comment for this exact mistake one layer up: "storing the page itself made every reader fetch the HTML as an image" (HistoryManager.swift:118-120).
kept.user_impact: Opening a tab on a domain not yet resolved this session fires a second full download of the page, over the same connection the page itself is loading on, purely to fail an image decode. On a heavy site that is hundreds of kilobytes per new tab.
kept.fix: Pass nil at both creation sites and let the resolved URL arrive from `setFavicon`'s completion, the way History already does: drop `favicon:` from the `Tab(...)` literal at TabManager.swift:566 and change `favicon:` to nil at TabManager+Spaces.swift:57, with a one-line comment saying an unresolved icon is not an icon. `FaviconService.faviconURL(for:)` should keep its homepage fallback only for callers that want a fetch target, not for callers storing a display URL.

kept.title: Launcher rows ignore the favicon already decoded on disk unless a remote URL is also set
kept.evidence: `icon` reaches `FavIcon` only through `else if suggestion.faviconURL != nil` (LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:66); a row with `faviconURL == nil` falls to the generic `globe`/`magnifyingglass` glyph at line 73, even when `suggestion.faviconLocalFile` is set. History rows carry both fields (LauncherViewModel.swift:389-391), and `HistoryManager.record` deliberately stores nil for an unresolved icon URL while still storing the local file (HistoryManager.swift:115-121), so the exact rows that have a file and no URL are the ones that render a glyph.
kept.user_impact: History suggestions for sites whose icon URL was never resolved show a magnifying glass in the launcher even though the icon is sitting decoded in FaviconService's file cache, which reads as the launcher not knowing sites it visibly knows.
