kept.fix: Widen the branch to the state that actually matters: `} else if suggestion.faviconURL != nil || suggestion.faviconLocalFile != nil {`. `FavIcon` already falls back to `LocalFavIcon` when `favicon` is nil (TabItem.swift:52, 68-71), so no other change is needed.

kept.title: LocalFavIcon never reloads when the icon file lands after the row is on screen
kept.evidence: `loadFavicon` is only invoked from `.onAppear(perform: loadFavicon)` on the globe branch (TabItem.swift:25), and `loadFavicon` returns silently when `faviconLocalFile` is nil or the file is not there yet (lines 29-31). The view has no `onChange`/`task(id:)` on `faviconLocalFile`, so once the globe is showing, a file written later by `downloadAndSaveFavicon` (Tab.swift:154-165) is never picked up for the life of that row. Today the `AsyncImage` branch above it hides this for tabs whose web view is ready (TabItem.swift:52-54), which is why it has not shown up as a visible bug.
kept.user_impact: Rows that only ever use the local path (a not-yet-ready tab, or the placeholder inside FavIcon) keep the globe glyph until something rebuilds the row, and any change that removes the AsyncImage branch on performance grounds would make this the default behaviour.
kept.fix: Replace `.onAppear(perform: loadFavicon)` with `.task(id: faviconLocalFile) { loadFavicon() }` so the decode re-runs when the file the row is pointed at changes. Same one-line shape, and it makes dropping the AsyncImage branch safe later.

shortcuts-menus.summary: The shortcut catalogue and the custom menu stack (AuraMenuController/Host/Panel) are genuinely well built: fixed metrics, a submenu safe zone, type-select, and a unit test that guards default-chord uniqueness. The wiring around them is where it falls apart: seven catalogue rows are rebindable in Settings but reach no command at all, the menu bar reads its chords once at launch so a rebind needs a relaunch, the recorder both fires and records the chord you type (recording ⌘W closes the tab under you) and happily accepts a modifier-less key that would then swallow every keystroke, and ⌘W is on two File-menu items where the second is permanently greyed out. Next/Previous Tab only raise the switcher overlay and never change tab, ⌘P is advertised in two menus but bound nowhere, and the "..." menu ships a second zoom implementation that ignores per-site zoom.

kept.title: ⌘W is on two File-menu items and the second one is permanently disabled
kept.evidence: "Close Tab" takes `KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.close` (⌘W, line 50) and immediately below it "Close Window" takes `.keyboardShortcut("w", modifiers: .command)` (line 57) with `.disabled({ guard let keyWindow = NSApp.keyWindow else { return true } … }())`. That closure runs when the `Commands` body is built, and the body's only dynamic properties are `@AppStorage` values, so `NSApp.keyWindow` is sampled once at launch (nil ⇒ disabled) and never re-sampled when the Passwords window becomes key. Two items on one chord also means AppKit matches the first one in menu order, which is Close Tab.
kept.user_impact: ⌘W in the Passwords window posts `.closeActiveTab` with that window as sender; `WindowEventScope.window` (aura/App/OraRoot.swift:329) requires `sender === window`, so no browser root claims it and the key does nothing. The "Close Window" item sits greyed out in the File menu forever.
kept.fix: Delete the second Button. In the Close Tab action route non-browser key windows to AppKit: `if let key = NSApp.keyWindow, !AppDelegate.isBrowserWindow(key) { key.performClose(nil) } else { NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .closeActiveTab, object: NSApp.keyWindow) }`. AppDelegate.isBrowserWindow (OraApp.swift:66) is the existing test; do not keep the title-string check, it names a window that no longer exists.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed from code. OraCommands.swift:50 binds Close Tab to ⌘W and :52-62 adds a second ⌘W item whose .disabled(...) closure is evaluated once per Commands body build; the struct's only dynamic properties are @AppStorage keys, so NSApp.keyWindow is a stale sample. Two corrections to the auditor: "Settings" is a tab (TabManager.swift:509 sets tab.title = "Settings"), not a window, so the title check only ever matches the Passwords window (PasswordsWindow.swift:44); and because the second item is normally disabled, NSMenu skips it during key-equivalent matching, so Close Tab wins and posts .closeActiveTab with the Passwords window as sender, which no OraRoot claims (WindowEventScope.window). Net user-visible effect: ⌘W does nothing in the Passwords window and the File menu shows a permanently greyed Close Window row. That is a secondary window with a working close button, so medium, not high.

kept.title: Recording a shortcut also executes it: the captured key event is passed through
kept.evidence: The row overlays `KeyCaptureView(onKeyDown: { event in handleKeyCapture(event) })`. That initialiser (aura/Core/Platform/Representables/KeyCaptureView.swift:6) wraps the closure as `{ event in onKeyDown(event); return event }`, so the local monitor returns the event and it continues into `NSApplication.sendEvent`, where menu key equivalents are matched. The unused `init(onKeyDownResult:)` on line 13 is the swallowing variant.
kept.user_impact: Pressing ⌘W while recording records ⌘W and closes the Settings tab at the same time; ⌘T records and opens the launcher on top of Settings; ⌘Q records and asks to quit. Escape is recorded as ⎋ instead of cancelling, so there is no way to back out of the recording chip except clicking it again.
kept.fix: Switch the overlay to `KeyCaptureView(onKeyDownResult:)` and return nil: cancel on `event.keyCode == 53` (Escape) via `cancelEditing()`, otherwise call `handleKeyCapture(event)`; return `event` only when no shortcut is being edited.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:63 uses KeyCaptureView(onKeyDown:), whose init (KeyCaptureView.swift:5-11) wraps the closure to return the event, and the coordinator's local monitor (line 45-49) forwards it, so the key press still reaches sendEvent and the main menu matches its key equivalent. The onKeyDownResult init exists and is unused. Escape (kVK_Escape is in KeyChord.namedKeys, Keyboard.swift:59) is recorded rather than cancelling, so there is no keyboard way out of the recording chip.

kept.title: The recorder accepts a chord with no modifiers, which then eats every keystroke of that letter
kept.evidence: `handleKeyCapture` stores anything `KeyChord(fromEvent:)` returns, and that initialiser (aura/Core/Domain/Keyboard.swift:66) builds an empty modifier set happily. `CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.setCustomShortcut` (line 36) and `SettingsStore.setCustomKeyboardShortcut` (aura/Core/Utilities/SettingsStore+Collections.swift:94) both write it through with no validation.
kept.user_impact: Fat-fingering a bare letter while the chip is armed binds a menu item to that letter. AppKit matches key equivalents before the responder chain, so from then on typing that letter anywhere, including in a page's text field, fires the menu command instead. The only escape is finding the row again and pressing Reset to Default.
kept.fix: Same guard, but also reject the named keys that make unusable bare equivalents: `guard !event.modifierFlags.intersection([.command, .control, .option]).isEmpty else { return }` in handleKeyCapture, before setCustomShortcut. Pair it with finding 2's Escape-cancels path so the chip has a keyboard exit.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. KeyChord(fromEvent:) (Keyboard.swift:66-79) builds an empty modifier set without complaint, handleKeyCapture (ShortcutsSettingsView.swift:87-94) stores whatever it returns, and setCustomShortcut (CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.swift:36-41) persists it. Combined with finding 2 the likely trigger is mundane: the user presses Escape to back out and instead binds a menu item to bare Escape, which then swallows Escape app-wide.

kept.title: Rebinding a shortcut does not reach the menu bar until the app relaunches
kept.evidence: `OraKeyboardShortcutModifier` exists precisely so a rebind re-renders (`@EnvironmentObject private var shortcutManager` in aura/Core/Extensions/View+Shortcuts.swift:6), but `oraShortcut` is used in only four views. Every menu item in OraCommands calls `.keyboardShortcut(KeyboardShortcuts.X.keyboardShortcut)` directly, and the struct's only dynamic properties are `@AppStorage` keys, none of which change when `CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.customShortcuts` publishes.
kept.user_impact: Changing New Tab to ⌥⌘T in Settings shows the new chord in the settings row and in the "..." menu, but the menu bar keeps ⌘T and the old key keeps working until the next launch. Silent, and it makes the whole Shortcuts page look broken.
kept.fix: Use `@StateObject private var shortcuts = CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.shared` rather than @ObservedObject: OraCommands is re-initialised by SwiftUI on each Scene update and @StateObject matches how keyModifierListener/updateService are held elsewhere in this codebase.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed that OraCommands never observes CustomKeyboardShortcutManager: its only dynamic properties are the six @AppStorage keys (OraCommands.swift:4-14) and every item calls .keyboardShortcut(KeyboardShortcuts.X.keyboardShortcut) directly. oraShortcut/View+Shortcuts.swift is used in six chrome views only. The auditor overstates "until the app relaunches": KeyboardShortcutDefinition.keyboardShortcut is computed, so any unrelated rebuild (toggling the sidebar, appearance, toolbar, bookmarks bar) picks the new chord up. That makes the failure intermittent rather than permanent, which is worse to diagnose but medium, not high.

kept.title: Next Tab / Previous Tab never switch tabs and leave the switcher overlay stuck open
kept.evidence: `WindowEvent(.nextTab) { _ in appState.isFloatingTabSwitchVisible = true }` and the identical `.previousTab` row are the only handlers for those events; nothing calls `tabManager.activateTab`. The switcher only commits a selection from `handleModifierChange`, which fires when Control is released (aura/Features/Tabs/Switcher/FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:243).
kept.user_impact: Choosing Tabs > Next Tab with the mouse, or running "Next Tab" from the command palette (aura/Features/Launcher/Models/AppCommand.swift:62), drops a dimming overlay over the window that never resolves because no Control key was ever held. The user has to press Escape or click the backdrop, and the tab never changed.
kept.fix: The proposed helper does not exist: TabManager has neighbour(after:) (TabManager.swift:623) and it only walks one direction, so it cannot serve Previous Tab. Minimal correct fix: keep the overlay off these rows and move the selection directly, e.g. compute the active container's sidebar-ordered tab list (the same ordering selectTabAtIndex builds, TabManager.swift:820-840) and activate the tab one step after/before the active one; factor that ordering out of selectTabAtIndex into a `orderedTabs` property so both callers share it. Files: aura/App/OraRoot.swift, aura/Features/Tabs/State/TabManager.swift.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraRoot.swift:434-435 are the only handlers for .nextTab/.previousTab and both do nothing but set appState.isFloatingTabSwitchVisible = true; the only commit path is handleModifierChange (FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:241-250), which needs a Control release. So the Tabs menu items and the palette rows (AppCommand.swift:62-66) drop a modal overlay that never resolves and never change tab. Not high: the keyboard ⌃⇥ path works, because the key handler at OraRoot.swift:279-283 consumes the event before the menu equivalent matches, so only mouse/palette users hit it.

kept.title: Seven Settings rows rebind shortcuts that no command reads
kept.evidence: `tabs.moveRight`, `tabs.moveLeft` and `developer.toggleDevTools` appear in `allShortcuts` (lines 377, 409) and nowhere else in the repo. `window.close` (⇧⌘W) and `window.fullscreen` (⌃⌘F) are equally unreferenced. `app.quit` and `app.hide` map to AppKit's own items, and `app.preferences` is only read for a display string while the real item hardcodes `.keyboardShortcut(",", modifiers: .command)` (aura/App/OraCommands.swift:336).
kept.user_impact: Settings > Shortcuts lists Move Tab Right, Move Tab Left, Toggle DevTools, Close Window, Fullscreen, Quit, Hide and Preferences as bindable. Pressing the advertised default does nothing for the first five, and rebinding any of the eight changes nothing anywhere.
kept.fix: Keep the deletions, but note the ripple: KeyboardPolishTests' defaultChordsAreUnique and retiredBindingsAreDropped (auraTests/KeyboardPolishTests.swift:110, 128) walk allShortcuts, and ExtensionCommands.collidesWithBuiltIn (ExtensionCommands.swift:92) uses it as the reservation list, so removing window.close (⇧⌘W) and window.fullscreen (⌃⌘F) also frees those chords for extensions. That is correct, since nothing owns them, but land it together with finding 16 so the list means exactly "chords Aura actually uses".
kept.verify_reason: Verified by grep: tabs.moveRight, tabs.moveLeft, developer.toggleDevTools, window.close and window.fullscreen appear only in their definitions and in allShortcuts (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:377, 385, 409). App.quit and App.hide appear only in allShortcuts (:412) and map to AppKit's own items. App.preferences is read in three places for display (AppCommand.swift:111, URLBarMenuButton.swift:150, TopToolbar.swift:183) while the real menu item hardcodes ⌘, (OraCommands.swift:336), so rebinding it changes three labels and no binding.

kept.title: ⌘P is printed next to two Print items but is not bound to anything
kept.evidence: The page context menu row `AuraMenuItem.item("Print…", icon: "printer", shortcut: "⌘P")` and the "..." menu row (aura/Features/Browser/URLBar/URLBarMenuButton.swift:101) both advertise ⌘P. Grepping every `keyboardShortcut(` call in the app returns no "p", and `OraCommands` never touches `CommandGroupPlacement.printItem`, so no menu item carries that key equivalent.
kept.user_impact: Pressing ⌘P on a page does nothing at all, while two menus say it prints. Printing only works by opening a menu and clicking the row.
kept.fix: Smaller than proposed: no new notification is needed if the handler goes where the other page tools live. Add `static func print(_ tab: Tab?)` to PageTools (aura/Features/PageTools/PageTools.swift), have both menus call it, and add the CommandGroup(replacing: .printItem) item posting an existing-style .printPage row through OraRoot's events table alongside .savePageAs. If you want the truly minimal version, drop the ⌘P hint from both menus instead; do not leave the two disagreeing.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: `grep 'keyboardShortcut("p"'` and `grep printItem` over aura/ return nothing, while PageContextMenu.swift:128 and URLBarMenuButton.swift:99 both print ⌘P next to a Print… row. BrowserPage.printPage() exists (BrowserPage+Actions.swift:59), so only the binding is missing.

kept.title: The "..." menu ships a second zoom and a second Save Page As that behave differently from the menu bar's
kept.evidence: `setZoom` writes `webView.pageZoom` directly (line 193) while the View menu's Zoom In/Out/Reset go through `SiteZoomController.step(_:for:)` and `.reset` (aura/App/OraRoot.swift:471-479), which store the level per site. `savePageAs` (line 200) calls `saveWebArchive(named:)` while the File menu and the page context menu both call `PageTools.savePageAs`. All three "..." zoom rows advertise the same chords as the View menu rows.
kept.user_impact: Zooming from the "..." menu is not remembered for the site and is out of step with what ⌘= just did on the same page, so the two zoom paths fight each other. The two Save Page As paths can produce different files and different error handling from the same-named item.
kept.fix: Do not route zoom through notifications: zoomSection() has no hostWindow parameter and tabManager is already in scope, so call the controller directly: `SiteZoomController.step(1, for: tabManager.activeTab)`, `step(-1, ...)`, `reset(tabManager.activeTab)`, and delete setZoom. Replace savePageAs's body with `PageTools.savePageAs(tabManager.activeTab)` and delete the local copy.
kept.verify_reason: The zoom half is confirmed and is the real defect: URLBarMenuButton.setZoom (line 191-194) writes webView.pageZoom in ±0.1 steps, bypassing SiteZoomController.set, which is documented as "the one place zoom is read, written and pushed at a page" (SiteZoom.swift:47), persists per registrable domain and feeds SiteZoomBadge. So the "..." menu's zoom is not remembered, does not follow the 50-300% ladder, and leaves the address-pill badge showing a stale level. The savePageAs half is weaker than claimed: URLBarMenuButton.savePageAs (line 200) reproduces PageTools.fileNameSeed exactly (PageTools.swift:82-85), so it is duplicate code, not different behaviour.

kept.title: ⌘T and ⌘N are dropped when the key window is not a browser window
kept.evidence: New Tab posts `.showLauncher` with `object: NSApp.keyWindow`. `WindowEventScope.windowOrKey` resolves a non-nil sender as `sender === (window ?? keyWindow)` (aura/App/OraRoot.swift:325-333), so when the Passwords window (a plain NSWindow, aura/Features/Passwords/Views/PasswordsWindow.swift:44) is key, no `OraRoot` matches. When `NSApp.keyWindow` is nil (all browser windows minimised) the post carries no sender and the same rule needs `keyWindow === window`, which is also false everywhere.
kept.user_impact: One of the owner's reported symptoms: ⌘T sometimes does nothing. Standing in the Passwords window, or with the browser windows minimised, ⌘T silently disappears instead of opening a tab in the frontmost browser window, which is what every other macOS browser does.
kept.fix: One call does both the addressing and the activation: `NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .showLauncher, object: (NSApp.delegate as? AppDelegate)?.getWindow())`. getWindow() (OraApp.swift:96) already picks the front browser window, deminiaturises it and makes it key, and creates one if none exists; AppDelegate.browserWindow(in:) alone would target a minimised window that never comes forward.
kept.verify_reason: The scope arithmetic checks out. With the Passwords window key, .showLauncher carries it as sender; .windowOrKey resolves target = window (non-nil in every mounted OraRoot) and sender !== target, so no root claims it. With NSApp.keyWindow nil the post has no sender and the nil branch needs keyWindow === target, also false. Same for New Window is not true (it uses openWindow), so the finding applies to New Tab and to every other keyWindow-addressed row. I am dropping the auditor's attribution to the owner's ⌘T complaint, which is unproven; the code path itself is verified.

kept.title: Assigning a chord that is already taken is accepted with no warning
kept.evidence: `setCustomShortcut(for:event:)` stores whatever chord it is handed. Nothing checks `allShortcuts` for an existing owner, and `ShortcutRowView` has no state for a conflict. The invariant is only enforced for defaults, by `KeyboardShortcutTableTests.defaultChordsAreUnique` (auraTests/KeyboardPolishTests.swift:110), whose own comment says two commands on one chord means AppKit picks by menu order.
kept.user_impact: Binding Close Tab to ⌘T leaves two ⌘T menu items; one of them silently stops working and nothing in the UI says which or why. The user's mental model is that the last binding wins, and it does not.
kept.fix: Do not silently clear the other command's binding, that trades one invisible surprise for another. Reject instead: in handleKeyCapture, `if let taken = KeyboardShortcuts.allShortcuts.first(where: { $0.id != editingShortcut.id && $0.currentChord == chord })`, keep editingShortcut set, store the conflict in a @State and pass it into ShortcutRowView so the chip reads "Used by \(taken.name)" until the next key press. The row already takes a displayText override for exactly this kind of message.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: setCustomShortcut (CustomKeyboardShortcutManager.swift:36) stores unconditionally, handleKeyCapture does no lookup, and the uniqueness invariant is only asserted for defaults in tests (auraTests/KeyboardPolishTests.swift:110-121). Two menu items on one chord means AppKit picks by menu order, exactly what that test's comment says nobody should have to reason about.

kept.title: ⌃⇧⇥ opens the switcher on the next tab instead of the previous one
kept.evidence: The registered handler is `guard event.keyCode == 48, event.modifierFlags.contains(.control)` and then unconditionally shows the switcher; it never looks at `.shift`. `FloatingTabSwitcher.onAppear` and its `onChange` both set `focusedTab = recentTabs[recentTabs.count == 1 ? 0 : 1].id` (lines 38-41 and 47-53), i.e. always the next tab. Only the second and later presses reach `keyboardHandler`, which does honour shift (line 183).
kept.user_impact: Holding ⌃⇧ and tapping Tab once lands on the same tab as plain ⌃⇥ instead of walking backwards, so back-cycling through recents needs an extra press every time.
kept.fix: Correct in shape; note the state lives on AppState, which is declared in OraRoot.swift:32 as @State private var appState = AppState() — check where AppState is defined before listing OraApp.swift as a file to touch. Alternatively avoid new state entirely: have the raise handler set focus by posting nothing and let the switcher read keyModifierListener.modifierFlags.contains(.shift) in onAppear, since it already observes that object.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: the raise handler (OraRoot.swift:279-283) tests only keyCode 48 and .control, and both seeding sites in the switcher (FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:38-41 and 47-53) hardcode index 1, so the first ⌃⇧⇥ press selects the next tab. Only the second and later presses reach keyboardHandler (line 181-189), which does honour shift. Net: ⌃⇧⇥ does the opposite of what macOS convention promises on the first press.

kept.title: Context menus print hardcoded chords that go stale after a rebind
kept.evidence: Back/Forward/Reload/Reader/View Source/Save Page As pass literal strings ("⌘[", "⌘]", "⌘R", "⌥⌘R", "⌥⌘U", "⇧⌘S"), and the "..." menu's Show All History passes "⌘Y" (aura/Features/Browser/URLBar/URLBarMenuButton.swift:163). `AuraMenuItem.item(_:icon:shortcut:…)` already has an overload taking a `KeyboardShortcutDefinition` that reads `currentChord.display` (aura/Shared/Components/Menu/AuraMenuItem.swift:72), which the rest of both menus use.
kept.user_impact: After rebinding Reload or Back, the right-click menu keeps advertising the old key. Small, but it is exactly the kind of drift a demanding user spots.
kept.fix: Back/Forward/Reload/Show All History swap to the definition overload. Reader, View Source and Save Page As have no catalogue entry and their menu chords are hardcoded in OraCommands (lines 177, 188, 193); adding catalogue entries for them is the same edit finding 16 needs, so do both at once rather than dropping the hints.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PageContextMenu.swift:33-38 pass "⌘[", "⌘]", "⌘R"; :111, :117, :123 pass "⌥⌘R", "⌥⌘U", "⇧⌘S"; URLBarMenuButton.swift:163 passes "⌘Y". The definition-taking overload exists (AuraMenuItem.swift:71-87) and reads currentChord.display, and the rest of both menus use it.

kept.title: Paste is always enabled in the page context menu, even with an empty clipboard
kept.evidence: Cut and Copy carry `isDisabled: !info.hasSelection`, but Paste and Select All carry no state at all, so Paste is live in an editable field with nothing on the pasteboard.
kept.user_impact: Right-clicking a text field with an empty clipboard offers Paste, and it does nothing. WebKit's own menu greys it out.
kept.fix: Use an emptiness test rather than a string-class test: `isDisabled: NSPasteboard.general.pasteboardItems?.isEmpty ?? true`. canReadObject(forClasses: [NSString.self]) would grey Paste out for an image-only clipboard, which WebKit can paste into a rich editable field.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PageContextMenu.swift:97-99 gives Paste no isDisabled while the Cut and Copy rows above it carry !info.hasSelection. The menu is rebuilt per right-click, so a pasteboard read at build time is accurate.

kept.title: The Help menu is SwiftUI's default and the app ships no help book
kept.evidence: No `CommandGroup(replacing: .help)` anywhere in the app (the only command groups are appInfo, appSettings, newItem, saveItem, sidebar, undoRedo), and aura/Info/Info.plist has no `CFBundleHelpBookName` key. The "..." menu instead sends Help to https://github.com/Sowyu/Aura (aura/Features/Browser/URLBar/URLBarMenuButton.swift:153).
kept.user_impact: Help > Aura Help puts up the system "help isn't available" sheet, which reads as an unfinished app, and it disagrees with the Help row in the app's own menu.
kept.fix: Post .openURL with `object: (NSApp.delegate as? AppDelegate)?.getWindow()` rather than NSApp.keyWindow, for the same reason as finding 9: with a utility window key the post is dropped. Better still, call the same openInNewTab path the "..." row uses so both entry points share one URL constant instead of repeating the literal.
kept.verify_reason: Verified: no CommandGroup(replacing: .help) anywhere in aura/, and no CFBundleHelpBookName in any plist, so the auto-generated Help menu's item hits the missing-help-book sheet. The "..." menu sends Help to the GitHub page (URLBarMenuButton.swift:154-158).

kept.title: The tab switcher advances on any Control-key press, not just Tab
kept.evidence: `keyboardHandler` checks only the modifiers: `if event.modifierFlags.contains([.control, .shift]) { focusPreviousTab() } else if event.modifierFlags.contains(.control) { focusNextTab() }`. The key code is never examined, unlike the handler that raises the switcher (aura/App/OraRoot.swift:281), which does check `keyCode == 48`.
kept.user_impact: With the switcher up, ⌃A, ⌃E or any other Control chord walks the selection, so an accidental Control combination moves the highlight and releasing Control then activates the wrong tab.
kept.fix: Add the same key test the raising handler uses: `guard event.keyCode == 48 else { return }` at the top of the closure.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:181-189 branches on modifierFlags alone and never reads keyCode, so any Control chord typed while the switcher is up walks the selection and the eventual Control release activates whatever it landed on.

kept.title: An extension can claim a menu chord that is not in the shortcut catalogue
kept.evidence: `collidesWithBuiltIn` compares against `KeyboardShortcuts.allShortcuts` only. Seven live menu chords are hardcoded in OraCommands and never appear there: ⇧⌘S (line 177), ⌥⌘R (188), ⌥⌘U (193), ⌥⇧⌘R (222), ⌘, (336), ⌘W on Close Window (57), plus ⌘B for Compact Mode whose definition is absent from `allShortcuts`.
kept.user_impact: An add-on suggesting ⌥⌘R takes Reader away, and `performCommand` (aura/Features/Extensions/Services/ExtensionManager+Commands.swift:98) consumes the event before the menu ever sees it, so the browser's own item stops responding with no way to tell why.
kept.fix: Adding Window.toggleCompactMode to allShortcuts also puts it in Settings > Shortcuts, which is a fix in itself, but it must land with finding 4: today a rebind of it would not reach the menu bar. Sequence: 4, then 6, then 16, so the catalogue means "every chord Aura owns" and defaultChordsAreUnique covers the newly added entries.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: collidesWithBuiltIn (ExtensionCommands.swift:92-94) checks allShortcuts only, and performCommand's monitor (ExtensionManager+Commands.swift:96-107) consumes the event before the menu bar sees it. Window.toggleCompactMode (⌘B, KeyboardShortcuts.swift:167-172) really is absent from allShortcuts despite being bound at OraCommands.swift:125, so an extension can take ⌘B; the same holds for ⇧⌘S, ⌥⌘R, ⌥⌘U, ⌥⇧⌘R and ⌘,. The ⌘W-on-Close-Window example is moot once finding 1 deletes that item.

kept.title: Sidebar, compact, find and panel commands fire in every open window at once
kept.evidence: BrowserView is mounted once per window (OraRoot.swift:41 holds a per-window `@State private var sidebarManager = SidebarManager()`), and lines 215-238 subscribe with plain `.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for:))` for .findNext, .findPrevious, .toggleSidebar, .toggleSidebarPosition, .toggleCompactMode, .showHistoryPanel and .showDownloadsPanel. None of them checks the notification's object, unlike every row in OraRoot's `events` table, which goes through WindowEventScope.accepts (OraRoot.swift:317-333). Two of the posters do not even address a window: OraCommands.swift:110 and :131 post .toggleSidebar and .toggleSidebarPosition with `object: nil`.
kept.user_impact: With two browser windows open, ⌘S toggles the sidebar in both, ⌘B flips compact mode in both, ⌘G steps the find match in the background window's tab too, and ⌘Y opens the history panel in every window. The background window's layout changes behind the user's back and has to be put back by hand.
kept.fix: Route these through the same table the rest of the window events use: move the seven rows into OraRoot's `events` array as `WindowEvent(.toggleSidebar, .windowOrKey) { ... }` style entries calling into sidebarManager/toolbarManager, which OraRoot already holds, and delete the onReceive modifiers. If that is too large for one pass, the smaller version is to keep the onReceive calls and guard each body with the same test: `guard WindowEventScope.windowOrKey.accepts(note, window: window) else { return }`, which needs BrowserView to read the window it is in.

kept.title: "New Tab" means two different things depending on which menu you open it from
kept.evidence: The File menu's New Tab posts .showLauncher (OraCommands.swift:25-27), which opens the launcher panel over the current page (OraRoot.swift:369-380). The "..." menu's New Tab row (URLBarMenuButton.swift:68-70) and the command palette's New Tab row (AppCommand.swift:55) post .newTab, whose handler calls tabManager.openHomeTab (OraRoot.swift:383-391). All three carry the same name and the same advertised chord, KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.new.
kept.user_impact: Clicking New Tab in the "..." menu lands on the home page with no caret in a field; pressing the ⌘T that the same row advertises opens a launcher instead. The user cannot predict which one they get, which is the same class of confusion as the reported "⌘T opens but typing goes nowhere".
kept.fix: Pick one meaning for the name. Post .showLauncher from all three, and if a plain home tab is still wanted, give it its own row and name ("New Home Tab") with no chord. The .newTab notification then has one caller, the sidebar's plus button, or none.

kept.title: Rebinding Next/Previous Tab leaves the real ⌃⇥ handler on the old chord
kept.evidence: The handler that actually raises the switcher hardcodes `event.keyCode == 48, event.modifierFlags.contains(.control)` (OraRoot.swift:279-283), and the commit path keys off Control being released (FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:241). Neither reads KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.next/.previous, which Settings > Shortcuts offers as bindable (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:25-36, listed at :376).
kept.user_impact: Rebinding Next Tab to, say, ⌥⇥ leaves ⌃⇥ still opening the switcher, and the new chord only reaches the menu item, whose handler does not switch tabs at all (finding 5). The setting reads as applied and nothing behaves as promised.
kept.fix: After finding 5 gives the menu items a real action, make the raise handler read the catalogue instead of a literal keycode: compare KeyChord(fromEvent: event) against KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.next.currentChord and .previous.currentChord, and keep the Control-release commit only while the bound chord actually contains Control (otherwise commit on the next Return/Escape). If that is more than this pass is worth, remove tabs.next and tabs.previous from the Settings catalogue the way finding 6 removes the other unbindable rows, so nothing advertises a rebind that cannot work.

kept.title: The recording chip never says it is listening, and VoiceOver reads it as glyphs
kept.evidence: While isEditing the chip keeps showing the old chord and only changes fill and stroke colour (ShortcutRowView, lines 139-158). There is no accessibilityLabel and no .help anywhere on the row, so the button's label reaches VoiceOver as the raw glyph string ("⌘T"), and the accent tint is the only cue that a key press is being captured. The neighbouring "Reset to Default" is a stock SwiftUI Button with default AppKit chrome, the one un-styled control on an otherwise custom settings page.
kept.user_impact: A user who cannot see the accent tint, or who simply looks away, has no idea the row is armed, which is how a stray key ends up bound (findings 2 and 3). VoiceOver announces symbol characters rather than "Command T".
kept.fix: Show `Text(isEditing ? "Press a shortcut" : (displayText ?? item.display))` in the chip and add `.accessibilityLabel(Text(isEditing ? "Recording shortcut for \(item.name)" : "\(item.name) shortcut, \(item.currentChord.display)"))`. Give the reset button the same .buttonStyle(.plain) treatment the chip uses so the row reads as one designed control.

engine.summary: The engine layer is unusually well built for a hobby browser: the navigation, download, popup-adoption and crash-recovery paths are all thought through, commented with real measurements, and covered by tests. What is missing is the last mile of "acts like a browser" behaviour — non-web schemes (mailto:, tel:, app links) fall into the error page, HTTP basic auth is silently refused, geolocation never reaches Aura's own permission prompt, and the most common TLS failure (expired certificate) lands on a generic "Something Went Wrong" with no way through. The rest is presentation debt: JavaScript dialogs are raw NSAlerts titled "Alert"/"Confirm"/"Prompt" (the prompt one opens with no caret in its field), the error page mixes stock AppKit buttons into custom chrome, and the paint probe hangs two ordinary NSWindows on screen that a tiling window manager treats as real windows.

kept.title: mailto:, tel: and app-scheme links show the error page instead of opening the app
kept.evidence: `decidePolicyFor navigationAction` builds a `BrowserNavigationAction` and passes every scheme straight to `decisionHandler(.allow, preferences)`. Nothing in the app calls `NSWorkspace.shared.open` for a navigation: grep over aura/ shows only Settings, the file tray and Downloads use it. `Tab.navigate(to:)` (Tab.swift:412) also just calls `page.load(URLRequest(url: target))`. WebKit cannot load `mailto:`/`tel:`/`zoommtg:`, so the load fails and `didFailProvisionalNavigation` hands it to `tab.setNavigationError`, which paints StatusPageView over the page the user was reading.
kept.user_impact: Clicking a mailto link on any contact page, or a Zoom/Slack/Teams/App Store link, replaces the page with "Something Went Wrong" instead of opening the right app. Going back is the only recovery.
kept.fix: Same shape, but the allow-list must also contain "javascript" (javascript:void(0) links are everywhere and must never be handed to NSWorkspace) and "blob"/"data"/"about" as listed. Keep the gate on navigationType == .linkActivated || .formSubmitted, and place the check after applyJavaScriptPolicy but before the shouldPerformDownload branch. Note the same rule is needed in createWebViewWith (BrowserPage.swift:745-765), where a target=_blank mailto link arrives instead: there, cancel by returning nil after opening the URL.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. BrowserPage.swift:448-497 passes every scheme to decisionHandler(.allow); the only delegate implementation (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:85-122) routes by mouse button/modifiers and rule space, never by scheme; grep over aura/ shows NSWorkspace.shared.open only in Settings, OpenedFileRow, DownloadDestination and DownloadManager. Nothing converts an external scheme into an app launch, and didFailProvisionalNavigation (BrowserPage.swift:578-599) only swallows NSURLErrorCancelled, so the unsupported-URL failure reaches StatusPageView.

kept.title: Paint probe hangs two plain NSWindows on screen, which tiling window managers adopt and re-tile
kept.evidence: `hostWindow(for:slot:)` builds `NSWindow(contentRect:styleMask:[.borderless]...)`, sets `.floating`, `[.canJoinAllSpaces, .stationary, .ignoresCycle, .transient]` and calls `orderFrontRegardless()`. It is still an ordinary NSWindow with the default accessibility subrole and it is not a panel, so a third-party tiler (yabai, Amethyst, Loop) sees two new windows appear about a second after the first page load and re-lays out the space around them. `probe()` retries once on `.inconclusive` (AuraWebBundle.swift:179), so this can happen twice per launch.
kept.user_impact: Opening the first web page of a session shoves the browser window off screen on any Mac running a window manager. The two grey dots also live at the screen corners for 2 to 4 seconds every launch.
kept.fix: NSPanel with [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel] plus isFloatingPanel = true and isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true is the right change; a panel already reports an AXFloatingWindow subrole, so setAccessibilitySubrole(.unknown) is belt and braces rather than the mechanism, and .auxiliary should be dropped (it belongs to the full-screen behaviour group and buys nothing here) while .fullScreenAuxiliary is worth keeping. Do not change the frame maths: screenSample(of:) reads the window by windowNumber and needs the one point on screen, and the slot 0/slot 1 corners keep the two windows from occluding each other.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:315-338: plain NSWindow, borderless, level .floating, orderFrontRegardless, two of them (slot 0 and slot 1), and AuraWebBundle.probe (AuraWebBundle.swift:168-188) can run PaintProbe.run twice. It is gated on AuraWebBundle.isEnabled, i.e. the opt-in extensionRequestBlocking setting, which the owner has on, and it is kicked off from WebRequestBroker.prepare() at launch.

kept.title: Middle-click opens the wrong link: the hit point is not converted out of AppKit's flipped coordinates or divided by page zoom
kept.evidence: `handleMiddleClick` does `let locationInContentView = contentView.convert(location, from: nil)` and injects `document.elementFromPoint(\(locationInContentView.x), \(locationInContentView.y))`. `WKWebView` does not override `isFlipped` (the three views in this codebase that need top-left origins do so explicitly: TabDropZoneView.swift:18, TabDragSourceView.swift:140, AuraContextMenu.swift:99), so y is measured from the bottom while `elementFromPoint` expects CSS viewport coordinates from the top. `page.zoom` (`webView.pageZoom`) is not divided out either, so on a zoomed site the point is off by that factor as well.
kept.user_impact: Middle-clicking a link opens whatever link happens to sit at the mirrored position — usually nothing, sometimes a completely different link. It is silently wrong rather than obviously broken, which is worse.
kept.fix: Fix stands. Keep the existing isFinite/non-negative guard on the pre-conversion point, since bounds.height - y can legitimately be small, and interpolate the converted values.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. contentView is page.contentView, which is the WKWebView itself (BrowserPage.swift:200-202); WKWebView does not override isFlipped, so convert(_:from: nil) yields a bottom-left origin while elementFromPoint wants top-left CSS coordinates, and page.zoom (webView.pageZoom, BrowserPage.swift:248-251) is never divided out. Severity lowered to medium: it is wrong every time, but only on middle-click, and the usual outcome is that no link is found and nothing happens rather than data loss.

kept.title: An expired certificate lands on "Something Went Wrong" with no way to continue
kept.evidence: `errorType` maps only `NSURLErrorServerCertificateUntrusted`, `NSURLErrorClientCertificateRequired` and `NSURLErrorSecureConnectionFailed` to `.security`. `NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasBadDate` (-1201), `NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasUnknownRoot` (-1203) and `NSURLErrorServerCertificateNotYetValid` (-1204) fall into `default: return .unknown`, and the "Continue Anyway" button is gated on `errorType == .security` (line 63), so `Tab.continueToInsecureSite()` is unreachable for them.
kept.user_impact: The most common TLS failure there is — an expired certificate on an internal tool or a lapsed site — shows a generic "An unexpected error occurred" with Try Again and Go Back, and no way through. Safari and Chrome both offer to proceed.
kept.fix: Add the three codes to the `.security` case in `errorType`: `case NSURLErrorServerCertificateUntrusted, NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasBadDate, NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasUnknownRoot, NSURLErrorServerCertificateNotYetValid, NSURLErrorClientCertificateRequired, NSURLErrorSecureConnectionFailed:`. Nothing else changes: `bypassSSL(for:)` already keys off the host.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at StatusPageView.swift:126-142: only -1202, -1206 and -1200 map to .security, and the Continue Anyway button is gated on errorType == .security (line 63). Tab.continueToInsecureSite/BrowserPage.bypassSSL key off the host only, so widening the mapping needs nothing else.

kept.title: HTTP basic auth is refused, so password-protected sites can never be reached
kept.evidence: `webView(_:didReceive challenge:completionHandler:)` handles only `NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust` for bypassed hosts; everything else, basic/digest/NTLM included, takes `completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)`. WKWebView presents no credential panel of its own, so the challenge is answered without credentials and the site returns its 401 body.
kept.user_impact: A router page, a staging site behind htpasswd or an internal tool with basic auth cannot be logged into at all — the tab shows the raw 401 and there is no prompt.
kept.fix: Keep the new delegate method, but two constraints: the completion handler must be called exactly once on every path (WebKit hangs the load otherwise), and anything that is not basic/digest/NTLM must still fall through to .performDefaultHandling. Present through the existing present(_:on:respond:) sheet (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:404-418) rather than DialogManager, for the reason in engine-8, and set alert.window.initialFirstResponder to the user field (same defect as engine-6).
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at BrowserPage.swift:602-614: only NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust for bypassed hosts is handled, everything else takes performDefaultHandling, and WKWebView presents no credential UI of its own.

kept.title: JavaScript prompt() opens with the caret in no field, so typing goes nowhere
kept.evidence: `runJavaScriptPrompt` builds `let textField = NSTextField(...)`, assigns `alert.accessoryView = textField` and sheets the alert. Nothing sets `alert.window.initialFirstResponder`, and AppKit gives key focus to the default button, not to an accessory view.
kept.user_impact: Exactly the launcher complaint, in a second place: the dialog appears, the user types, nothing lands, and they have to click the field first.
kept.fix: Just `alert.window.initialFirstResponder = textField` before present(...), plus `textField.selectText(nil)` so a default value comes up selected. Drop the placeholderString sentence in the proposed fix, it is noise.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:438-458: the accessory NSTextField is installed and the alert is sheeted with no initialFirstResponder set. The one-line fix is harmless even in the cases where AppKit would have focused the field anyway.

kept.title: Geolocation requests never reach Aura's permission prompt, and the comment says the hook does not exist
kept.evidence: `BrowserPermissionKind`'s doc says "geolocation and web notifications have no public hook, so a page asking for those is answered by WebKit itself", and only `requestMediaCapturePermissionFor` is implemented in BrowserPage.swift:679. `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:requestGeolocationPermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:decisionHandler:)` has been public since macOS 12. Meanwhile `SitePermissionKind` (SettingsTypes.swift:12) already stores `.location`, and `SitePermissionKind.promptable` (line 18) is itself never read anywhere in the app.
kept.user_impact: A map or weather site gets WebKit's own unstyled prompt, and the answer is never remembered, never listed in Settings and never revocable from Aura, unlike camera and microphone.
kept.fix: Correct the two comments to say the hook landed in macOS 27, and implement the method behind @available(macOS 27.0, *) with the real Swift name webView(_:requestGeolocationPermissionForOrigin:initiatedByFrame:decisionHandler:), mapping to a new BrowserPermissionKind.location whose siteKinds is [.location]. Delete promptable rather than extending it: nothing reads it.
kept.verify_reason: Partly refuted. The delegate method does exist, but the SDK header (WKUIDelegate.h:302) marks webView(_:requestGeolocationPermissionForOrigin:initiatedByFrame:decisionHandler:) API_AVAILABLE(macos(27.0)), not macOS 12, and the project's MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET is 15.0, so implementing it changes nothing for users below macOS 27. What is verified today is the stale narrative comment (BrowserEngineTypes.swift:33-35, SettingsTypes.swift:3-8) and the unread SitePermissionKind.promptable (only hit is its own declaration). Downgraded to low.

kept.title: JavaScript dialogs are stock NSAlerts titled "Alert"/"Confirm"/"Prompt" and never name the site
kept.evidence: `alert.messageText = "Alert"` / `"Confirm"` / `"Prompt"` with the page's string as `informativeText`, presented as a system sheet. The app has its own dialog stack for exactly this shape — `DialogManager.confirm(title:message:icon:confirmLabel:...)` and `DownloadCollisionDialog`, which DownloadManager reaches through its `dialogManager` weak reference (DownloadManager.swift:32).
kept.user_impact: A page-driven modal breaks out of the custom chrome into a stock macOS alert, and a header reading "Alert" tells the user nothing about which site is talking to them — the classic setup for a page that fakes a system message.
kept.fix: Do not route JS dialogs through DialogManager. DialogManager.dismissAll() (DialogManager.swift:35-39) removes dialogs without firing onDismiss, so a dialog torn down that way would never call WebKit's completion handler and would park the web process forever; there is also no text-field dialog for prompt(). Take the minimum instead: set alert.messageText = page.currentURL?.host ?? "This page" in all three methods and move the page's own string to informativeText as it already is. Only aura/Features/Tabs/Browser/TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift is touched.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:420-437: messageText is the literal "Alert"/"Confirm"/"Prompt" and the origin never appears. DialogManager.confirm does exist (DialogManager.swift:49-86).

kept.title: The error page mixes stock AppKit buttons into the custom chrome
kept.evidence: `Button("Try Again").buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large)` and `Button("Go Back").buttonStyle(.bordered)`, while the "Continue Anyway" button eight lines below already uses `OraButton(label:variant:size:action:)`. The failed URL is also rendered as plain unselectable monospaced text.
kept.user_impact: The one full-screen surface a user sees when something goes wrong is the least Aura-looking screen in the app: two blue-and-grey system buttons above a custom ghost button.
kept.fix: Swap both for `OraButton(label: "Try Again", variant: .default, size: .md, action: onRetry)` and `OraButton(label: "Go Back", variant: .secondary, size: .md, action: goBack)`, and add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the failed-URL `Text` so the address can be copied. Also drop the `// Error icon` / `// Error title` comments while touching the file.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at StatusPageView.swift:45-60: .borderedProminent and .bordered system buttons sit directly above an OraButton at line 63, and the failed URL Text (line 38) has no textSelection. OraButton's memberwise init takes label/variant/size/action in that order, so the proposed call sites compile.

kept.title: A failed download says only "Failed" — the stored reason is never shown anywhere
kept.evidence: `statusText` returns the bare string `"Failed"`. `Download.error` is written by `markFailed` on three paths with distinct causes (`"Stalled"`, `"Interrupted by quit"`, and `error.localizedDescription` from WebKit) and cleared in `adopt`, but grep over aura/Features/Downloads shows no read of it outside those writes. The failure toast is equally bare: `toastManager?.show("Download failed \(download.fileName)", type: .error)`.
kept.user_impact: A download that stopped because the app was quit looks the same as one the server refused, so the user cannot tell whether Resume is worth trying.
kept.fix: `case .failed: return download.error.map { "Failed \u{00B7} \($0)" } ?? "Failed"` in `statusText`, and pass the reason into the toast in `DownloadManager.failDownload`: `toastManager?.show("\(download.fileName) failed: \(error)", type: .error)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. DownloadHistoryRow.swift:275 returns the bare "Failed"; Download.error is written by markFailed (Download.swift:73) from DownloadManager.swift:90 and :166 and cleared at :632, and grep shows no read of download.error anywhere in the UI. The toast at DownloadManager.swift:174 is equally bare.

kept.title: Find bar's icon-only buttons have no accessibility labels
kept.evidence: `stepButton(icon:forward:)` and `closeButton` wrap bare `Image(systemName:)` in a `Button` with no `.accessibilityLabel` and no `.help`. VoiceOver reads them as "chevron.up", "chevron.down", "xmark". The media player card next door does set `.help("Go to playing tab")` on its favicon button, so the pattern exists in the codebase.
kept.user_impact: The find bar is unusable with VoiceOver and gives no tooltip on hover, unlike the rest of the chrome.
kept.fix: Add the labels and help strings, but drop the .accessibilityHidden suggestion for the counter: matchCounter renders an empty string when there is nothing to say, and an empty Text announces nothing already.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at FindView.swift:117-137: stepButton and closeButton wrap a bare Image(systemName:) with no accessibilityLabel and no help, while the media card at GlobalMediaPlayer.swift:109 does set .help.

kept.title: The only print() left in the app sits on the rule-list compile failure path
kept.evidence: `print("Failed to compile privacy rule list \(identifier): \(error.localizedDescription)")`. Grep for `^\s*print(` over aura/ returns this one hit; every other error path uses `AuraLog.category(...)` (DownloadManager.swift:352) or `os.Logger` (AuraWebBundle.swift:21).
kept.user_impact: Nothing reaches the log when tracker or cookie blocking silently fails to compile, so a space that is not blocking anything is undiagnosable from a user's log bundle.
kept.fix: Replace with a category logger matching the file's neighbours: add `private static let log = AuraLog.category("Privacy")` and `Self.log.error("Compiling \(identifier, privacy: .public) failed: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: BrowserPrivacyService.swift:578 is the only print( in aura/ and AuraLog.category exists (AuraLog.swift:12-14). Downgraded to low: it is invisible to users and only costs a line in a log bundle.

kept.title: PlayerIconButtonStyle is dead code with hardcoded colours and an off-scale radius
kept.evidence: Grep for `PlayerIconButtonStyle` over the repo returns only its own declaration. `GlobalMediaPlayer` uses `.buttonStyle(.interactive(cornerRadius: AuraRadius.button))` throughout. The dead style hardcodes `Color.white.opacity(...)` (ignores the theme) and `cornerRadius: 8`, which is on neither rung of the AuraRadius scale.
kept.user_impact: None directly — it is a trap for the next person, who will find a player-specific button style and use it, breaking the theme and the radius scale.
kept.fix: Delete the file and its Xcode project reference.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: grep over the whole repo returns only the declaration, and the project.pbxproj has no PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup, so the file reference at project.pbxproj:300/1022/2171/2958 really does have to be removed by hand. Downgraded to low: zero user impact.

kept.title: MediaController's "removed" case removes the session twice and keeps a commented-out case
kept.evidence: Lines 98-99 are `//        case "ready":` with a comment under it. The `"removed"` case removes the session by index and then calls `self.removeSession(for: tab.id)`, which searches for and removes the same session again, clears `isPlayingMedia` a second time and re-runs `updateTitleSyncTimer()`. Three `// Update tab's isPlayingMedia property` comments restate the line under them.
kept.user_impact: None visible; it is the kind of duplication that hides a real ordering bug the next time someone edits the case.
kept.fix: Delete the commented-out `case "ready"`, replace the body of `case "removed"` with the single call `removeSession(for: id)`, and drop the three restating comments.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at MediaController.swift:98-99 (commented-out case "ready") and 118-124, where the session is removed by index and then removeSession(for:) (line 194) removes it again, re-clears isPlayingMedia and re-runs updateTitleSyncTimer. removeSession also clears tabRefs[tabID], which the inline body does not, so collapsing to the single call is strictly better.

kept.title: BrowserNavigationAction.isUserInitiated is never read and its comment does not match what it computes
kept.evidence: The field is documented "True for a link click or a form submission, as opposed to a redirect or a reload", but BrowserPage.swift:468 fills it with `navigationType == .linkActivated || .formSubmitted || .other`, and `.other` is exactly the redirect/programmatic case. Grep shows the only two hits in the repo are the declaration and that assignment: nothing reads it.
kept.user_impact: A future guard written against this field would allow every programmatic navigation through, believing it was a click.
kept.fix: Delete the property and the three lines that compute it. If the external-scheme gate in engine-1 lands, it reads `navigationAction.navigationType == .linkActivated` directly rather than resurrecting this.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: the only two hits for isUserInitiated are the declaration (BrowserEngineTypes.swift:56) and the assignment (BrowserPage.swift:468-470), which includes .other and so contradicts its own doc comment.

kept.title: Every downloads row builds a RelativeDateTimeFormatter on every redraw
kept.evidence: `timeAgo(from:)` does `let formatter = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()` per call, and it is called from `statusText` for every completed row on every body evaluation — which the 10 Hz progress ticks of any in-flight download trigger for the whole list. The codebase already caches this kind of object elsewhere (`TabBrowserPageDelegate.averagingContext`, TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:576).
kept.user_impact: A downloads panel with 50 rows open while something is downloading allocates and configures 50 formatters ten times a second.
kept.fix: Hoist it: `private static let relativeFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = { let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter(); f.unitsStyle = .abbreviated; return f }()` and use `Self.relativeFormatter.localizedString(for:relativeTo:)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at DownloadHistoryRow.swift:285-289: a RelativeDateTimeFormatter is built per call. The 10 Hz timer at DownloadManager.swift:706 is real, but with @Observable per-download tracking only rows whose properties changed re-render, so the "50 formatters ten times a second" figure is overstated; the hoist is still the right one-line change.

kept.title: Closing the find bar wipes the user's own text selection
kept.evidence: `clear()` evaluates `window.getSelection().removeAllRanges()`, and `FindManager.close(_:)` calls it on every Escape or close click. The comment above it explains the highlight is the document selection, but the same call also drops a selection the user made by hand before opening the bar.
kept.user_impact: Select a paragraph, open find to check a word, press Escape — the paragraph is deselected and has to be re-selected.
kept.fix: Guard in close(_:) on the session: `guard let page = tab.browserPage, !session(for: tab.id).query.isEmpty else { return }`. Only FindManager.swift changes; FindController needs no new state.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: FindManager.close(_:) (FindManager.swift:60-63) calls FindController.clear() unconditionally, and clear() (FindController.swift:46-48) removes all selection ranges, including one the user made by hand before opening the bar.

kept.title: Media player transport buttons have no accessibility labels or tooltips
kept.evidence: The previous/play-pause/next buttons (lines 112-127) and the close button (line 86) wrap controlGlyph/Image(systemName:) with no .accessibilityLabel and no .help. Only the favicon button gets .help("Go to playing tab") at line 109, so the pattern is present and simply not applied to the controls that matter. VoiceOver announces "backward fill", "play fill", "forward fill", "xmark".
kept.user_impact: The global media player cannot be operated by VoiceOver, and hovering the transport controls shows no tooltip while the favicon next to them does.
kept.fix: Add `.accessibilityLabel("Previous track")` / `"Play"`-`"Pause"` (driven by session.isPlaying) / `"Next track"` on the three transport buttons and `.accessibilityLabel("Stop controlling this tab")` on the close button, each with a matching `.help(...)` so hover matches the favicon button already there.

kept.title: Save page and save screenshot fail silently after the user has picked a destination
kept.evidence: saveWebArchive (lines 70-83) does `guard case let .success(data) = result else { return }` and then `try? data.write(to: destination)`; saveFullPageScreenshot (lines 223-234) returns silently when captureFullPageImage or pngData yields nil, so the save panel never even appears, and its write is `try?` as well. No toast, no log: DownloadManager has toastManager for exactly this kind of report (DownloadManager.swift:161, :174).
kept.user_impact: Choose Save Page As, pick a folder, click Save, and on a failure nothing is written and nothing says so; the user believes the file exists. Save Screenshot on a page WebKit cannot snapshot does nothing at all, with no panel and no message.
kept.fix: Route both failures to the toast the app already uses: hand BrowserPage's delegate a failure message (or reuse the tab's downloadManager?.toastManager) and show "Could not save <name>" when the archive/snapshot result is not .success or the write throws. Replace `try?` with do/catch so the thrown error is what gets reported.

kept.title: View source's Copy Source is a stock AppKit push button inside the custom chrome
kept.evidence: `Button("Copy Source") { ClipboardUtils.copyToClipboard(markup) }.controlSize(.small)` carries no buttonStyle, so it renders as a system bordered push button in a pane whose header, rows and background are all custom. Nothing confirms the copy either. Same defect class as StatusPageView (engine-9), and OraButton with size .sm is what the rest of the app uses.
kept.user_impact: The one control on the view-source pane looks like it belongs to a different application, and clicking it gives no sign that anything was copied.
kept.fix: Replace with `OraButton(label: "Copy Source", variant: .secondary, size: .sm) { ClipboardUtils.copyToClipboard(markup) }` and flip the label to "Copied" for about a second with the existing AnimationSettings.easeOut helper so the click has a visible result.

a11y-keyboard.summary: The custom menu stack is the strongest part of this area: AuraMenuHost handles arrow keys, Return, Escape, left/right submenu traversal and type-ahead, and AuraMenuPanel labels every row and wires an accessibilityAction, so the pattern the rest of the app should copy already exists in the repo. Everything built out of tap gestures instead of Buttons missed it, though: launcher suggestion rows, emoji and icon tiles, the colour picker, the custom traffic lights and the toast close button all reach VoiceOver as unnamed fragments, and the sidebar rows put their labels on containers that are not accessibility elements. The two defects that hit users who never open VoiceOver are reduce motion ignoring the system Accessibility setting (Aura's own toggle is the only switch, defaulting to off) and theme.mutedForeground not following the glass chrome's forced foreground, which drops secondary sidebar text to near-zero contrast under a dark tint.

kept.title: Launcher suggestion rows are invisible to VoiceOver and have no activation
kept.evidence: The row body is a plain `HStack` ending in `.onTapGesture { suggestion.action() ... }` and `.onHover { ... focusedElement = suggestion.id }` (lines 156-167). There is no `accessibilityElement`, no `accessibilityLabel`, no `.isButton`/`.isSelected` trait and no `accessibilityAction`. The keyboard highlight is a private `focusedElement: UUID` compared at line 43 (`focusedElement == suggestion.id`), which is drawn as a background fill only (line 50-53) and never reported to accessibility. `LauncherSuggestionsView` (lines 11-24) is a bare `VStack` with no container semantics either, and `LauncherMain` passes no `accessibilityValue` to the field, so arrowing through results announces nothing.
kept.user_impact: A VoiceOver user pressing ⌘T can type into the field but never hears the results, cannot tell which row the arrow keys landed on, and cannot activate a row: the launcher is the app's main way to open anything.
kept.fix: As proposed, but also mirror the keyboard highlight so arrowing is announced: put `.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)`, `.accessibilityLabel(...)`, `.accessibilityAddTraits(isFocused ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)`, `.accessibilityAction { suggestion.action() }` on the row, and add `.accessibilitySortPriority` nothing else. Reuse the existing `shouldShowURL`/`suggestion.url` values already computed rather than re-deriving the host, and fold `actionLabel`'s wording ("Switch to tab", "Ask X") into the label so the row's action is spoken too.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:122-168: the row body is HStack -> .onTapGesture -> .onHover with zero accessibility modifiers, and LauncherSuggestionsView.swift:12-23 is a bare VStack. The field itself does carry a label (LauncherTextField.swift:165,208 setAccessibilityLabel), so the field is fine, but the result rows expose nothing and the keyboard highlight (focusedElement, line 41-43) is never mirrored into a trait, so VoiceOver cannot follow arrow-key movement or activate a row.

kept.title: Reduce motion never follows the system Accessibility setting
kept.evidence: `AnimationSettings` seeds its cache from `UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: SettingsStore.reduceMotionKey)` and `SettingsStore` loads it the same way (`SettingsStore.swift:501`: `reduceMotion = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.reduceMotionKey)`). Nothing in the repo reads `NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion` (grep for `accessibilityReduceMotion|reduceMotion` returns only these two files, the settings toggle and the tests). Every animation in the app does route through `AnimationSettings`, so the one switch controls everything, and it defaults to off.
kept.user_impact: Someone who turned on System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Reduce Motion still gets every sidebar, launcher, toast and menu animation until they find Aura's own toggle. For motion-sensitive users this is the setting that matters and it is silently ignored.
kept.fix: Do not seed SettingsStore.reduceMotion from the system flag: `reduceMotion` has a `didSet` (SettingsStore.swift:386-390) that writes straight back to defaults, so `load()` assigning the system value would persist it and the user could never return to following macOS. Instead OR the two in the one place that reads them: in AnimationSettings use `initialState: UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: SettingsStore.reduceMotionKey) || NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`, make `reduceMotionDidChange(to:)` store `value || NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`, and add one NSWorkspace.shared.notificationCenter observer for `accessibilityDisplayOptionsDidChangeNotification` that calls `AnimationSettings.reduceMotionDidChange(to: SettingsStore.shared.reduceMotion)`. Files stay AnimationSettings.swift plus wherever the observer is installed (AppDelegate/OraRoot), not SettingsStore.load.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: AnimationSettings.swift:7-9 seeds the cache from UserDefaults only, SettingsStore.swift:501 loads it the same way, and a repo-wide grep for reduceMotion/accessibilityDisplay returns only those two files, AccessibilitySettingsView.swift:14 and the tests. Nothing reads NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion or the SwiftUI accessibilityReduceMotion environment key, so the system setting is ignored.

kept.title: Secondary text keeps its own colour on glass chrome, so it can vanish against the tint
kept.evidence: `foreground` honours the chrome override (`forcedForeground ?? ...`, line 70-72) but `mutedForeground` returns a flat `.secondary` (line 111-113), as do `placeholder` and `border`. `GlassChrome` (aura/Core/Styles/AuraGlass.swift:157) injects `theme.withForeground(chromeForeground)` where `chromeForeground` is computed from the blended tint luminance, so on a dark tint in Light appearance `foreground` flips to white while every `theme.mutedForeground` call in the same chrome stays dark grey: `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:44,53,93,97`, `BookmarksBar.swift:87`, `DownloadsWidget.swift:53`, `PinnedTabsList.swift:22`.
kept.user_impact: Turn on Liquid Glass with a dark tint in Light mode (or a pale tint in Dark mode) and the sidebar's address line, the "Pinned" heading and the bookmark labels drop to near-zero contrast while the primary labels stay readable.
kept.fix: Same shape, but apply it to `placeholder` and `border` too, since both are flat semantic colours in the same chrome: `var mutedForeground: Color { forcedForeground?.opacity(0.65) ?? .secondary }`, `var placeholder: Color { forcedForeground?.opacity(0.45) ?? Color(.placeholderTextColor) }`, `border` gets `forcedForeground?.opacity(0.18) ?? <current>`. Leave popover/dialog colours alone: those views are not inside GlassChrome so forcedForeground is nil there and nothing changes.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed mechanically: Theme.foreground (Theme.swift:70-72) honours forcedForeground, mutedForeground (111-113) returns a flat `.secondary`, and GlassChrome (AuraGlass.swift:150-157) injects theme.withForeground(chromeForeground) where chromeForeground flips white/black on the blended tint luminance (AuraGlass.swift:64-66). All the cited muted call sites exist (SidebarURLDisplay.swift:44,53,93,97; BookmarksBar.swift:87; DownloadsWidget.swift:53; PinnedTabsList.swift:22). Downgraded from high: it needs the experimental Liquid Glass toggle plus a tint whose luminance opposes the appearance; with the default accent tint at 0.35 the blended colour stays on the appearance's side and `.secondary` still reads.

kept.title: Custom traffic lights are unlabelled images, not buttons
kept.evidence: `WindowControlButton.body` is `Image(imageName).resizable()...onTapGesture { performAction() }` (lines 64-85). There is no `accessibilityLabel`, no `.isButton` trait, no `accessibilityAction` and no `.help`. `imageName` resolves to asset names such as "close-hover" and "no-focus" (lines 54-57), which is what VoiceOver falls back to reading. This row replaces the native traffic lights whenever the top toolbar is hidden (`SidebarHeader.swift:23`).
kept.user_impact: With the toolbar hidden, VoiceOver users hear "close-normal image" instead of "Close window", and there is no accessible way to close, minimise or zoom the window from the chrome.
kept.fix: Same fix, but the zoom case calls `window.toggleFullScreen(nil)` (WindowControls.swift:96), not zoom, so label it "Toggle Full Screen", not "Zoom window". Use "Close Window"/"Minimize Window" to match the title-case wording the rest of the chrome help strings use ("Toggle Sidebar", "Go Back"). `.accessibilityElement()` is unnecessary on an Image; `.accessibilityLabel` + `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` + `.accessibilityAction(perform: performAction)` + `.help(label)` is enough.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: WindowControlButton (WindowControls.swift:63-85) is a raw Image with .onTapGesture and no label, trait, action or help; imageName resolves to asset names like "close-hover"/"no-focus" (49-52). The file is the only chrome control with zero labels: every other icon button goes through oraShortcutHelp, which sets both .help and .accessibilityLabel (View+Shortcuts.swift:22-26). Used from SidebarHeader.swift:23 and also HistoryPanelView.swift:66, FilesPanelView.swift:37, DownloadsHistoryView.swift:38.

kept.title: Sidebar rows put accessibility on a container, so each row reads as several duplicate buttons
kept.evidence: `TabItem` applies `.accessibilityLabel(Text(tab.title))` and `.accessibilityAddTraits(...)` to the row's `HStack` without `.accessibilityElement(children:)` (lines 163-164). Same shape in `FavTabItem.swift:103`, `FolderItem.swift:52`, `SidebarURLDisplay.swift:106` and `SpaceHeaderRow.swift:93-97`. SwiftUI propagates those modifiers into the still-separate children (favicon, title `Text`, the close `Button`), so the row is never one element. `AuraMenuPanel.swift:90` shows the pattern the codebase already knows: `.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)` before the label.
kept.user_impact: Swiping through the sidebar with VoiceOver hits the same tab two or three times under the same name, the `.isSelected` trait lands on decorations rather than the row, and `SpaceHeaderRow`'s "Rename space" custom action is attached to fragments instead of the row.
kept.fix: Do not use `.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)` on TabItem/FavTabItem: it would drop the close/unpin button (TabItem.swift:196-206), which carries its own label, out of the tree entirely, and TabItem's comment at 160-162 says that button is meant to keep it. For those two rows use `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` so the nested button survives as a custom action, or keep `.ignore` and add `.accessibilityAction(named: Text("Close Tab"), onClose)` next to it. `.ignore` is correct as-is for FolderItem, SidebarURLDisplay and SpaceHeaderRow's `label`, which contain no nested controls.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed that the five rows apply accessibilityLabel/traits to a container that is not an accessibility element (TabItem.swift:161-164, FavTabItem.swift:103-104, FolderItem.swift:53-56, SidebarURLDisplay.swift:106-108, SpaceHeaderRow.swift:92-97), so SwiftUI pushes them down into the still-separate children instead of forming one row element. AuraMenuPanel.swift:90-94 is the in-repo pattern that does it correctly. Confidence is only moderate because the exact number of duplicate elements SwiftUI emits per row is not something I can prove from source alone; the missing container element itself is certain.

kept.title: Emoji and icon picker tiles are unlabelled text with tap gestures
kept.evidence: `emojiTile` is `Text(emoji).frame(...).contentShape(Rectangle()).onHover { ... }` (lines 60-68) with the tap attached in `cell(for:)` (lines 26-32); nothing carries a label or a button trait. `SpaceIconPicker.symbolGrid` (lines 102-121) is the same shape around `SpaceIconView` with only a hover fill, and the emoji category buttons (lines 128-143) are image-only `Button`s whose only content is `Image(systemName: categoryIcon(...))` with no `accessibilityLabel` or `.help`. Only the colour swatches got a `.help` (line 92).
kept.user_impact: Choosing a space icon with VoiceOver is guesswork: the grid reads as bare glyphs, the category row announces SF Symbol names like "pawprint", and the hover fill is the only indication of the current tile, so a keyboard-only user has none.
kept.fix: Two corrections. First, attach the button trait and the action where the tap lives, not on the shared tile: `emojiTile` is used by both `cell(for:)` and `variantStrip` with different actions, so putting `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` on the tile but `.accessibilityAction` at each call site keeps the two paths right, and a tile with variants should announce that it opens a strip (`.accessibilityHint(Text("Opens skin tone options"))` where `!item.variants.isEmpty`). Second, include the colour swatch (SpaceIconPicker.swift:82-96) in the same pass: it has `.help` but is a Circle with a tap gesture, so it also needs `.accessibilityLabel(Text(hex ?? "Auto"))`, `.isButton` and `.accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: emojiTile (EmojiPickerView.swift:59-67) is a Text with a hover fill and the tap bolted on at cell(for:) 24-34 and variantStrip 48-52; SpaceIconPicker.symbolGrid (102-121) is the same shape around SpaceIconView; the category buttons (126-143) contain only Image(systemName:) with no label or help. No accessibility modifier exists in either file.

kept.title: Colour picker is drag-only: no keyboard, no labels, no adjustable actions
kept.evidence: `saturationSquare` (lines 47-74) and `bar(fill:knobColor:fraction:onChange:)` (lines 112-132) drive hue, saturation, brightness and opacity purely from `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)`. None of them is focusable, none carries `accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityValue`/`accessibilityAdjustableAction`. The preset swatches (lines 144-165) are `Button`s whose label is a bare `Circle().fill(Color(hex: preset))` with no label, so they announce nothing.
kept.user_impact: A user who cannot drag precisely, or who is using VoiceOver, can only set a space or accent colour by typing a hex string into the field at the bottom; the picker itself is unusable without a mouse.
kept.fix: The proposed adjustable action does not fit the square, which has two axes and no single `fraction`. Do the bars only: inside `bar(...)` add a `label: String` parameter and hang `.accessibilityElement()`, `.accessibilityLabel(Text(label))`, `.accessibilityValue(Text("\(Int(fraction * 100))%"))` and `.accessibilityAdjustableAction { onChange(clamped(fraction + ($0 == .increment ? 0.02 : -0.02))) }` on the GeometryReader, passing "Hue" and "Opacity" from hueBar/intensityBar. For the square, give it two adjustable elements is overkill: label it `.accessibilityLabel(Text("Saturation and brightness"))` with `.accessibilityValue` reporting both, and leave precise entry to the hex field. Presets: `.accessibilityLabel(Text(preset))` plus `.help(preset)`, matching SpaceIconPicker's swatch.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: saturationSquare (AuraColorPicker.swift:47-73) and bar(fill:knobColor:fraction:onChange:) (112-131) are driven only by DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) with no labels, values or adjustable actions, and the preset buttons (139-157) wrap a bare Circle with no label. The hex field at 163-168 is the only keyboard path, which keeps this at medium rather than high.

kept.title: Modal dialogs and the launcher do not trap VoiceOver behind them
kept.evidence: `DialogsOverlay` draws the dim backdrop and `DialogContentView` over the whole window (lines 109-121) with no `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)` on the dialog and no `.accessibilityHidden(true)` on what is behind it; the backdrop's `.onTapGesture` (line 114) is also an unlabelled accessibility element. Nothing moves VoiceOver focus into the dialog when it appears (no `AccessibilityFocusState` anywhere in the repo). `LauncherView` (aura/Features/Launcher/LauncherView.swift:102-122) stacks its panel the same way over the live browser chrome.
kept.user_impact: With a confirm dialog up, VoiceOver keeps wandering into the page and the sidebar underneath, and the user has to hunt for the dialog that is blocking them; the same is true of the launcher.
kept.fix: Put `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)` on the DialogContentView (and on LauncherView's `panel`), and mark the backdrop `.accessibilityHidden(true)` so its tap gesture stops appearing as an unnamed element. Skip any focus-moving code: there is no AccessibilityFocusState in this codebase and isModal alone is what prunes the rest of the window.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: DialogsOverlay (DialogView.swift:100-121) draws the backdrop and DialogContentView with no isModal trait, no accessibilityHidden on the backdrop, and its .onTapGesture at 108 makes the backdrop itself an element; grep finds no AccessibilityFocusState anywhere in the repo. LauncherView.swift:102-116 stacks its backdrop and panel the same way. Note the keyboard side is already handled (OraRoot.swift:262-275 routes Escape and Return to the top dialog), so this is the VoiceOver containment gap only, which is why medium rather than high.

kept.title: Toasts are never announced and their close button has no name
kept.evidence: `ToastItemView` ends its row with `Button(action: onDismiss) { Image(systemName: "xmark") ... }` (lines 146-153) carrying no `accessibilityLabel` and no `.help`, unlike every other icon button in the chrome. The toast itself (lines 155-163) has no `.accessibilityElement`, no `.isModal`-free live-region equivalent and no announcement, and `ToastsContainerView` (lines 48-85) only pauses timers on hover.
kept.user_impact: Confirmations such as "Moved to Work" never reach a VoiceOver user, and the only way to dismiss one is a swipe gesture or an unnamed "button".
kept.fix: Label the button (`.accessibilityLabel(Text("Dismiss"))` plus `.help("Dismiss")`, matching the one-word help strings used elsewhere), but do not add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` to the row: it would fold the dismiss button back into the combined element and undo the label. For the announcement, post it once from where a toast is created (ToastManager's show path) rather than from `.onAppear` in ToastView, because the container re-renders the stack on every enqueue and dismiss.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: ToastItemView's dismiss Button (ToastView.swift:145-153) wraps only Image(systemName: "xmark") with no label or help, and the toast row (155-163) has no accessibility grouping or announcement; ToastsContainerView (48-84) only pauses timers on hover. Every other icon button in the chrome gets a label via oraShortcutHelp, so this is a genuine inconsistency, not a style choice.

kept.title: Every dialog's Cancel chip prints the letters "esc" instead of the ⎋ glyph
kept.evidence: `OraButton` matches its shortcut hint against `["return", "command", "shift", "control", "option", "escape", "delete.left"]` (line 141), but all ten call sites pass `"esc"`: `DialogView.swift:45`, `BookmarkEditDialog.swift:20,60`, `ExtensionStoreCards.swift:454`, `DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:45`, `NewContainerButton.swift:85`, `EditContainerModal.swift:74`. So the Confirm button renders the `return` SF Symbol while the Cancel button next to it renders lowercase text `esc` inside the same chip.
kept.user_impact: Every confirm dialog in the app shows one key as a glyph and the one beside it as three letters, which reads as an unfinished component.
