kept.verify_reason: The stale-comment half is confirmed: `preConsentedIDs` contains `FullUBlockOrigin.folderName` (BundledExtensions.swift:39) and `blockingInputs()` hardcodes `fullConsented: true` / `fullConsentRecorded: true` with its own comment saying so (BundledExtensions.swift:318-320), so `plan(for:)` cannot return `pending == .consent` in the app and the PrivacySettingsView comment at line 41-42 and the SettingsStore comment at line 177 both describe a flow that does not ship.

kept.title: The request-blocking setting carries a launcher sentence under a Search heading
kept.evidence: `// MARK: - Search` is followed immediately by `/// The floating launcher sits mid-window and slides up when suggestions appear.` and then, in the same doc comment, `/// Loads the injected web bundle that gives extensions a blocking webRequest. Off by default…` on `var extensionRequestBlocking`. Two unrelated leftovers glued to one property: the launcher sentence belongs to `launcherBlur` further down, and "Off by default" is contradicted by line 442, which defaults the key to `true`.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime; it reads as merge residue and misleads the next reader about the default.
kept.fix: Move the extension settings out from under the Search MARK into a `// MARK: - Extensions` block, delete the launcher sentence, and change "Off by default" to "On by default; `BundledExtensions.plan(for:)` decides what a given launch does with it".
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed verbatim: `// MARK: - Search` at SettingsStore.swift:156 is followed by the launcher sentence and the request-blocking doc comment glued together on `extensionRequestBlocking` (lines 158-163), and "Off by default" contradicts line 442, which defaults the key to `true`. The launcher sentence belongs to `launcherBlur` at line 187.

kept.title: Leftover alias in the compatibility verdict
kept.evidence: `let functional = missing` followed by `return .partial(functional)`, with a comment about the webRequestBlocking case between them that no longer describes any filtering. Nothing narrows `missing` any more, so the alias is a remnant of a partition that was removed.
kept.user_impact: None; it makes the function look like it filters something it does not.
kept.fix: Delete the binding and return `.partial(missing)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: ExtensionCompatibility.swift:133 binds `let functional = missing` and line 137 returns `.partial(functional)` with nothing in between that narrows it.

kept.title: "Check for updates" gives no sign it ran
kept.evidence: The button calls `extensionManager.checkForUpdates(force: true)` and nothing else changes on screen. `checkForUpdates` stores its work in `updateCheckTask`, which is declared `@ObservationIgnored var updateCheckTask: Task<Void, Never>?` (ExtensionManager.swift:148), so no view can observe that a check is in flight, and `adoptUpdateCheck` only writes `extensionAvailableUpdates` (ExtensionManager+Updates.swift:47-50). The card's `summary` grows an "n updates available" clause only when something was found, so the common outcome (everything current, or AMO unreachable) is a button press with zero feedback for the several seconds the AMO round trips take. The guard `updateCheckTask == nil` also silently swallows a second press.
kept.user_impact: Pressing the button looks broken: no spinner, no "up to date", no error when the network is down, and pressing it again does nothing.
kept.fix: Add `private(set) var isCheckingForUpdates = false` beside `updatingIDs` on the observable manager, set it true in `checkForUpdates` right where `updateCheckTask` is assigned and false in `adoptUpdateCheck`, then in the settings card swap the button for a `ProgressView().controlSize(.small)` while it is true and append a one-line result to `summary` ("Checked just now." from `extensionUpdateLastCheck`, or the offline sentence once extensions-scripts-5 lets the check report failure).

kept.title: The install-from-file panel is written twice, word for word
kept.evidence: `promptForFile()` in ExtensionStoreView.swift:194-210 and `promptForFile()` in ExtensionsSettingsView.swift:92-108 are the same fifteen lines: same `NSOpenPanel` flags, same `allowedContentTypes = [UTType.zip] + ["xpi", "crx"].compactMap { UTType(filenameExtension: $0) }`, same `message`, same `prompt`, same do/catch differing only in which `@State` string the error lands in.
kept.user_impact: None today; the two copies drift, so a fix to the accepted file types or the panel copy in one place silently misses the other entry point.
kept.fix: One `static func chooseFile() -> URL?` next to `installExtension(fromFile:)` on `ExtensionManager` that runs the panel and returns the url, leaving each view with its own do/catch around `try extensionManager.installExtension(fromFile: url)`. Touch it together with extensions-scripts-4, which has to edit both call sites anyway.

kept.title: Cut inside an extension popup copies but never removes the text
kept.evidence: The polyfill overrides `document.execCommand` with `if ((command === 'copy' || command === 'cut') && copy(selectedText())) return true;`. For `cut` it puts the selection on `NSPasteboard` and returns true without ever calling `originalExec`, so the selected text stays in the field and the extension is told the cut succeeded. `copy` is correct here; `cut` was folded into the same branch.
kept.user_impact: An extension popup that offers Cut (password managers moving a note, colour pickers swapping a hex value) leaves the old text in the field while claiming it was cut, so the user ends up with a duplicated value.
kept.fix: Split the branch: keep the early return for `copy`, and for `cut` do the pasteboard write and then still hand off, `if (command === 'cut' && copy(selectedText())) { return originalExec.apply(document, arguments) || true; }`, so WebKit performs the deletion it is willing to do while the clipboard half comes from the bridge.

dropped.title: The paint probe opens two floating windows on every launch, on every profile
dropped.reason: Refuted against the current tree. AuraWebBundlePaintProbe.swift:311-330 already defines `final class HostPanel: NSPanel` with `canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain == false` and `accessibilitySubrole() -> .floatingWindow`, and `hostWindow(for:slot:)` builds it with `styleMask: [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel]`, `isFloatingPanel = true`, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true`, `ignoresMouseEvents = true`; the code comment names the exact yabai/AeroSpace retile the finding describes. The auditor quoted a pre-fix version. The remaining half (cache the verdict per OS+build) is not a bug and would defeat the probe's stated purpose: `probe` is a per-launch check of a four-symbol private-API stack whose failure mode is machine- and session-dependent, and its only fallback (`markUnavailable`) is deliberately session-scoped, so a cached `painted` would suppress detection on a launch where the stack really is broken. The probe also does not delay first navigation: `WebRequestBroker.prepare()` (WebRequestBroker.swift:172-177) fires it in a detached `Task`, and every wait inside it is an `await`, not a block.

onboarding-home.summary: The welcome flow and the native home page are unusually well thought through for a first-run surface: the draft only commits on the last screen, the launch policy defers after a crash, and the copy mostly sounds like a person wrote it. The real damage is in focus handling. HomePageView's one-shot focus pulse never releases the window's first-responder lock, which is a direct cause of the "launcher opens but the caret is not in it" complaint, and the same page steals focus underneath the modal welcome card. Everything else is smaller: StatusPageView still ships stock AppKit buttons and Xcode-generated comments, the default-browser request uses a deprecated LaunchServices call and reads the result back synchronously, and a few rows (shortcut tiles, session restore bar) do not survive a narrow window or a hidden toolbar.

kept.title: Home page focus pulse locks first responder forever, so the caret leaves the launcher after an app switch
kept.evidence: HomePageView passes `isEditing: focusRequest ? true : nil` (line 168) and drops focusRequest 0.1 s later in focusField() (lines 334-339), whose comment claims focus is "then dropped so a later click elsewhere on the page keeps first responder". LauncherTextField only acts on a non-nil value: `if let isEditing { nsView.wantsFocus = isEditing }` (aura/Features/Launcher/Main/LauncherTextField.swift:189). wantsFocus is the FirstResponderLock switch (same file, lines 73-78), so the pulse calls focusLock.lock() and nothing ever calls unlock(). lock() sets AuraWindow.lockedFirstResponder (aura/Core/Platform/AuraWindow.swift:64) and re-takes first responder on every didBecomeKeyNotification (lines 65-77), and AuraWindow.becomeKey() forces it back too (lines 32-39).
kept.user_impact: With a home tab open: press Cmd-T, switch to another app, switch back. The launcher panel is still on screen but first responder has been yanked to the blurred, invisible home page field, so typing goes nowhere. The same steal hits an in-progress URL bar edit and any typing during the welcome tour.
kept.fix: In LauncherTextField.updateNSView change line 189 to `nsView.wantsFocus = isEditing ?? false`, with a one-line reason above it: nil means "leave focus alone", not "hold the window lock forever". The launcher passes isEditing: true (LauncherMain.swift:48) and the URL bar passes a plain Bool, so both keep today's behaviour; only the home page's expiring pulse now releases the lock.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading all three files. HomePageView pulses isEditing true then nil (HomePageView.swift:168, 334-339); LauncherTextField only writes wantsFocus inside `if let isEditing` (LauncherTextField.swift:189), and wantsFocus's didSet is the only caller of FirstResponderLock.lock()/unlock() (lines 73-78). Nothing ever passes false for the home page, so the lock stays: AuraWindow.lockedFirstResponder is set (AuraWindow.swift:63) and both becomeKey() (lines 31-38) and the didBecomeKey observer (lines 62-77) re-take first responder for the home field. The launcher is an overlay in the same window (BrowserView.swift:201-203), and the browser window is an AuraWindow (WindowFactory.swift:6), so after an app switch the launcher panel loses the caret. This matches the owner's reported ⌘T symptom, so high is right.

kept.title: Home page takes focus underneath the modal welcome card, so first-run keystrokes fill an invisible search field
kept.evidence: OnboardingPresenter draws the card as an overlay over BrowserView (aura/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift:24-34), so the home tab keeps rendering underneath. HomePageView.start() calls focusField() unconditionally at line 308, and focusField() (334-339) asks for first responder. Nothing in HomePageView consults OnboardingPolicy. Keystrokes on the welcome, style, favourites and blocking screens therefore reach the home field, whose onTextChange (169-176) runs viewModel.searchHandler and renders the suggestion panel (lines 180-210) behind the card's blur.
kept.user_impact: On first run, anything typed while the tour is up silently fills the home page search box and pops a ghost suggestion list behind the blur; when the tour ends the new tab already has stray text in its field.
kept.fix: Keep the guard inside focusField(), but add the release: `.onChange(of: settings.onboardingCompleted) { _, done in if done { focusField() } }` on the body. Without it, pressing "Dive in" leaves the new tab with no caret at all, since focusField() only runs again on appear or a tab switch.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. OnboardingPresenter draws the card as an overlay over BrowserView (OnboardingView.swift:24-32) while the home tab keeps rendering underneath, and HomePageView.start() calls focusField() with no policy check (HomePageView.swift:308, 334-339). Both `settings` and `privacyMode` exist on the view, so the guard compiles. With finding 1's lock in play the home field also holds first responder against the card's own space-name field.

kept.title: "Set as Default" reads the result back synchronously, so the card and the tour both report failure
kept.evidence: requestSetAsDefault() calls LSSetDefaultHandlerForURLScheme for http and https (lines 50-54), deprecated since macOS 12 with NSWorkspace.setDefaultApplication(at:toOpenURLsWithScheme:completionHandler:) as the replacement. Both callers then immediately call updateIsDefault(): HomePageView.swift:126-129 and OnboardingCommit.apply (aura/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingModel.swift:118-121). checkIsDefault() asks LaunchServices right away (lines 39-48), before the change (and any system consent prompt) has landed.
kept.user_impact: Pressing "Set as Default" on the home page leaves the first-run card on screen as if nothing happened; it only disappears the next time Aura is reactivated (the didBecomeActive observer at lines 26-29). During onboarding the same request is fired with no feedback at all.
kept.fix: NSWorkspace.setDefaultApplication(at:toOpenURLsWithScheme:completionHandler:) is macOS 14+, fine for this target. Call it for http and https, and in the completion handler hop back with `DispatchQueue.main.async { self.updateIsDefault() }` rather than assuming the handler's queue; requestSetAsDefault() is currently `static`, so it needs to become an instance method (or take `shared`) to touch isDefault. Keep the didBecomeActive observer as the backstop for changes made in System Settings.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: requestSetAsDefault() fires the two deprecated LaunchServices calls (DefaultBrowserManager.swift:50-54) and both call sites read the answer back immediately (HomePageView.swift:126-129, OnboardingModel.swift:118-121) through checkIsDefault(), which queries LaunchServices synchronously. The system consent prompt has not been answered by then, so isDefault stays false and the first-run card stays on screen until the next didBecomeActive (lines 26-29).

kept.title: StatusPageView is the only screen still drawing stock AppKit buttons, with Xcode-style narrative comments
kept.evidence: `Button("Try Again") {...}.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large)` and `Button("Go Back") {...}.buttonStyle(.bordered)` (lines 47-59) sit right above an OraButton for "Continue Anyway" (lines 63-71), so one error page mixes stock system chrome with the design system. These two are the only .borderedProminent/.bordered uses in aura/Features/Browser. The file also carries restating comments: "// Error icon" (17), "// Error title" (23), "// Error description" (29), "// Failed URL (if available)" (36), "// Action buttons" (45), "// Network-related errors" (127), "// WebKit errors" (148).
kept.user_impact: Every failed navigation shows a blue system-tinted button pair that belongs to no other screen in the browser, which is the first thing anyone notices on an error page.
kept.fix: OraButton has no `.lg` size in the way the finding assumes it is spelled here; copy the size argument style already used in this repo (HomePageView.swift:126 uses `size: .sm`) and check OraButton.swift for the available cases before writing `.lg`. Otherwise the fix stands.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed line for line: .borderedProminent/.bordered at StatusPageView.swift:47-59 directly above an OraButton at 63-71, and the seven restating comments at 17, 23, 29, 36, 45, 127, 148. Every failed navigation shows the mismatch.

kept.title: Bookmark import problems during onboarding are toasts, which render behind the welcome card's blur
kept.evidence: OnboardingBring imports through BookmarkImportAction.run (aura/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingSteps.swift:249-255). run() reports the "wrong file" case with `ToastManager.shared.show("No bookmarks in that file.", type: .error)` (line 174) and the "nothing new" case at line 214, while only the read failure goes through dialogManager (182-188). The toast overlay is attached inside BrowserSplitView.contentView (.toast(manager:), aura/Features/Browser/Views/BrowserSplitView.swift:88), i.e. below the onboarding overlay, whose backdrop is a hudWindow blur plus a black scrim (OnboardingView.swift:98-111).
kept.user_impact: Pick the wrong file on the "Bring your things" screen and the explanation appears blurred out behind the card. The screen just sits there with no confirmation, so the user retries the same file.
kept.fix: The "Everything in that file was already saved" toast (report(), line 214) is on the same screen and equally invisible; it is the likelier of the two on a second import. Pass dialogManager into report() and route that case the same way, or the user still gets silence.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. BookmarkImportAction.run reports the empty-parse case with a toast (DataPortabilityViews.swift:174) while the read failure goes through dialogManager (182-188); the toast overlay is attached inside BrowserSplitView.contentView (BrowserSplitView.swift:89) and the onboarding card is applied above it at OraRoot.swift:139, over a hudWindow blur plus gradient plus scrim. During the "Bring your things" step the message is unreadable.

kept.title: Home page shortcut tiles are clipped at narrow pane widths instead of dropping the ones that do not fit
kept.evidence: The column is sized `min(740, max(geo.size.width - 48, 220))` (line 42), while shortcutsRow lays out up to maxShortcuts = 8 tiles in a plain HStack (lines 231-250) at tileSize 40 with spacing 10, so 8 tiles need 390 pt. BrowserWebContentView clips the page (`.clipped()`, line 99), so at a pane narrower than about 440 pt the outermost tiles are cut in half on both sides.
kept.user_impact: With the sidebar out or a half-screen window, the favourites row on the new tab page shows sliced-off icons at both ends rather than a shorter, complete row.
kept.fix: shortcutsRow is a computed property with no width in scope; make it `private func shortcutsRow(width: CGFloat)` and call it from `column` (which itself needs the width passed down from the GeometryReader at line 41). Otherwise the prefix arithmetic stands.
kept.verify_reason: The clipping is real: column width floors at 220 (HomePageView.swift:42), eight 40pt tiles with 10pt spacing need 390, and the page is clipped at BrowserWebContentView.swift:100. But the stated trigger is wrong: clipping starts below roughly 438pt of pane, and a half-screen window on a normal display leaves more than that. It needs a near-minimum window (contentMinSize is 500x360, WindowFactory.swift:18) with the sidebar out. Cosmetic and rare, so low.

kept.title: No way out of the seven-screen welcome tour except clicking Continue seven times
kept.evidence: OnboardingPage offers exactly two buttons, Continue and Back (lines 52-62), on every screen. The welcome screen has one arrow (135-173). Escape is not handled anywhere in OnboardingView, and OnboardingKeyGuard swallows every command chord except q, h, m, a, c, v, x, z (OnboardingView.swift:150-160), so Cmd-W cannot close it either. OnboardingCommit only runs from the finish screen (OnboardingView.swift:140-143).
kept.user_impact: A returning user who just wants a browser window has to click through six screens; quitting mid-way brings the whole tour back on next launch.
kept.fix: Nothing wrong with the fix, but the ghost Skip belongs next to Back on OnboardingPage only, not on the welcome screen (which has no Back) and not on .finish (whose primary button already commits).
kept.verify_reason: The code is as described: two buttons on every OnboardingPage (OnboardingSteps.swift:52-62), no Escape handling, and OnboardingKeyGuard swallows ⌘W (OnboardingView.swift:150-160). But the impact is overstated: the primary button carries .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) (OnboardingSteps.swift:60, and the welcome arrow at 166), so Return walks the whole flow in six presses, and OnboardingPresenter.retireForExistingProfiles already retires the tour for upgraded profiles (OnboardingView.swift:39-46). It is a first-run-only annoyance, so low.

kept.title: Onboarding key guard captures a nil window on appear, so it swallows command chords in every window of the app
kept.evidence: installKeyGuard captures `let window = window` once from the environment (lines 84-89) and the monitor's first line is `guard window == nil || event.window === window else { return event }`, i.e. a nil window means "swallow everywhere". The environment value is published by WindowReader into @State after the first render (OraRoot.swift:163-171), while installKeyGuard runs from .onAppear (line 74), so the captured value is nil on the pass that installs the monitor and is never refreshed.
kept.user_impact: During first run, a second window (opened from the File menu, which the monitor does not block) loses every command shortcut too, including the ones its own card wants to allow.
kept.fix: `.onChange(of: window, initial: true)` is fine (OraRoot.swift:192 already does onChange on the same optional NSWindow), but keep it paired with the existing .onDisappear removal so the monitor is not leaked when the flow ends between changes.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: installKeyGuard captures the environment window once at .onAppear (OnboardingView.swift:74, 84-89) and WindowReader publishes it a run loop later (WindowReader.swift:9-18), so the captured value is nil and `window == nil ||` makes the monitor global. Impact is narrower than claimed: the app is sandboxed (aura/Info/aura.entitlements), so the import file picker runs out of process and is unaffected, and a second window mounts its own card with the same allow-list. What is left is a second window's shortcuts dying during first run.

kept.title: Expired and unknown-root certificates fall through to "Something Went Wrong" with no Continue Anyway
kept.evidence: errorType maps only NSURLErrorServerCertificateUntrusted, NSURLErrorClientCertificateRequired and NSURLErrorSecureConnectionFailed to .security (lines 137-140). NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasBadDate, NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasUnknownRoot and NSURLErrorServerCertificateNotYetValid hit the default and become .unknown (143-144). The Continue Anyway button, and with it Tab.continueToInsecureSite / bypassSSL (aura/Features/Tabs/Models/Tab.swift:466-472), is gated on `errorType == .security` (line 63).
kept.user_impact: The most common certificate failure, an expired certificate, shows the generic "An unexpected error occurred" page with no explanation and no way through, even though the bypass machinery exists.
kept.fix: Add NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasBadDate, NSURLErrorServerCertificateHasUnknownRoot and NSURLErrorServerCertificateNotYetValid to the .security case at line 137.
kept.verify_reason: errorType really does map only three codes to .security (StatusPageView.swift:137-140) and Continue Anyway is gated on that (line 63), with the bypass wired through Tab.continueToInsecureSite (Tab.swift:466-472) into BrowserPage.bypassSSL (BrowserPage.swift:370-372). Whether WebKit reports an expired certificate as -1201 or as -1202 is not verifiable from this code, so the frequency claim is unproven, but adding the three codes is correct and costs nothing.

kept.title: Home page logo is announced to VoiceOver as "ora logo plain"
kept.evidence: `Image("ora-logo-plain")` (line 64) is decorative but carries no accessibility treatment, so AppKit falls back to the asset name. The same pattern is in OnboardingWelcome, `Image("OraColorLogo")` (aura/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingSteps.swift:143).
kept.user_impact: VoiceOver users hear the old product name read out of an asset filename on the new tab page and on the first screen of the welcome flow.
kept.fix: On the home page prefer `Image(decorative: "ora-logo-plain")`, the native way to say "no label", over adding .accessibilityHidden(true) to a decorative image. The welcome logo keeps .accessibilityLabel(Text("Aura")).
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: Image("ora-logo-plain") at HomePageView.swift:64 and Image("OraColorLogo") at OnboardingSteps.swift:143 carry no accessibility treatment, so SwiftUI falls back to the asset name and VoiceOver reads the retired product name.

kept.title: Xcode boilerplate header left on DefaultBrowserManager
kept.evidence: Lines 1-6 are the generated `//  DefaultBrowserManager.swift / //  aura / //  Created by keni on 9/30/25.` block. Only two files in the whole source tree still carry it (this one and aura/Features/FindInPage/FindView.swift); every other file opens with a doc comment.
kept.user_impact: None for the user; it is the kind of leftover that makes a codebase read as unfinished during review.
kept.fix: Delete the header in DefaultBrowserManager.swift and FindView.swift only, and leave aura/Shared/Layout/SplitView/** alone (vendored). DefaultBrowserManager has no doc comment to fall back on, so replace the block with one line, e.g. `/// Whether Aura is the system handler for http and https, and the request to become it.`
kept.verify_reason: The header is there (DefaultBrowserManager.swift:1-6), but the count is wrong: twelve files still carry it, and ten of them are the vendored Shared/Layout/SplitView sources, which should keep their upstream headers.

kept.title: Session restore message truncates to one line with no way to read the rest
kept.evidence: `Text("Aura quit unexpectedly. The tabs from that session are still open.").lineLimit(1)` (lines 22-25) sits before a Spacer and two buttons in a fixed 12 pt padded row. In a narrow window the sentence is cut mid-word, and there is no .help() behind it.
kept.user_impact: In a half-screen window the only explanation of why two unfamiliar buttons appeared reads "Aura quit unexpectedly. The tabs from..." with no way to see the rest.
kept.fix: Add `.help("Aura quit unexpectedly. The tabs from that session are still open.")` to the Text, reusing the same string via a private static constant so the label and tooltip cannot drift.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: SessionRestoreBar.swift:22-25 sets lineLimit(1) on the explanation with two buttons after it in a 12pt padded row, and there is no .help(). In a narrow window the sentence truncates with no way to read the rest.

kept.title: The address bar reads "home / New Tab" on the new-tab page instead of showing its placeholder
kept.evidence: displayText passes the tab's URL straight to URLDisplayUtils.displayString (URLBarField.swift:310-313). For a home tab that URL is aura://home and the title is "New Tab" (TabManager.swift:434, Tab.swift:395-397), so displayParts returns host "home" with title "New Tab" (URLDisplayUtils.swift:9-32) and the pill renders "home / New Tab". The same path gives "settings / Settings" and "extensions / Extensions". Because displayText is non-empty, LauncherTextField never shows its "Search or enter address" placeholder (LauncherTextField.swift:181-183).
kept.user_impact: The most-seen screen in the browser shows a fake address made of an internal host and a tab title, where Safari, Chrome and Arc all show an empty field inviting you to type.
kept.fix: In displayText return "" for the new-tab page before falling through: `if tab.url.isOraHome { return "" }`, with a reason that a new tab has no address to show, so the field falls back to its placeholder. Leave the sidebar pill (SidebarURLDisplay.swift:143-147) alone, where "New Tab" is the tab's name rather than an address.

kept.title: The welcome card clips its own Continue button in a small window
kept.evidence: cardWidth/cardHeight cap the card at size - 48 (OnboardingView.swift:132-138), and the card is clipShape'd to that frame (line 124). The window's contentMinSize is 500x360 (WindowFactory.swift:18), so the card can be forced down to about 452x312 while OnboardingPage puts a 300pt copy column with 36pt padding, a title, a fixedSize message and two stacked buttons on the left (OnboardingSteps.swift:39-65) and a 3x3 72pt grid on the right (OnboardingSteps.swift:369-374). Nothing scrolls, so the overflow is cut off rather than compressed.
kept.user_impact: A first run in a small or resized window loses the Continue and Back buttons off the bottom of the card; Return still advances, but there is nothing on screen saying so.
kept.fix: Wrap the card's content in a ScrollView when it does not fit, or drop OnboardingPage's copy column width to `min(300, cardWidth * 0.42)` and let the page scroll: the smallest honest change is `.frame(...)` on the card followed by a ScrollView inside OnboardingStepView so a short window scrolls instead of clipping.

dropped.title: Session restore bar is not gated on the toolbar row, so after a crash it sits against the window edge under the traffic lights
dropped.reason: The stated impact is wrong. WindowAccessor.updateTrafficLights hides the native window buttons whenever the toolbar row is down (`button.isHidden = !(isFullscreen || showInToolbar)`, WindowAccessor.swift:166-173), so nothing is drawn over the restore bar; the sidebar draws its own controls instead. What is left is a cosmetic edge-flush row. Worse, the proposed gate hides a bar that cannot be dismissed any other way (SessionRestoreBar.swift:6-9): with the toolbar hidden the user would never see the question and their crashed session would sit unanswered until they happened to hover-reveal the chrome. Not worth the trade.

tabs-state.summary: The tab layer is the most carefully built part of this codebase I looked at: neighbour selection, cross-window delete reconciliation, hibernation scoring and session capture are all factored into pure, tested functions with comments that explain why rather than what. The bugs left are at the seams where one subsystem hands off to another: a popup adoption that builds a web view it immediately throws away, an undo that silently demotes a pinned tab, ⌘1-9 counting a flat tab list while the sidebar renders folders, and a favicon view that never re-reads after the download lands. The rest is honest wear: a 10 ms deferred closure that keeps a strong reference and no page identity check, an O(n log n) score recomputation inside a sort comparator that the same repo already fixed once in the launcher, and a store-open failure path that ends in fatalError with nothing on screen.

kept.title: Adopting a window.open popup builds and throws away a whole web view
kept.evidence: `didRequestAdopt` calls `tabManager.addTab(url: url ?? about:blank, ...)` with the default `activateAfterAdding: true`. `addTab` calls `activateTab(newTab, persist: false)`, which sees `!tab.isWebViewReady` and runs `restoreTransientState` — building a full `BrowserPage`, its delegate, and scheduling the 10 ms deferred `startRestoredLoad`. Only afterwards does line 161 do `newTab.browserPage = popup`, dropping the just-built page without `teardown()`. The doc comment at line 145 ("`isWebViewReady` is set here so `restoreTransientState` leaves it alone") describes the opposite order to the one the code runs in: line 164 sets the flag after `addTab` already returned.
kept.user_impact: Every `window.open` (OAuth sign-in popups, payment flows, "open in new window" links) spins up an extra WebContent process and navigates it to about:blank before abandoning it. On a machine already under memory pressure that is a second process launch and a main-thread page build the user pays for on every popup.
kept.fix: Fix as proposed, with one detail: end with activateTab(newTab, persist: false) rather than activateTab(newTab), because addTab already saved and the popup path adds no further store mutation worth a second transaction.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading the chain: TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:151 calls addTab with the default activateAfterAdding: true (TabManager.swift:426), addTab line 458 calls activateTab(persist: false), activateTab line 777-785 sees !isWebViewReady and calls restoreTransientState, and about:blank / a popup URL is not isOraInternal (URL+Ora.swift:27-30) so a full BrowserPage, profile and delegate are built and a 10 ms deferred load is scheduled. Line 161 then overwrites browserPage with the popup without teardown(). The throwaway page is also built on the wrong store identifier, since newTab.browsingContainer is assigned after addTab returns. The doc comment at line 145 does describe the opposite order. Downgraded from high: nothing breaks visually and the orphan page is released once the deferred closure fires, so the cost is one wasted WebContent process plus a main-thread page build per window.open, not a user-visible failure.

kept.title: Reopening a deleted pinned or favourite tab brings it back as a normal tab
kept.evidence: `deleteTab` sets `tab.type = .normal` and `tab.savedURL = nil` *before* calling `closeTab`, and `closeTab` is what calls `trackRecentlyClosedTab(tab)` (line 660-662). So `ClosedTabSnapshot.init` records `type: .normal, savedURL: nil`. `restoreLastTab` faithfully rebuilds from the snapshot, and `shiftRestoredTabOrders` already handles a non-normal `snapshot.type`, so the machinery to restore it correctly is present and simply never gets the right data.
kept.user_impact: Delete a pinned tab from its context menu, hit ⌘⇧T to undo, and the tab comes back as an ordinary tab in the normal-tab section with its pinned URL lost. The user has to re-pin it and re-set the pinned URL by hand.
kept.fix: Snapshot before demoting: `func deleteTab(tab: Tab) { guard tab.type != .normal else { closeTab(tab: tab); return }; trackRecentlyClosedTab(tab); tab.type = .normal; tab.savedURL = nil; closeTab(tab: tab, shouldTrackForRestore: false) }`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. deleteTab (TabManager.swift:729-735) demotes to .normal and nils savedURL before calling closeTab, and closeTab tracks the snapshot at line 660-662 after the demotion, so ClosedTabSnapshot.init (TabManager+RecentlyClosed.swift:29-44) records type .normal and savedURL nil. restoreLastTab rebuilds faithfully from the snapshot and shiftRestoredTabOrders already handles a non-normal type. The user path is real: TabItem.swift:271-276 routes the context menu's Close Tab to deleteTab for any pinned or favourite tab, and TabLifecycleTests.swift:214 covers the delete but not the reopen.

kept.title: ⌘1–⌘9 counts a flat tab list while the sidebar renders folders inline
kept.evidence: `selectTabAtIndex` builds `allTabs = favoriteTabs + pinnedTabs + normalTabs` where `normalTabs` is every `.normal` tab in the space sorted by `order`, folders ignored. `NormalTabsList.rows` (NormalTabsList.swift:47-49) interleaves folders and top-level tabs on the shared `order` scale, and renders a folder's tabs nested underneath it — and not at all when `folder.isCollapsed`. So the flat index and the visible row index diverge the moment a space has a folder.
kept.user_impact: In any space with a folder, ⌘3 selects a different tab than the third row on screen, and can select a tab hidden inside a collapsed folder. The comment on line 823 ("Match the sidebar ordering") is stale.
kept.fix: Same shape, plus two details the auditor missed. The sidebar's first row is NewTabButton, not a tab, so index 1 must still mean the first tab row: keep counting tabs only. And ContainerView.swift:48 hides the whole pinned section in a private window, so the pinned tabs should be dropped from the list when privacy mode is on, or ⌘1 in a private window selects an invisible pinned tab. Passing the same filter the sidebar uses (or reading privacyMode at the call site) is the smallest way to keep the two in step.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. selectTabAtIndex (TabManager.swift:822-846) filters every .normal tab in the space, including tabs that live in a folder, while ContainerView.swift:104-108 passes only tabs with folder == nil to NormalTabsList and NormalTabsList.rows (line 47) interleaves folders with those top-level tabs, rendering a folder's tabs nested and only when !folder.isCollapsed. The flat index and the visible order diverge as soon as a space has one folder, and a hidden tab can be selected.

kept.title: A restored web view's deferred load holds the tab strongly and never checks the page is still current
kept.evidence: `restoreTransientState` ends with `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.01) { self.startRestoredLoad(page: page, loading: loading); self.isWebViewReady = true }` — the only escaping closure in Tab.swift without `[weak self]` (compare `setFavicon` line 156, `updateHeaderColor` line 197, `recordScrollOffset` line 192). Nothing checks `browserPage === page`. Anything that runs `destroyWebView()` or `stopMedia()` inside that 10 ms window (`closeTab` → `stopMedia` → `modelContext.delete`; `navigate(to:)` on an aura:// target; `rehost`; `ContainerManager.rebind`) leaves the closure calling `startRestoredLoad` on a torn-down page — reading `launchURL`, i.e. the persisted `type`, `savedURL` and `url`, off a row already deleted and saved — and then setting `isWebViewReady = true` with `browserPage == nil`.
kept.user_impact: `BrowserWebContentView` (line 121 and 165) renders an indeterminate spinner forever for a tab whose `isWebViewReady` is true but whose `browserPage` is nil, with no reload path out of it. The stored-property read on a deleted SwiftData row is the same hazard `TabPosition` was written to avoid (TabManager+Deletion.swift:30-33).
kept.fix: `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.01) { [weak self, weak page] in guard let self, let page, self.browserPage === page else { return }; self.startRestoredLoad(page: page, loading: loading); self.isWebViewReady = true }`.
kept.verify_reason: The closure at Tab.swift:307-310 does capture self strongly and never checks that browserPage is still the page it built, confirmed. The 'only escaping closure without weak self' claim is wrong (setNavigationError at line 444 and clearNavigationError at line 452 both capture self strongly), but the substance holds: the codebase itself documents the hazard at TabManager+Deletion.swift:30-33, 'reading any stored property off the model traps inside SwiftData', and startRestoredLoad (TabSession.swift:220-221) reads launchURL, which is the persisted type, savedURL and url. Reachable by closing a just-activated tab inside the 10 ms window (key-repeat ⌘W): closeTab calls stopMedia then deleteIfPresent then save, and the closure then reads the deleted row. The 'spinner forever' half is weaker than stated, since most destroy paths either re-enter restoreTransientState or leave an aura:// URL that renders natively, but the guard is one line.

kept.title: A downloaded favicon never reaches a sidebar row that is already on screen
kept.evidence: `LocalFavIcon` loads its image only from `.onAppear(perform: loadFavicon)` inside the `else` branch of `if let image`. `Tab.setFavicon` (Tab.swift:154-167) sets `faviconLocalFile` from an async download completion, long after the row appeared. Because `image` stays nil, SwiftUI keeps the same `else` branch view identity and `onAppear` never fires again, so `loadFavicon` is never re-run with the now-non-nil path.
kept.user_impact: A hibernated or pinned tab (the two cases where `FavIcon` renders `LocalFavIcon` rather than the `AsyncImage`) sits with the grey globe placeholder for the rest of the session, even though its icon is on disk. Relaunching the app fixes it, which is exactly the shape of bug a demanding user notices and cannot explain.
kept.fix: Re-run the load when the path arrives: add `.onChange(of: faviconLocalFile) { _, _ in loadFavicon() }` next to the existing `.onAppear(perform: loadFavicon)`.
kept.verify_reason: The defect is real: LocalFavIcon (TabItem.swift:4-41) loads only from .onAppear inside the else branch, so a faviconLocalFile that arrives while that branch stays mounted with image == nil is never picked up. The stated impact is overstated, though. setFavicon (Tab.swift:151) sets favicon synchronously before the download, and FavIcon (TabItem.swift:52-72) switches branch on favicon/isWebViewReady, so hibernating or parking a tab remounts LocalFavIcon and fires onAppear. The case that survives is narrow: AsyncImage fails on the guessed favicon URL and downloadAndSaveFavicon returns a nil sourceURL, leaving the placeholder globe up with a good file on disk. Downgraded to low, kept because the fix is one line and cannot regress anything.

kept.title: Favicon files are keyed by tab id, so the cached image goes stale on navigation and duplicates share a file
kept.evidence: `setFavicon` writes to `"\(self.id.uuidString).favicon"` — one path per tab, reused for every domain the tab ever visits. `FaviconService.icon(atFile:)` (FaviconService.swift:249-257) memoises in an `NSCache` keyed by `fileURL.path`, and nothing ever calls `removeObject`. So once a tab navigates from github.com to google.com, the file on disk is overwritten but the in-memory cache keeps serving github's icon under the same path. `duplicateTab` (TabManager.swift:880) copies `faviconLocalFile` verbatim, so the copy points at the original tab's file and silently adopts whatever the original navigates to next.
kept.user_impact: Hibernated and pinned rows show the previous site's icon, and a duplicated tab's icon changes under it when the tab it was copied from navigates. Ten tabs on the same domain also each download and store their own copy of the same bytes.
kept.fix: Sanitise the name before using it as a path component: a host can be an IPv6 literal ([::1]) or an IDN, so use the already-normalised domain with ':' and '/' replaced, e.g. let fileName = "\(domain.replacingOccurrences(of: ":", with: "_").replacingOccurrences(of: "/", with: "_")).favicon". Old tab-id-named files stay on disk pointed at by persisted faviconLocalFile values until each tab next navigates, which is harmless; no migration needed.
kept.verify_reason: Both halves confirmed: Tab.swift:145 names the file by tab id, FaviconService.swift:249-257 memoises by fileURL.path and nothing ever calls removeObject on fileImages, and duplicateTab (TabManager.swift:881) copies faviconLocalFile verbatim. Visible only on the LocalFavIcon path (hibernated or parked rows), because a live tab renders the remote AsyncImage, so it is a stale icon on unloaded rows plus redundant per-tab downloads rather than a medium-severity defect.

kept.title: Memory-pressure eviction recomputes the importance score inside the sort comparator
kept.evidence: `evictionOrder` is `tabs.sorted { importanceScore($0, now: now) < importanceScore($1, now: now) }`. `importanceScore` line 121 calls `manager?.isActiveInAnyWindow(tab)`, which calls `TabManager.activeTabIDsAcrossWindows` (TabManager.swift:60-63) — that mutates the static registry with `removeAll` and builds a fresh `Set` on every call. Both also read `SettingsStore.shared` through `isEligible`. So one pressure pass over n candidates does ~2·n·log n registry mutations and Set allocations, on the main thread, at the exact moment the system is short of memory. The repo already fixed this exact shape once: TabSearchingService.swift:47 — "Score once per tab: recomputing inside the comparator ran the scorer O(n log n) times per launcher keystroke."
kept.user_impact: A memory-pressure warning with 60 open tabs stalls the main thread doing redundant set-building before it unloads anything, which is the worst possible moment for a hitch. Mutating shared static state from inside a sort comparator is also a correctness hazard if the registry is ever touched concurrently.
kept.fix: Only the decorate-sort-undecorate line is worth doing. Hoisting the active-id set into isEligible and evictionCandidates changes two more signatures and their callers (cleanupOldTabs, enforceLiveTabLimit, handleAppResignActive) for no measurable gain; skip it.
kept.verify_reason: Mechanically confirmed: evictionOrder (TabManager+Hibernation.swift:140) scores inside the comparator, importanceScore line 121 calls isActiveInAnyWindow which calls TabManager.activeTabIDsAcrossWindows (TabManager.swift:60-63), and that mutates the static registry with removeAll and builds a fresh Set on every call. hibernateInRounds re-runs the whole sort per round. But the absolute cost is small (a few hundred tiny Set builds for 60 candidates), everything is @MainActor so the 'concurrency hazard' does not apply, and the claimed stall is not supported. Kept as a low perf/hygiene item because the repo already fixed this exact shape once, at TabSearchingService.swift:47.

kept.title: A refused store ends in fatalError with nothing on screen and no pointer to the error file
kept.evidence: `openStore` retries once with no delay at all (`attempt += 1` loops straight back into `createOraContainer`), then calls `fatalError("Failed to initialize ModelContainer: \(error)")`. `recordStoreFailure` writes the reason to `~/Library/Application Support/Aura/last-store-error.txt` — which is how the recorded `SwiftDataError.unknownDataStoreSchema` of 2026-08-22 survived — but nothing ever tells the user that file exists. The comment on line 23 justifies the retry as covering "a lock held by a window still closing", which a zero-millisecond retry cannot outlast.
kept.user_impact: When the store refuses to open, Aura crashes on launch with a macOS crash report the user cannot act on, and every subsequent launch does the same. The recovery note the code went to the trouble of writing is invisible.
kept.fix: Keep the alert to the non-private branch only (an in-memory store failing is a programmer error, not something the user can act on), and add a 'Reveal error file' button using NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([path]) beside Quit so the recorded reason is one click away instead of a path the user has to retype.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraRoot.swift:118-131 loops with no delay (StoreOpenFailure.action at line 26 allows exactly one retry) and ends in fatalError, while recordStoreFailure (line 135-145) writes ~/Library/Application Support/Aura/last-store-error.txt and nothing ever surfaces that path. The retry comment at line 23 claims it covers 'a lock held by a window still closing', which a zero-delay retry cannot. Note the other two callers of createOraContainer (SiteSpaceRuleService.swift:125, PasswordManagerService.swift:677) use try? and degrade, so this fatal path is unique to launch.

kept.title: Tab expiry saves the store and posts a notification once per tab instead of once per pass
kept.evidence: `removeOldTabs` and `autoClearContainerTabs` both call `closeTab(tab:shouldTrackForRestore:false)` inside a loop over `Array(container.tabs)`. Each `closeTab` ends with `saveOrLog(modelContext)` and `announceDeletedTabs(deleted)` (TabManager.swift:674-675). Compare `ContainerManager.delete`, which was explicitly rewritten to avoid this: "Going through `move(_:to:)` saved once per tab and rebuilt each web view synchronously, so deleting a container with a dozen tabs froze the window."
kept.user_impact: When a space's auto-clear window elapses, the minute tick does one SQLite transaction and one cross-window notification per expired tab on the main thread. A space with fifty stale tabs is fifty commits in one run-loop turn — a visible stall in a window the user is typing in.
kept.fix: Do not duplicate closeTab's teardown inside the hibernation file. Add a persist flag to closeTab in the shape the file already uses for activateTab(_:persist:): closeTab(tab:shouldTrackForRestore:persist:) skips saveOrLog and returns the deleted id instead of announcing, and the two expiry loops collect the ids, then do one saveOrLog and one announceDeletedTabs. The same helper also fixes TabFolderManager.delete(folder:closeTabs:) (line 55-59) and closeAllTabs(in:) (line 62-66), which have the identical per-tab commit. files_to_touch must therefore include aura/Features/Tabs/State/TabManager.swift.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: removeOldTabs (TabManager+Hibernation.swift:342) and autoClearContainerTabs (line 366) both call closeTab per tab, and closeTab ends with saveOrLog plus announceDeletedTabs (TabManager.swift:674-675). Each pass therefore does one SQLite commit and one cross-window notification per expired tab, and observeCrossWindowDeletes uses queue: nil (TabManager.swift:172) so every other window reconciles inline, once per tab. The default tabRemovalTimeout is 24 hours (SettingsStore.swift:648), so leaving twenty tabs overnight is twenty commits on one minute tick in a window the user may be typing in. closeTab also runs a fetchCount per tab through deleteIfPresent.

kept.title: Selection can fall into a collapsed folder, leaving the sidebar with nothing highlighted
kept.evidence: `neighbour(after:)`'s last fallback (line 630-632) and `activateContainer`'s `max(by: lastAccessedAt)` (line 392) both consider every tab in the space, including tabs inside a collapsed folder — `NormalTabsList.folderRow` renders those tabs only when `!folder.isCollapsed`. `move(tab:to:)` (TabFolderManager.swift:79) and `restoreLastTab` (TabManager+RecentlyClosed.swift:76) both expand the folder for exactly this reason; `activateTab` does not.
kept.user_impact: Collapse a folder, close the last top-level tab in the space, and the page that comes up belongs to a tab with no visible row — the sidebar shows no selection at all until the user finds and expands the folder.
kept.fix: Guard the write so it is not a no-op store mutation on every tab switch: `if tab.folder?.isCollapsed == true { tab.folder?.isCollapsed = false }`. Assigning an equal value still marks the row dirty in SwiftData, and activateTab runs on every selection change.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. neighbour(after:) (TabManager.swift:623-632) falls back to any remaining tab in the space by lastAccessedAt, and activateContainer (line 388-392) does the same, both including tabs inside a folder; NormalTabsList.folderRow (NormalTabsList.swift:137) renders those tabs only when !folder.isCollapsed. move(tab:to:) (TabFolderManager.swift:79) and restoreLastTab (TabManager+RecentlyClosed.swift:74) both expand for exactly this reason, so the one guard in activateTab is consistent with the file's own precedent.

kept.title: The header-colour snapshot config takes a parameter it ignores
kept.evidence: `static func configuration(for viewSize: CGSize) -> BrowserSnapshotConfiguration { .thumbnail }` never reads `viewSize`. The sole caller (line 508) threads `bounds.size` through it for nothing, and the doc comment above it argues about rect-scoped snapshots the function no longer takes.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime. It reads as a function that adapts to the view size and does not, which is the kind of thing that gets trusted later.
kept.fix: Do not delete the function, drop the parameter: `static var configuration: BrowserSnapshotConfiguration { .thumbnail }`, update line 509 and BrowserPageTests.swift:370. The test is what keeps the 'never a rect' rule from regressing, so it stays. files_to_touch: aura/Features/Tabs/Browser/TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift, auraTests/BrowserPageTests.swift.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: HeaderColorSnapshot.configuration(for:) (TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:48-50) ignores viewSize and the sole production caller at line 509 threads bounds.size through it. But the finding's files_to_touch is incomplete: auraTests/BrowserPageTests.swift:370 calls it and asserts the rect-is-nil, width-32 contract, so deleting the function deletes a real regression test.

kept.title: Tab search has a dead all-tabs branch and a sentinel UUID for "no space"
kept.evidence: `predicate = #Predicate { _ in true }` for empty input returns every tab in every space with no container filter — the only caller, `LauncherViewModel.searchHandler`, short-circuits empty text before reaching `runLocalSearch`, so the branch is unreachable and would be wrong if it were reached. Line 23's `activeContainer?.id ?? UUID()` fabricates a random id to mean "match nothing", which `LauncherViewModel` line 113 then copies for the history search.
kept.user_impact: None today. It is a trap: the first caller that passes empty text gets cross-space results the launcher was designed not to show.
kept.fix: Write the guard the way the codebase words such things: `guard let activeContainerId = activeContainer?.id, !trimmedText.isEmpty else { return [] }` and keep one predicate. The auditor's phrase 'non-optional UUID?' is a contradiction; the parameter stays TabContainer? and the guard does the work. TabLifecycleTests.swift:410 exercises the non-empty path and keeps passing.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. TabSearchingService.swift:27-28 returns a match-everything predicate with no container filter for empty input, and the only route in, LauncherViewModel.searchHandler (line 55-63), returns defaultSuggestions before runLocalSearch for empty or whitespace-only text, so the branch is unreachable and would return cross-space results if it were reached. The sentinel `activeContainer?.id ?? UUID()` at line 23 is copied at LauncherViewModel.swift:113 for the history search.

kept.title: Four copies of "build the active tab's web view if it has none"
kept.evidence: The same lazy-restore block appears in `BrowserView.onChange(of: activeTab)` (+0.01s), `BrowserView.onAppear` (+0.1s), `TabItem.onAppear` (TabItem.swift:141-150) and `FavTabItem.onAppear` (FavTabItem.swift:72-81) — on top of `TabManager.activateTab` (TabManager.swift:778-785), which already does it synchronously. The two sidebar-row copies fire whenever a row scrolls into view, and the `BrowserView.onChange` copy always fires because `restoreTransientState` leaves `isWebViewReady` false for its first 10 ms.
kept.user_impact: No visible breakage — `restoreTransientState` guards on `browserPage != nil` — but four differently-delayed copies of one rule means the next change to the restore path has to be found in four places, and the delays are arbitrary (0.01 vs 0.1).
kept.fix: Delete the `onAppear` blocks in TabItem and FavTabItem and the `onChange` block in BrowserView; `activateTab` already covers selection, and `BrowserView.onAppear` covers the launch case where the manager set `activeTab` directly in `initializeActiveContainerAndTab` without activating it.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed all four copies: BrowserView.swift:253-262 and 268-277, TabItem.swift:141-150, FavTabItem.swift:72-81, on top of activateTab (TabManager.swift:777-785). I checked the deletion is safe: the only two assignments of a non-nil activeTab are initializeActiveContainerAndTab (TabManager.swift:292, no activation, covered by BrowserView.onAppear) and activateTab itself (line 770), so removing the onChange block and the two row blocks leaves every path covered. restoreTransientState's `if browserPage != nil { return }` is what makes the current duplicates harmless rather than any deliberate design.

kept.title: Space deletion wraps synchronous work in a Task and swallows the fetch error next door
kept.evidence: `deleteContainer` opens with `Task { @MainActor in ... }` around a body that is entirely synchronous main-actor work (`PasswordManagerService.deleteEntries` throws but does not await), so the space survives one extra run-loop turn after the user confirms. Separately, `fetchContainers` (line 850-858) catches its fetch error into a bare `// Failed to fetch containers` comment and returns `[]` — in a file whose opening lines exist because "`try?` swallowed the error, so a dropped write only showed up later as a tab or a space that came back wrong". A failed container fetch here reads as "no spaces", which is what `initializeActiveContainerAndTab` turns into a brand-new empty Default space.
kept.user_impact: The deleted space visibly lingers for a frame. A transient fetch failure at launch silently presents the user with an empty browser and a new Default space instead of their tabs.
kept.fix: Lead with the fetchContainers logging, which is the half with user impact; the Task unwrap is cosmetic. Use the file's own wording style: AuraLog.category("Tabs").error("Fetching spaces failed: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)").
kept.verify_reason: Both halves confirmed. deleteContainer (TabManager.swift:337-339) wraps a fully synchronous main-actor body in Task { @MainActor in }; PasswordManagerService.deleteEntries is called with try and no await. fetchContainers (line 850-858) catches into a bare comment and returns [], and initializeActiveContainerAndTab turns an empty result into a new Default space (line 295-297), so a transient fetch failure at launch presents an empty browser. The 'lingers for a frame' claim is not supported (nothing observable changes between the call and the hop, and neither call site at SpaceHeaderRow.swift:259 or ContainerSwitcher.swift:124 runs anything after it), but the async hop is still unnecessary and the swallowed error contradicts the doctrine stated at the top of the same file.

kept.title: Every window installs an UndoManager on its ModelContext that nothing ever undoes
kept.evidence: `self.modelContext.undoManager = UndoManager()` in `TabManager.init`. `grep -rn "undoManager\|undo()" aura/ auraTests/` returns this one line and nothing else: no menu item, no view, no test ever calls `undo()`, `redo()`, `beginUndoGrouping` or reads `modelContext.undoManager`. Core Data (which SwiftData sits on) registers an undo operation for every insert, delete and property change while a context has an undo manager, and NSUndoManager has no level limit by default, so the stack grows for the life of the window. This context is written on every tab switch (`activateTab` sets `lastAccessedAt`, `container.lastAccessedAt`), on every minute tick, on every navigation that touches `url`/`title`, and on every hibernation pass.
kept.user_impact: A browser left open all day accumulates undo groups for tens of thousands of writes, each retaining the changed objects, and never releases them. Pure growth with no feature behind it; the Edit menu's ⌘Z goes to the focused text field's own undo manager, never here.
kept.fix: Delete the line. If per-window undo is ever wanted, it belongs behind a real menu command with `levelsOfUndo` set, not on by default.

kept.title: "Remove tabs after: Never" still removes tabs, because only the sibling pass honours the sentinel
kept.evidence: `cleanupOldTabs` (line 261-264) opens with `guard timeout < 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 else { return }` and the comment `// Skip cleanup if set to "Never" (365 days)`. `removeOldTabs` (line 328-330) has no such guard: it computes `cutoffDate` straight from `SettingsStore.shared.tabRemovalTimeout` and deletes anything older. TabManagementSettingsView.swift:18 offers `("Never", 365 * 24 * 60 * 60)` for both rows, and SettingsStore.swift:637-642 stores that same sentinel for `tabRemovalTimeout`. The deletion runs with `shouldTrackForRestore: false`, so ⌘⇧T cannot bring the tab back.
kept.user_impact: A user who picks "Never" specifically to stop Aura throwing tabs away still loses every normal tab whose `lastAccessedAt` is over a year old, with no undo. `lastAccessedAt` is persisted, so this survives relaunches; it is not a year of uptime.
kept.fix: Mirror the sibling pass at the top of `removeOldTabs`: `let timeout = SettingsStore.shared.tabRemovalTimeout; guard timeout < 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 else { return }`, then build `cutoffDate` from `timeout`.

kept.title: TabContainer.init takes an `isActive` flag it drops on the floor and defaults the emoji to a pile of poo
kept.evidence: `init(id:name:isActive:emoji:iconSymbol:iconColorHex:order:)` at lines 33-51 never assigns `isActive` to anything, and the model has no such property. `emoji: String = "💩"` is the default for a persisted, user-visible space label. The only production caller, `TabManager.createContainer` (TabManager.swift:302-313), passes `ContainerConstants.defaultEmoji` ("•") and no `isActive`, so the defaults survive only in the seven test call sites, which is why nobody has seen the poo emoji in the sidebar.
kept.user_impact: None today, but a space created anywhere that omits `emoji` ships a joke glyph into the sidebar, and a parameter that looks like it sets active state and does nothing is exactly the kind of thing a later caller trusts.
kept.fix: Drop the `isActive` parameter and make the emoji default `ContainerConstants.defaultEmoji`; fix the two or three test call sites that pass `isActive` (none do today, so the parameter can go outright).

dropped.title: Deleting a browsing container is not announced to the other windows
dropped.reason: Could not confirm the premise, and one piece of it is refuted. BrowsingContainer.swift:25 declares @Relationship var tabs: [Tab] with the inverse on Tab.browsingContainer and no cascade, so SwiftData's default nullify rule clears the relationship in the store when the row is deleted; another window's context resolves that to nil rather than a dangling reference, and Tab.storeIdentifier (Tab.swift:74-76) already falls back to BrowserEngine.defaultStoreIdentifier for nil. The remaining verifiable part is that ContainerManager.revision (line 17) is per window, so a second window's settings list can show a deleted container until something else invalidates it, which is cosmetic and only reachable with two windows both showing container settings. Not worth a new notification plus observers.

design-system.summary: The token layer is genuinely good: AuraRadius, AuraShadow, AnimationSettings and the AuraMenu stack are coherent, commented for "why", and covered by tests, and the menu/toast/dialog chrome is real custom design rather than stock AppKit. The gaps are at the edges where the system was not enforced: three modal cards invent their own 11/14pt radii and a 20pt shadow that the Theme comment explicitly forbids, OraButton/OraInput carry a second 8/10/12 radius scale, Settings is still stock checkboxes and pop-up buttons next to that custom chrome, and "About Aura" opens a blocking NSAlert. The one real defect is behavioural: four dialogs draw a ↩ chip on their primary button while nothing in the app binds Return for dialogs opened through DialogManager.show, so pressing Return does nothing on the download-collision, extension-consent and bookmark dialogs.

kept.title: Return chip on dialog primary buttons is dead for every dialog opened with DialogManager.show
kept.evidence: `OraRoot.swift:268` is the only Return binding for dialogs: `if event.keyCode == 36, let onConfirm = dialogManager.dialogs.last?.onConfirm`. `DialogManager.confirm` (DialogManager.swift:79) sets `dialog.onConfirm`, but `DialogManager.show` (line 13) never does. Four dialogs are opened through `show` and still draw a ↩ chip: `DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:53` (`OraButton(label: "Keep both", variant: .default, keyboardShortcut: "return")`, no text field in the whole view), `ExtensionStoreCards.swift:456` (`OraButton(label: "Install", keyboardShortcut: "return")`, no text field), and `BookmarkEditDialog.swift:25` and `:65`, whose fields exist but are never focused (no `@FocusState`, unlike `ContainerForm.swift:24` `.onAppear { isNameFocused = true }`).
kept.user_impact: A download lands on an existing name, the dialog offers "Keep both ↩", the user presses Return and nothing happens; same for extension install consent and for both bookmark dialogs until the user first clicks into a field. The chip promises a key that is not bound.
kept.fix: The `onConfirm:` parameter on `DialogManager.show` is right, but two of the three call sites in the proposed fix are wrong. (1) DownloadManager.swift:335: passing `{ choose(.keepBoth) }` fires `choose` twice, because `.onDisappear` at line 341 calls `choose(answer.value ?? .cancel)` right after and the second call re-enters `enqueue`/`completion`. Pass `{ answer.value = .keepBoth }` instead and let onDisappear deliver it. (2) ExtensionStoreCards.swift:486: `allowsPrivateWindows` is `@State` inside `ExtensionConsentSheet`, not in scope at the `dialogManager.show` call, so no onConfirm closure at that site can read the toggle. Either hoist that toggle to the presenter, or simply drop `keyboardShortcut: "return"` from ExtensionStoreCards.swift:456 so the chip stops promising a key nothing binds. (3) For the two bookmark dialogs, note OraInput's `@FocusState` is private (OraInput.swift:24), so the only precedent is ContainerForm.swift:93, which puts `.focused($isNameFocused)` on the composite OraInput and sets it in `.onAppear` (line 24); copy that exactly, and if focus does not actually move there either, expose a focus binding on OraInput rather than repeating the pattern.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraButton's `keyboardShortcut` is a decorative String only (OraButton.swift:138-157 renders a chip, no `.keyboardShortcut()` modifier anywhere), and OraRoot.swift:268 binds Return only to `dialogs.last?.onConfirm`, which only `DialogManager.confirm` sets (DialogManager.swift:76-80). `show` (line 12-18) never sets it. DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:53 and ExtensionStoreCards.swift:456 draw a return chip with no text field in the view, so Return is dead there. Bookmark dialogs do reach `save` through OraInput's `onSubmit` but only once the field has focus, and neither dialog focuses one. Downgraded from high: Escape still works (DownloadManager.swift:341 `.onDisappear { choose(answer.value ?? .cancel) }`), the buttons are still clickable and nothing is lost, so this is a broken promise rather than a stuck state.

kept.title: Three modal cards use an 11/14pt radius and a 20pt shadow the shared dialog forbids
kept.evidence: `BookmarkDialogCard` ends with `.cornerRadius(11)` / `stroke(theme.border, lineWidth: 0.5)` / `.cornerRadius(14)` / `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 20, y: 8)` (lines 110-118), and its own doc comment two lines above claims "no shadow beyond the one a floating Aura surface may carry". `EditContainerModal.swift:32-41` and `NewContainerButton.swift:101-110` repeat the same four values. `ConfirmDialogView` (DialogView.swift:59-68) and `DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:64-73) use `AuraRadius.row` / `AuraRadius.pane`, `lineWidth: 1` and `.auraFloatingShadow()`, and `Theme.swift:30` states "at most this much shadow. Anything larger reads as a different elevation model".
kept.user_impact: Open "Edit Bookmark" and then "Delete Space" back to back and the two cards sit at different elevations with different corner curvature and a fainter hairline, on the same dark backdrop.
kept.fix: In all three, replace `.cornerRadius(11)` with `.cornerRadius(AuraRadius.row)`, `ConditionallyConcentricRectangle(cornerRadius: 11).stroke(theme.border, lineWidth: 0.5)` with `lineWidth: 1`, `.cornerRadius(14)` with `.cornerRadius(AuraRadius.pane)` and the `.shadow(...)` line with `.auraFloatingShadow()`. Delete the now-accurate comment claim or leave it, it becomes true.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed verbatim in all three files: BookmarkEditDialog.swift:110-118, EditContainerModal.swift:32-41, NewContainerButton.swift:101-110 all use 11/0.5/14 and `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 20, y: 8)`, while ConfirmDialogView (DialogView.swift:57-67) and DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:63-73 use AuraRadius.row/pane, lineWidth 1 and `.auraFloatingShadow()`. Theme.swift:22 and :30 state both rules, and BookmarkDialogCard's own comment at :85-86 claims the shadow it then draws is absent. These are the only literal `.cornerRadius(n)` calls in the app besides OraButton's chip and the launcher's 99pt pill.

kept.title: Cancel shows a lowercase "esc" word chip next to a ⏎ glyph chip on every dialog
kept.evidence: `let systemIcons = ["return", "command", "shift", "control", "option", "escape", "delete.left"]` — the list holds "escape", but all eight call sites pass `keyboardShortcut: "esc"` (DialogView.swift:45, DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:45, EditContainerModal.swift:74, NewContainerButton.swift:85, ExtensionStoreCards.swift:454, BookmarkEditDialog.swift:20 and :60). So Cancel falls into the `Text(shortcut.lowercased()).opacity(0.5)` branch while the neighbouring Confirm draws `Image(systemName: "return")` at full strength.
kept.user_impact: Every dialog footer pairs a faded three-letter word with a crisp symbol, so the two buttons read as different kinds of control.
kept.fix: One line in OraButton: `let symbolName = shortcut == "esc" ? "escape" : shortcut` and test/draw with `symbolName` (keep `shortcut` for the width rule). Drop the `.opacity(0.5)` from the text branch so the two chips share one weight.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraButton.swift:141 lists "escape" but all seven Cancel call sites pass "esc" (DialogView.swift:45, DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:45, EditContainerModal.swift:74, NewContainerButton.swift:84, ExtensionStoreCards.swift:454, BookmarkEditDialog.swift:20 and :60), so Cancel takes the `Text(shortcut.lowercased()).opacity(0.5)` branch next to a full-strength `Image(systemName: "return")`. Dropping the opacity is safe: "esc" and "return" are the only two values passed anywhere in the app.

kept.title: Settings draws stock AppKit checkboxes while the extension cards draw switches
kept.evidence: `SettingsCard` renders `content()` in a plain `VStack`, so a bare `Toggle("Block fingerprinting", isOn:)` (PrivacySettingsView.swift:173, and ~30 more across LookAndFeel, Passwords, TabManagement, Spaces, About) falls back to the system checkbox with the system blue accent, ignoring `theme.accent`. `ExtensionStoreCards.swift:98, 211, 256, 448` all set `.toggleStyle(.switch).controlSize(.small)`, and `SitePermissionPromptView.swift:23` sets `.toggleStyle(.checkbox)` explicitly.
kept.user_impact: The same on/off idea appears as a blue system checkbox in Settings and as a switch in the extension store, and neither follows the chosen accent colour, so Settings reads as a different app from the chrome.
kept.fix: Drop `.controlSize(.small)` from the proposed change. controlSize propagates to every control in the card, and the settings cards also contain Sliders (AccessibilitySettingsView.swift:23, GlassSettingsCard.swift:71), Steppers (TabManagementSettingsView.swift:34), Pickers (TabManagementSettingsView.swift:46/63/79) and TextFields, all of which would shrink. Apply only `.toggleStyle(.switch)` and `.tint(theme.accent)` to `content()`. Also leave ExtensionStoreCards alone: its toggles use `.mini` and `.small` deliberately and are not inside a SettingsCard.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: SettingsCard.swift:28 renders `content()` with no style applied, and every settings toggle sits inside a SettingsCard (checked PrivacySettingsView.swift:168-175, AccessibilitySettingsView.swift:9-38, DataPortabilityViews.swift:120), so they render as system checkboxes with the system blue while ExtensionStoreCards.swift:98/211/256/448 render switches. ToggleStyle and tint both propagate through the environment, so the one-file fix works.

kept.title: "About Aura" opens a blocking stock NSAlert even though a designed About page exists
kept.evidence: `private func showAboutWindow() { let alert = NSAlert(); alert.messageText = "Aura Browser"; ... alert.addButton(withTitle: "OK"); alert.runModal() }`, wired at line 323 `Button("About Aura") { showAboutWindow() }`. Meanwhile `SettingsTab.about` exists (SettingsContentView.swift:18, title "About Aura") and `AboutSettingsView` already shows the version, the update state and the auto-update toggle.
kept.user_impact: The first thing a curious user clicks in the app menu is a grey system alert with the generic app icon and a "© 2025 Aura Browser" string, which also blocks the main run loop until dismissed.
kept.fix: The post alone regresses the no-window case: OraRoot.swift:461 claims `.openSettingsTab` with scope `.windowOrKey`, so with every browser window closed (Aura still running) nothing happens, where the NSAlert did show. Guard it: `if NSApp.keyWindow == nil { WindowFactory.openWindow(with: .oraSettings(section: .about)) } else { NotificationCenter.default.post(...) }` — `URL.oraSettings(section:)` is already there (URL+Ora.swift:120) and `WindowFactory.openWindow(with:)` at WindowFactory.swift:49. The existing Settings menu item (OraCommands.swift:333) has the same hole, so fixing both is one shared helper.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraCommands.swift:323 `Button("About Aura") { showAboutWindow() }` and :342-353 build and `runModal()` an NSAlert, while SettingsTab.about exists and UpdateDriver.swift:208-212 already posts `.openSettingsTab` with `userInfo: ["tab": SettingsTab.about.rawValue]`, so the designed route is one line away.

kept.title: Opening the space icon picker parses 584 KB of emoji JSON on the main thread every time
kept.evidence: `EmojiViewModel.init()` calls `loadEmojis()`, which does `Data(contentsOf: url)` plus `JSONSerialization.jsonObject` plus `EmojiVariants.group` synchronously (lines 78-115). `aura/Shared/EmojiPicker/emoji-set.json` is 584,224 bytes. `SpaceIconPicker.swift:18` holds `@StateObject private var emojiModel = EmojiViewModel()`, and the picker is built fresh inside `ContainerForm.swift:55`'s `.popover`, so every open of the picker re-parses the file on the main actor.
kept.user_impact: The icon popover hangs for a beat before its first frame, every single time it is opened, and it does that even when the user only wants the Icons tab, which never touches the emoji set.
kept.fix: Worth naming that `isLoading` (line 69) is published but no view ever reads it, so there is not even a spinner to cover the stall. A `private static let catalog: [EmojiCategory]` is safe here: EmojiCategory/EmojiItem hold only UUID/String/[String], so they are implicitly Sendable and a `static let` gets thread-safe one-shot initialisation. Keep `error` as a static too, as proposed.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: emoji-set.json is 584,224 bytes, EmojiViewModel.init (EmojiPickerModel.swift:74-76) calls loadEmojis, which does Data(contentsOf:) + JSONSerialization + EmojiVariants.group synchronously (78-115). SpaceIconPicker.swift:18 holds it in @StateObject and the picker is constructed inside ContainerForm.swift:55's `.popover`, so a fresh model (and a fresh parse) is built on every open, on the main thread, even when the user only wants the Icons tab.

kept.title: Reduce motion ignores the system accessibility setting
kept.evidence: `private static let cachedReduceMotion = OSAllocatedUnfairLock(initialState: UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: SettingsStore.reduceMotionKey))` — the only source is Aura's own `a11y.reduceMotion` default, set from the toggle in `AccessibilitySettingsView.swift:14`. Nothing reads `NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`.
kept.user_impact: A user who turned Reduce Motion on in System Settings still gets every sidebar, launcher, toast and dialog animation until they find Aura's private copy of the switch.
kept.fix: Seeding is not enough on its own: the system switch can flip while Aura runs, and the cached value would go stale until relaunch. Also observe `NSWorkspace.shared.notificationCenter` for `NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayOptionsDidChangeNotification` and re-derive with the same OR, so both switches can only add motion suppression, never remove it.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: AnimationSettings.swift:7-8 seeds only from `SettingsStore.reduceMotionKey`, and a grep for accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion across aura/ returns nothing. The app's own toggle (AccessibilitySettingsView.swift:14) is the only input.

kept.title: The custom colour picker ends in a stock rounded-bezel text field
kept.evidence: `TextField("#RRGGBB", text: $hexField).textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder).font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))` — the only `.roundedBorder` in the app. The file's own header says it exists because `ColorPicker`/`NSColorPanel` "ignore Aura's styling", and every other field in the app is `.plain` inside a themed fill (`OraInput.swift:120`, `SettingsContentView.swift:373`, `EmojiPickerView.swift:82`).
kept.user_impact: The Liquid Glass tint picker is a hand-drawn HSV square and two custom bars sitting on top of a system-bezel field with system focus ring, at a font size nothing else in the app uses.
kept.fix: Fix all three in the same pass, otherwise the app keeps two field looks anyway. For the hex row, `OraInput(text: $hexField, placeholder: "#RRGGBB", size: .sm, onSubmit: applyHexField)` loses the monospaced digits; if those matter, keep the TextField with `.textFieldStyle(.plain)` on `theme.mutedBackground` at `AuraRadius.button` with a `theme.border` hairline, and use `.font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced))` rather than `.body` so it stops being the one body-sized field in the app.
kept.verify_reason: The defect is real (AuraColorPicker.swift:176-178 uses `.roundedBorder` plus `.font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))` inside a hand-drawn HSV panel whose header at :4-5 says it exists precisely because system pickers ignore Aura's styling), but the evidence overstates it: this is not the only `.roundedBorder` in the app. BrowsingSettingsView.swift:62 and PasswordVaultView.swift:77 use it too. One stock field inside one picker is cosmetic, so low rather than medium.

kept.title: Space icon picker: stock segmented control, raw red error text, no empty state
kept.evidence: Line 45-48 `Picker("", selection: $mode) { ... }.pickerStyle(.segmented)` is a system NSSegmentedControl inside an otherwise hand-drawn 400x400 panel. Line 67 `Text("Error: \(error)").foregroundColor(.red)` uses a developer prefix and `.red` rather than `theme.destructive`. `symbolGrid` (line 102) renders `SpaceIconCatalog.search(search)` and `EmojiGridView` renders `viewModel.filteredEmojis` with no branch for an empty result.
kept.user_impact: Typing "zzz" in the picker leaves a blank 340pt void with no explanation, and the two mode buttons are the one piece of stock macOS in the whole space-creation flow.
kept.fix: Two details: bind `SpaceIconCatalog.search(search)` to a local `let results` and use it for both the grid and the empty branch, otherwise the search runs twice per body pass. And put the emoji empty state inside EmojiGridView next to `viewModel.filteredEmojis` rather than in SpaceIconPicker, so the grid owns its own empty case.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: SpaceIconPicker.swift:45-49 is a stock segmented Picker inside a hand-drawn 400x400 panel, :67 renders `Text("Error: \(error)").foregroundColor(.red)` with a developer prefix and a raw red instead of theme.destructive, and neither symbolGrid (:102-121) nor EmojiGridView (EmojiPickerView.swift:14-22) has an empty branch, so a query with no hits leaves a blank panel. `categoryRow` (:125-143) is the in-house button pattern the segmented control should follow.

kept.title: Toasts are invisible to VoiceOver and their close button has no label
kept.evidence: `Button(action: onDismiss) { Image(systemName: "xmark") ... }` with no `.accessibilityLabel`, and the toast row itself carries no accessibility traits or live-region hint (lines 133-164). `AuraMenuPanel.swift:91` shows the codebase's own pattern (`.accessibilityLabel(Text(item.title))`), and `TabItem.swift:163` does the same for tab rows.
kept.user_impact: "Download failed", "Cookies cleared" and every other confirmation never reaches a VoiceOver user, and the close button reads as "button".
kept.fix: Do not add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` to the outer HStack: combining swallows the close Button, so VoiceOver loses the only way to dismiss the toast. Add `.accessibilityLabel(Text("Dismiss"))` to the close Button and the `.onAppear` announcement post on the HStack, and leave the children as they are.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: ToastView.swift:146-152 has no accessibilityLabel on the close Button, and nothing in ToastItemView (133-164) announces the message.
