"Invisible to VoiceOver" is a slight overstatement — the message is a plain Text and is reachable by navigation — but a toast that auto-dismisses is gone before a VoiceOver user navigates to it, so in practice it never reaches them.

kept.title: OraButton and OraInput carry a second radius scale (8/10/12) beside AuraRadius
kept.evidence: `private var cornerRadius: CGFloat { switch size { case .sm: 8; case .md: 10; case .lg: 12 } }` in OraButton, repeated verbatim in `OraInput.swift:52`, plus a bare `.cornerRadius(4)` on the shortcut chip (OraButton.swift:155). `Theme.swift:22` states "Every surface picks one of these; a literal radius anywhere else is a bug. Buttons and chips 6, rows/fields/cards/menus/overlays 10, panes 13."
kept.user_impact: A dialog's Save button (10) is rounder than a toolbar button (6) and its inner shortcut chip (4) is squarer than both, so a single dialog footer shows three curvatures the scale does not contain.
kept.fix: Split by role instead of by size, which is what the scale actually says: every OraButton size maps to `AuraRadius.button`, every OraInput size maps to `AuraRadius.row`, and the chip takes `AuraRadius.button`. Mapping `.lg` to `AuraRadius.row` as proposed just reintroduces a size-dependent scale. Note this shrinks the dialog Save/Cancel curvature from 10 to 6, which is the intended alignment with the toolbar but is a visible change; check the dialog footers once after.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: OraButton.swift:62-68 and OraInput.swift:52-58 each hold an 8/10/12 scale and OraButton.swift:155 hard-codes `.cornerRadius(4)` on the chip, against Theme.swift:22 saying a literal radius anywhere else is a bug. It is a genuine second scale, but the visible effect is a couple of points of curvature on dialog buttons, so low rather than medium.

kept.title: Eight icon shape files and two registry cases are never drawn (~870 lines of dead vector art)
kept.evidence: Only `.spaceCards` (4 sites), `.copy` (ClipboardUtils.swift:42, PasswordVaultView.swift:349) and `.brush1` (HistoryPanelView.swift:80, DownloadsHistoryView.swift:54) are referenced outside `OraIcon.swift`. `.star` and `.circle` appear only in the `#Preview`; `.spaceCardsDelete`, `.spaceCardsEdit`, `.autofill`, `.brush2`, `.downloadBox`, `.downloadBox2`, `.shieldLock`, `.shieldBan` appear nowhere else, and neither do their shape types (`AutofillIcon`, `ShieldBanIcon`, `Brush2`, `DownloadBox`, `DownloadBox2`, `ShieldLockIcon`, `SpaceCardsDeleteIcon`, `SpaceCardsEditIcon`), 864 lines across eight files.
kept.user_impact: None at runtime; it is dead weight that makes the icon registry look like a shipped set when three of thirteen entries are real.
kept.fix: Delete the eight unused shape files and their `OraIconType` cases, keep `.star`/`.circle` only if the preview is worth it (otherwise drop them and trim the preview to the icons in use).
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by per-case grep across aura/ and auraTests/: spaceCardsDelete, spaceCardsEdit, autofill, brush2, downloadBox, downloadBox2, shieldLock, shieldBan have zero references outside OraIcon.swift (the one `.autofill` hit is `passwordCoordinator?.autofill(...)`, unrelated), and `.star`/`.circle` appear only in the #Preview at OraIcon.swift:118-136. The eight files total 864 lines exactly.

kept.title: Theme's "Search engine colors" block is dead and duplicates SearchEngineService
kept.evidence: Lines 151-191 define `grok`, `claude`, `openai`, `t3chat`, `perplexity`, `reddit`, `x` (with a `// swiftlint:disable:next identifier_name`), `google`, `youtube`, `github`. `rg "theme\.(grok|claude|openai|t3chat|perplexity|reddit|youtube|github)"` and `rg "theme\.x\b"` return nothing across aura/ and auraTests/. The live values live in `SearchEngineService.swift:87-213` (`color: Color(hex: "#FC0D1B")` and friends).
kept.user_impact: None visible; it is a second, silently diverging copy of the engine palette inside the theme token file, and it is the reason a lint suppression sits in Theme.swift.
kept.fix: Delete lines 151-191 (including the swiftlint suppression). The engine colours already have one home in `SearchEngineService`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: Theme.swift:151-191 defines the ten engine colours including the swiftlint suppression at :176, and no `theme.<engine>` reference exists in aura/ or auraTests/ (the `.grok`/`.claude` hits in LauncherViewModel.swift:154-156 are engine-name enum cases, not theme properties). SearchEngineService holds the live palette.

kept.title: GradientAnimatingBorder is a retired no-op modifier with a live public entry point
kept.evidence: The whole type is `struct GradientAnimatingBorder: ViewModifier { let color: Color; let trigger: Bool; func body(content: Content) -> some View { content } }` under the comment "Retired: the launcher's animated gradient sweep is gone". `View+Modifiers.swift:4` still exports `func gradientAnimatingBorder(color:trigger:)`, and nothing in aura/ calls it.
kept.user_impact: None; it is a decoy API that reads as a working effect.
kept.fix: Delete `GradientAnimatingBorder.swift` and the `gradientAnimatingBorder` extension in `View+Modifiers.swift`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: GradientAnimatingBorder.swift:4-11 returns `content` untouched under a "Retired" comment, and the only reference to `gradientAnimatingBorder` in the whole repo is its own declaration at View+Modifiers.swift:4.

kept.title: Four user-facing strings use "..." where the rest of the app uses "…"
kept.evidence: `placeholder: "eg. work, streaming, finance..."` here, `"Search files..."` (DownloadsHistoryView.swift:78), `"Search history..."` (HistoryPanelView.swift:105) and `isAuthenticating ? "Unlocking..." : "Unlock Passwords"` (PasswordVaultView.swift:199). Everything else uses the real ellipsis: "New Space…", "Edit…", "Import HTML…", "Save Page As…", and `OraInput`'s own previews say "Search…".
kept.user_impact: Three dots render wider and looser than the ellipsis used two rows away, and "eg." is not how the abbreviation is spelled.
kept.fix: While in the area, EmojiPickerView.swift:81 uses the bare placeholder "Search" where the rest of the app writes "Search…"; folding it in keeps the sweep to one pass.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed, exactly four sites: ContainerForm.swift:90, PasswordVaultView.swift:199, HistoryPanelView.swift:105, DownloadsHistoryView.swift:78, against 62 uses of the real ellipsis elsewhere including every menu item that opens a dialog.

kept.title: Menu shortcut hints for rebindable actions are hard-coded strings
kept.evidence: `.item("Back", icon: "chevron.left", shortcut: "⌘[", ...)`, `"Forward"` with `"⌘]"` (line 36), `"Reload"` with `"⌘R"` (line 39), and `URLBarMenuButton.swift:163` `"Show All History"` with `"⌘Y"`. All four have rebindable definitions (`KeyboardShortcuts.Navigation.back/.forward/.reload` at KeyboardShortcuts.swift:133-150, `KeyboardShortcuts.History.show` at :237), and `AuraMenuItem.item(_:icon:shortcut:)` already has the overload that takes a `KeyboardShortcutDefinition` "so a rebind shows up here too" (AuraMenuItem.swift:71).
kept.user_impact: A user who rebinds Reload in Settings still sees ⌘R in the page context menu, so the menu teaches the wrong key. Cut/Copy/Paste literals are fine, those are not rebindable.
kept.fix: Swap the four literals for the definition overload: `shortcut: KeyboardShortcuts.Navigation.back` etc.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PageContextMenu.swift:33/36/39 pass literal "⌘[", "⌘]", "⌘R" and URLBarMenuButton.swift:163 passes "⌘Y", while KeyboardShortcuts.Navigation.back/.forward/.reload (KeyboardShortcuts.swift:133-150) and History.show (:237-242) are rebindable and AuraMenuItem.swift:71-87 already provides the definition overload, which also carries `isDisabled` so the back/forward rows keep their disabled state.

kept.title: No type scale beside the radius and shadow scales, so one-off font sizes drift in
kept.evidence: `AuraRadius` and `AuraShadow` are enumerated tokens, but text sizes are 268 literals across 72 files: 11pt (114), 13pt (58), 12pt (37), 14pt (14), 10pt (13) carry almost everything, while 8, 9, 12.5 (AuraMenuPanel.swift:117), 15, 26, 28 and 30 appear once or twice each. Dialog headings alone are 22 (DialogView.swift:29, EditContainerModal.swift:50, DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:29) and 18 (BookmarkEditDialog.swift:99).
kept.user_impact: Two dialogs opened in a row have differently sized titles, and the odd 12.5 and 9pt glyphs read as accidents next to the tight 10/11/12/13 rhythm.
kept.fix: Do not add an AuraFont enum that only three files use. A token enum nothing else adopts is a third scale next to the 268 literals, not a fix. Ship the verified corrections only — BookmarkDialogCard 18 → 22, AuraMenuPanel 12.5 → 13, OraInput's `fontSize - 0.5` → `fontSize - 1` — and raise the full type scale as its own task, where the enum lands together with a sweep of all 72 files.
kept.verify_reason: The concrete part checks out: dialog headings are 22 at DialogView.swift:29, EditContainerModal.swift:50 and DownloadCollisionDialog.swift:29 but 18 at BookmarkEditDialog.swift:98, and half-point sizes exist at AuraMenuPanel.swift:117 (12.5) and OraInput.swift:102 (fontSize - 0.5). The broader "add a type scale" part is a proposal, not a defect.

kept.title: OraButton's leading icon ignores labelColor, so it does not dim when the button is disabled
kept.evidence: `if let icon = leadingIcon { Image(systemName: icon).font(.system(size: fontSize - 1, weight: .medium)) }` — no `.foregroundColor(labelColor)`, unlike the trailing icon at line 132-136 and the `Text` at line 128-130. `labelColor` returns `theme.disabledForeground` when `isDisabled`.
kept.user_impact: `PasswordVaultView.swift:197` disables the button while authenticating: the label greys out to "Unlocking…" but the Touch ID glyph beside it stays at full strength. On a `.default` (accent) button a leading icon would also inherit the ambient colour instead of white.
kept.fix: Add `.foregroundColor(labelColor)` to the leading `Image`, matching the trailing one.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed at OraButton.swift:123-126: the leading Image has no `.foregroundColor(labelColor)` while the trailing one (:132-136) and the Text (:128-130) do. Raised from low because the worst case is not the Touch ID button: DataPortabilityViews.swift:255-266 is a `.destructive` OraButton with `leadingIcon: "square.and.arrow.up"`, so in light appearance the glyph inherits the ambient primary (black) and draws black on the red fill beside white text, and it stays at full strength while the button is disabled (which is the default state, `passwords.entries.isEmpty`).

kept.title: ContainerConstants holds five dead constants and a duplicate of AuraRadius.row
kept.evidence: `static let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 10` is the same number as `AuraRadius.row` and is used at ContainerForm.swift:32, 45, 63, 64 for a 32pt icon button that the scale would put at `AuraRadius.button`. `popoverWidth`, `minDialogHeight`, `defaultTabAliveTimeout`, `defaultTabRemovalTimeout` and `Animation.hoverDuration` have no references outside this file (`Animation.emojiPickerDuration` has exactly one, ContainerForm.swift:40).
kept.user_impact: None visible; it keeps a second, stale copy of the radius and animation scales alive next to the real ones.
kept.fix: Use `AuraRadius.row`, not `AuraRadius.button`, at the four ContainerForm sites. That button is a 32pt icon well sitting directly beside the OraInput name field, which is on the row radius; dropping it to 6 while its neighbour stays at 10 makes the pair worse, not better.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by per-constant grep: popoverWidth, minDialogHeight, defaultTabAliveTimeout, defaultTabRemovalTimeout and Animation.hoverDuration have zero references outside ContainerConstants.swift; emojiPickerDuration has exactly one (ContainerForm.swift:40); UI.cornerRadius is used only at ContainerForm.swift:32/45/63/64.

kept.title: InteractiveButtonStyle has no disabled state, so a busy toolbar pill looks clickable
kept.evidence: `let opacity = configuration.isPressed ? pressOpacity : (isHovering ? hoverOpacity : 0)` — the style never reads `@Environment(\.isEnabled)`. `URLBarButton.swift:46` works around it by hand (`.opacity(isEnabled ? Self.enabledOpacity : Self.disabledOpacity)`), but `UpdatePill` (TopToolbar.swift:346-360) sets `.foregroundColor(theme.accent)` and `.disabled(updateService.phase.buttonAction == .busy)` with no dimming.
kept.user_impact: While an update downloads, the "Downloading 42%" pill stays at full accent strength and looks like a live button, so the user clicks it and nothing happens.
kept.fix: The proposed global change double-dims three existing hand-rolled treatments: URLBarButton.swift:46 (`enabledOpacity` 0.7 / `disabledOpacity` 0.35), FindView.swift:126 (`theme.disabledForeground`) and GlobalMediaPlayer.swift:114/126 (`controlGlyph(isEnabled:)`). If the style gains the dimming, strip those three in the same commit (URLBarButton keeps only `enabledOpacity`); files_to_touch becomes InteractiveButtonStyle.swift, URLBarButton.swift, FindView.swift, GlobalMediaPlayer.swift. If that diff is too wide for the payoff, the honest one-line version is `.opacity(updateService.phase.buttonAction == .busy ? 0.5 : 1)` on the pill alone.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: InteractiveButtonStyle.HoverBody (InteractiveButtonStyle.swift:23-43) never reads `\.isEnabled`, and UpdatePill (TopToolbar.swift:345-361) sets `.foregroundColor(theme.accent)` with `.disabled(...)` and no dimming. Impact is mild, though: the pill's own label reads "Downloading 42%", so the state is communicated even without the dimming.

kept.title: Toast stack has an opacity condition that can never be true
kept.evidence: `.opacity(depth >= maxVisible ? 0 : 1)` where `let visible = Array(manager.toasts.suffix(maxVisible))` (line 49) and `let depth = visible.count - 1 - index` (line 53), so `depth` is at most `maxVisible - 1`.
kept.user_impact: None; it is a leftover guard that suggests the stack renders hidden rows it does not.
kept.fix: Delete the `.opacity(...)` line.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: ToastView.swift:49 takes `suffix(maxVisible)` and :53 computes `depth = visible.count - 1 - index`, so depth tops out at maxVisible - 1 and the `depth >= maxVisible` test at :66 is never true.

kept.title: Password autofill trigger is painted in two hard-coded greys
kept.evidence: `.foregroundStyle(Color(hex: "#4A4A4A"))` and `.fill(Color(hex: "#EFEFEF").opacity(isHovering ? 1 : 0.7))` with no comment. These are the only literal hex colours in the app outside `Theme`, `SearchEngineService`'s brand list and `SpaceIconCatalog.palette`.
kept.user_impact: The key button sits on the page, so on a dark site it is a light grey chip with dark glyph pasted onto black, and it never follows the theme or the appearance.
kept.fix: Do not route it through `theme.popoverBackground`: on a dark page in dark appearance that paints a dark chip on a dark field and the affordance disappears, which is worse than today. Keep the fixed light chip (it is the same choice Safari's autofill mark makes), add the one-line comment naming why the chrome theme does not reach here, and replace the local `private let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 6` at :136 with `AuraRadius.button` so at least the radius comes from the scale.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: PasswordAutofillOverlayView.swift:147 and :152 are the only literal hexes outside Theme, SearchEngineService and SpaceIconCatalog.palette, and there is no comment saying why. The chip does sit on page content rather than chrome, so a fixed light treatment is defensible; what is missing is the reason, not the colours.

kept.title: Glass chrome recolours only `foreground`, so every secondary label keeps the appearance colour
kept.evidence: `GlassChrome` (AuraGlass.swift:157) overrides the environment theme with `theme.withForeground(chromeForeground)`, and `Theme.foreground` (Theme.swift:70-71) honours `forcedForeground`. `mutedForeground` (:111-113 `.secondary`), `disabledForeground` (:119-121), `placeholder` (:127-129) and `border` (:131-133) ignore it and stay keyed to the system appearance. Chrome that uses them inside the glass scope: BookmarksBar.swift:87 (`emptyHint`, under `.auraGlassChromeForeground()` at :66) and SidebarView.swift:434/443 (the sidebar empty state, under the same modifier at :89).
kept.user_impact: Turn Liquid Glass on in dark appearance and pick a light tint: the chrome flips to black text as designed, but the bookmarks bar hint "Drag the address bar's icon here to keep a page" and the sidebar empty-state subtitle stay in the dark-mode secondary grey, so they sit near-invisible on the now-light chrome. The same holds in reverse for a dark tint under light appearance.
kept.fix: Derive the muted tokens from the forced colour when one is set, in the same file that already owns the override: `var mutedForeground: Color { forcedForeground.map { $0.opacity(0.6) } ?? .secondary }`, and the same shape for `disabledForeground` (opacity 0.35) and `placeholder` (opacity 0.45). Comment the why: the glass foreground is chosen against the tint's luminance, so anything derived from it has to follow, not fall back to the appearance.

kept.title: Dialogs are not modal to VoiceOver, so the page behind stays reachable
kept.evidence: `DialogsOverlay` (DialogView.swift:100-126) paints `Color.black.opacity(0.4)` plus `DialogContentView` as an overlay on the browser content. Neither carries `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)` and the backdrop is not hidden, so the whole page and chrome behind a "Delete Space" confirmation stay in the accessibility tree. The app knows the pattern elsewhere: AuraMenuPanel.swift:40 sets `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` on the menu panel.
kept.user_impact: A VoiceOver user answering the quit or delete confirmation can rotor straight past it into the tab list and the page underneath, which are inert to the pointer but still announced, and there is nothing telling them a dialog is open.
kept.fix: On `DialogContentView` add `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)` and on the backdrop `Color` add `.accessibilityHidden(true)`, both inside the `if let dialog = dialogs.last` branch so they come and go with the dialog.

kept.title: OraButton's shortcut chip is read aloud as part of the button label
kept.evidence: The chip Group (OraButton.swift:144-157) is a plain `Text`/`Image` inside the Button's label with no `.accessibilityHidden(true)`, so SwiftUI folds it into the derived label. Every dialog Cancel therefore announces as "Cancel esc" and every confirm as "Save return" (the SF Symbol contributes its own description).
kept.user_impact: VoiceOver reads a hint glyph as if it were part of the button's name on all seven dialogs, and the key it names is not even bound for the dialogs opened through `DialogManager.show`.
kept.fix: Add `.accessibilityHidden(true)` to the chip `Group` at OraButton.swift:150 (after `.foregroundColor(labelColor)`), so the chip stays a visual hint only.

kept.title: EmojiPicker ships its own SearchBar that re-implements OraInput
kept.evidence: `SearchBar` (EmojiPickerView.swift:72-93) draws a magnifyingglass Image plus a `.plain` TextField on `theme.mutedBackground` at `AuraRadius.row` with a `theme.border` hairline. That is exactly `OraInput(variant:leadingIcon:)` (OraInput.swift:106-139), which the three other search fields in the app already use (HistoryPanelView.swift:105-107, DownloadsHistoryView.swift:78-80, BookmarksSettingsView.swift:87). The copy differs in the details: no focus ring, no placeholder ellipsis, fixed 8pt padding against OraInput's size scale.
kept.user_impact: The icon picker's search field is the one search field in the app that does not brighten its border on focus, so typing into it gives no focus feedback while every other search field in the app does.
kept.fix: Replace `SearchBar(text: $search)` at SpaceIconPicker.swift:51 with `OraInput(text: $search, placeholder: "Search…", size: .sm, leadingIcon: "magnifyingglass")` and delete the `SearchBar` type. Check for other callers first — `SearchBar` is a non-private type in a shared folder.

dropped.title: Glass menus force a foreground computed against the window background while frosting the page
dropped.reason: The mechanism is real (AuraMenuSurface at AuraMenuPanel.swift:145-146 is the only `.withinWindow` caller, and AuraGlass.blended at :68-69 blends over `Theme(colorScheme:).background`, not over the page behind the panel), but the proposed fix does not fix the stated symptom. In dark appearance the forced foreground resolves to white for any tint dark enough to matter, and `theme.foreground` without the override is also white, so removing the override changes nothing in exactly the case described. If the panel really does wash out over a bright page, the fix is an opaque base under the glass sheet, not a foreground change, and I could not confirm the washout by reading alone.

launcher.summary: The launcher's ranking and merge layer is the strongest part of this area: ported from Beam with attribution, covered by real tests, and the two Aura-specific rules (typed text owns row 0, late engine results never move the focused row) are enforced and pinned. The chrome around it is where the rough edges live: opening a page from a suggestion row hands the new tab a fallback DownloadManager with no toast or dialog stack, the suggestion list's hover highlight never fires because nothing makes the window accept mouse-moved events, ⌘T is silently dropped when the Passwords window is key, and the panel is cut off screen instead of fading out. The ⌘T focus complaint is being fixed in the working tree right now (no-toggle plus a focus token), but two of its causes are still there: a dead SwiftUI FocusState path racing the AppKit one, and a first-responder lock the home page takes and never gives back.

kept.title: Pages opened from a suggestion row get a fallback DownloadManager, so their downloads are invisible
kept.evidence: `typedURLSuggestion` (310-316) and `historySuggestions` (413-419) call `tabManager.openTab(url:historyManager:isPrivate:)` with no `downloadManager`, even though the view model holds one (`private(set) var downloadManager: DownloadManager?`) and `openTabSuggestions` uses it. `TabManager.openTab` builds the `Tab` with `downloadManager: nil` and then `activateTab` fills it in with `tab.downloadManager ?? fallbackDownloadManager` (TabManager.swift:781), a second manager built lazily inside `TabManager` (TabManager.swift:111). Only the window's own manager is wired up: `OraRoot.start()` sets `downloadManager.toastManager = toastManager` and `downloadManager.dialogManager = dialogManager`. `DownloadManager.activeDownloads` is per-instance in-memory state and the downloads panel reads `@Environment(DownloadManager.self)`. `TabManager.openFromEngine` (TabManager.swift:210), the AI rows' action, has the same omission.
kept.user_impact: Open a page from the launcher's history or typed-address row, then download a file from it: no download toast, no progress in the downloads panel or on the downloads button, and a name collision silently keeps both files instead of asking (`askAboutCollision` falls back to `.keepBoth` with no dialog manager). This is the launcher's most common action, so it is most of the browser's downloads.
kept.fix: Fix stands. Two checks I ran that make it safe: TabManager.init (:116-140) never builds a web view (initializeActiveContainerAndTab only sets activeTab), and BrowserView.onAppear restores the active tab with the real manager, so nothing touches the lazy var before OraRoot.start() assigns it. Put the assignment next to the existing two lines at OraRoot.swift:214-216, before the initialURL open at :222. fallbackHistoryManager has the same shape but no observable consequence, so leave it.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed end to end. LauncherViewModel.swift:310-316 and :413-419 call openTab without downloadManager; TabManager.openTab:572 passes it into Tab(downloadManager: nil); activateTab (TabManager.swift:781) substitutes fallbackDownloadManager (:111), and TabBrowserPageDelegate.swift:476 routes WKDownload to tab.downloadManager, i.e. the spare instance. Only the window's own manager gets toastManager/dialogManager (OraRoot.swift:214-216), and DownloadManager.activeDownloads/recentDownloads (:8-9) are per instance, which is what the sidebar widget and downloads panel read from the environment. openFromEngine (TabManager.swift:200-209) has the same gap. The rows still land in SwiftData, so the file downloads and appears in history, but there is no toast, no live progress and no collision prompt (askAboutCollision falls back to .keepBoth at :327-329).

kept.title: ⌘T does nothing while the Passwords window is key
kept.evidence: The New Tab item posts `.showLauncher, object: NSApp.keyWindow`. `PasswordsWindow.swift:44` opens a plain `NSWindow` titled "Passwords" that becomes key. `WindowEventScope.windowOrKey.accepts` (OraRoot.swift:330-333) resolves a non-nil sender as `sender === (window ?? keyWindow)`, and every browser root has its own non-nil `window`, so no root claims a post addressed to the Passwords window. `AppDelegate.browserWindow(in:)` exists for exactly this case, with the comment "Settings and utility windows cannot receive navigation events" (OraApp.swift:79-86).
kept.user_impact: ⌘T is dead in the Passwords window: no launcher, no new tab, no beep, nothing. That is one of the reported "sometimes ⌘T does not open the launcher" cases, and Safari and Chrome both open a tab in the frontmost browser window instead.
kept.fix: Fix stands, with one caveat to note in the comment: when no browser window exists, getWindow() builds one through WindowFactory and the post lands before that root has registered its observers, so the launcher will not open on that first ⌘T — the window itself does. That is still strictly better than nothing happening. Same treatment is arguably owed to .closeActiveTab and .findInPage on the lines above, but leave them out of this diff.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. PasswordsWindow.swift:38-44 makes a plain NSWindow that becomes key, OraCommands.swift:26 posts with object: NSApp.keyWindow, and WindowEventScope.windowOrKey (OraRoot.swift:330-333) resolves every browser root's target to its own non-nil window, so the post matches nobody. The Settings window (same title check at OraCommands.swift:53-61) is dead the same way. One more case falls out of the same rule and the same fix: with every window minimised, NSApp.keyWindow is nil, so the post carries no sender, target resolves to the root's own window, and `sender == nil ? keyWindow === target` is nil === window, false — no root claims it, and ⌘T does nothing at all.

kept.title: Every keystroke fetches 200 history rows on the main thread to display six
kept.evidence: `search(_:activeContainerId:)` sets `descriptor.fetchLimit = 200` and the launcher is its only caller (`LauncherViewModel.runLocalSearch` line 113). `historySuggestions` then does `histories.prefix(6)`, so 194 `History` models are materialized and dropped per run. The predicate is two `localizedStandardContains` calls, which no index can serve, so this is a full scan of the space's history table, synchronously on the main thread, at most 40 ms apart while typing (`localSearchDebounce`).
kept.user_impact: Typing in the launcher gets choppier the longer the profile has been used: the scan is between the key going down and the character appearing, and the row budget means most of the work is thrown away.
kept.fix: fetchLimit = 20 is right, and the comment should say why 20 rather than 6: the row score (:404) ranks by visitCount, so the fetch needs more than six most-recent rows to rank from.
kept.verify_reason: Facts confirmed: HistoryManager.swift:165 sets fetchLimit = 200, LauncherViewModel.swift:113 is the only caller, and historySuggestions takes prefix(6) (:395) before anything else sees the rows, so 194 materialised History models are dropped every run. Downgraded from medium because the cost is one bounded fetch at most every 40 ms and I have no measurement showing it is felt; the waste is certain, the choppiness is not.

kept.title: The launcher fades in but is cut off screen, never out
kept.evidence: `dismiss()` sets `isVisible = false` and then `DispatchQueue.main.async { appState.showLauncher = false }`. `BrowserView.swift:201` mounts the panel with `if appState.showLauncher { LauncherView() }`, so the view is torn out one runloop turn (~1 frame) into a 0.12 s opacity animation. `onSubmit` (line 72) and the row tap (`LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:159`) skip `isVisible` altogether and drop `showLauncher` straight to false, so those paths never animate at all.
kept.user_impact: Escape, a click away, or picking a row makes the whole panel and its dimmed backdrop vanish in one frame while the entrance was a smooth 0.12 s fade. Next to Arc or Raycast the asymmetry is the first thing you notice.
kept.fix: Apply the transition, but keep the two paths that immediately open a tab instant. A 0.12 s fade-out on those overlaps the deferred openTab, and the WKWebView build stalls the main thread mid-fade — which is the frozen-panel symptom the comment at LauncherView.swift:69-71 says was already fixed once. So: `.transition(.opacity)` on LauncherView() plus `.animation(AnimationSettings.easeOut(0.12), value: appState.showLauncher)` in BrowserView, delete isVisible and the async in dismiss(), and wrap the submit and row-tap writes in `withTransaction(Transaction(animation: nil))` so a navigation still cuts.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. dismiss() (LauncherView.swift:86-91) drops showLauncher one runloop turn into a 0.12 s fade, and BrowserView.swift:201 unmounts on that flag with no transition and no animation bound to it, so the panel and its dimmed backdrop are cut in one frame. onSubmit (:72) and the row tap (LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:159) never touch isVisible at all. The entrance does animate (onAppear sets isVisible = true), so the asymmetry is real.

kept.title: Suggestion rows are invisible to VoiceOver: no button trait and no action
kept.evidence: The row's only activation is `.onTapGesture { suggestion.action() ... }`. There is no `.accessibilityElement`, `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` or `.accessibilityAction`, so the row reads as loose text with no way to run it, and the "Switch to tab" / "Ask Grok ↩" labels are announced as separate strings. The sidebar's address pill in this same codebase does it properly: `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` plus `.accessibilityAction { openLauncher() }` (SidebarURLDisplay.swift:107-108).
kept.user_impact: A VoiceOver user can type in the launcher but cannot hear one row as one item or activate it; the whole suggestion list is unusable without a mouse or the arrow keys.
kept.fix: Lift the tap body into `private func activate()`, then add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)`, `.accessibilityAction(perform: activate)` next to `.onTapGesture(perform: activate)`.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed by reading the whole view: LauncherSuggestionItem.swift:128-168 has one .onTapGesture and one .onHover and no accessibility modifier anywhere, so each row is a bag of loose Text elements with no button trait and no action. SidebarURLDisplay.swift:105-108 is the in-repo pattern the fix should copy, exactly as claimed.

kept.title: A SwiftUI FocusState path the code says does not work is still wired up and racing AppKit
kept.evidence: LauncherMain passes both `isFocused: isFocused` and `isEditing: true`, and the comment on the next line says the AppKit route is used because "SwiftUI's focus bridge onto the field, `isFocused` above, did not reliably land the caret on ⌘T". The bridge is still fully plumbed: `@FocusState private var isTextFieldFocused` (LauncherView.swift:17), set in `onAppear` and `onDisappear` (207, 245), `var isFocused: FocusState<Bool>.Binding` (LauncherMain.swift:6), and the `field`/`textField` split in LauncherField.swift:76-80 that exists only to apply `.focused()`. The home page passes nil, so the launcher is the sole user. Both mechanisms then aim first responder at the same field in the same update pass, which is a plausible remaining cause of the intermittent "⌘T opens but the caret is not in the field".
kept.user_impact: Two focus owners fighting over one field on every ⌘T, plus about twenty lines of plumbing that the code's own comment marks as not working.
kept.fix: Fix stands; drop the causal claim from the rationale. Also delete the two isTextFieldFocused assignments in LauncherView.onAppear/onDisappear, not just the property, and note that LauncherFocusTests still passes because it asserts on the field editor, not on FocusState.
kept.verify_reason: The dead plumbing is real: LauncherMain.swift:43 passes isFocused alongside isEditing: true, the comment at :44-48 says the SwiftUI route did not land the caret, and the whole chain (LauncherView.swift:17/197/207/245, LauncherField.swift:21 and the field/textField split at :75-82) exists only for a .focused() on an NSViewRepresentable that declares no focusability. Downgraded to low because the second half of the claim — that it races AppKit and explains the intermittent caret loss — is speculation; nothing in the code shows the FocusState bridge writing first responder.

kept.title: The palette's "New Tab" row shows ⌘T but does something ⌘T never does
kept.evidence: `AppCommand("command.newTab", "New Tab", .newTab, shortcut: KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.new)` posts `.newTab`, which `OraRoot` handles with `tabManager.openHomeTab(...)`. The File menu item bound to that same shortcut posts `.showLauncher` (OraCommands.swift:26), as do the sidebar background menu and the space header. The type's own doc says "A row posts the same notification the menu item does" (AppCommand.swift:8-10). `URLBarMenuButton.swift:69` has the same mismatch: a "New Tab" item labelled ⌘T that posts `.newTab`.
kept.user_impact: Typing ">new tab" in the launcher, or picking New Tab from the ⋯ menu, opens a blank home tab, while the ⌘T printed next to the row opens the launcher. Two labels, one chord, two behaviours.
kept.fix: Keep the catalog row, drop only its `shortcut:` argument. `>new tab` is not a no-op: the same catalog feeds the URL bar's inline palette (URLBarField.swift:235 → searchHandler → commandSuggestions), where opening a blank home tab is a real command. Deleting the row removes working behaviour; removing the chord removes the lie. Repointing URLBarMenuButton at .showLauncher is right as written.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. AppCommand.swift:55 prints KeyboardShortcuts.Tabs.new next to a row that posts .newTab (OraRoot.swift:390 → openHomeTab), while the chord it prints posts .showLauncher (OraCommands.swift:26). URLBarMenuButton.swift:68-70 repeats it in the ⋯ menu, which is the user-facing half: an item labelled New Tab ⌘T that does something ⌘T never does.

kept.title: An empty launcher shows nothing, but emptying the field shows five rows
kept.evidence: `defaultSuggestions()` (five rows: the default engine plus Grok, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) is only reachable through `searchHandler("")`, and `searchHandler` only runs from `LauncherField`'s `.onChange(of: text)`. `LauncherView.onAppear` never calls it, so a fresh ⌘T shows a bare field; typing one character and deleting it makes five rows appear under it, as `onSubmit`'s comment acknowledges ("Clearing the field leaves the default suggestions up").
kept.user_impact: The launcher has two different empty states for the same empty field, and the taller one arrives by deleting text.
kept.fix: Note the blast radius: the URL bar's inline dropdown shares this view model (URLBarField.swift:231-236), so clearing the address field stops showing the five rows too. That is the consistent outcome — the URL bar already opens empty because of suppressInitialSearch (:234) — but it belongs in the commit message.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed. defaultSuggestions() (LauncherViewModel.swift:144-159) is reachable only from searchHandler's empty branch (:58-63), searchHandler runs only from LauncherField's onChange(of: text) (LauncherField.swift:101-103), and LauncherView.onAppear never calls it — so ⌘T shows a bare field and emptying the field shows five rows.

kept.title: The field editor is configured twice, once through a helper and once inline
kept.evidence: `updateNSView` lines 212-224 repeat `configureEditorIfNeeded()` (lines 84-99) verbatim: insertion point colour, resizable flags, zero inset, `widthTracksTextView`, container size, clipping line break, one line. The only difference is the copy reads `nsView.bounds.height` where the method reads `bounds.height` on the same view.
kept.user_impact: Two copies of the same six-property setup drift apart the first time one is edited.
kept.fix: Drop `private` from `configureEditorIfNeeded()` and replace the inline block with `nsView.cursorColor = NSColor(cursorColor)` followed by `nsView.configureEditorIfNeeded()`.
kept.verify_reason: Verbatim duplicate confirmed: LauncherTextField.swift:84-99 and :212-224 set the same six properties, differing only in bounds.height vs nsView.bounds.height on the same view.

kept.title: The shared search row shows different placeholder copy in its two homes
kept.evidence: The launcher builds `"Search with \(engine?.name ?? "Google") or enter address"`; the home page hands the same `LauncherField` the literal `"Search or enter address"` (HomePageView.swift:165), as do the URL bar (URLBarField.swift:216) and the sidebar pill. `LauncherField`'s doc comment is "The one search row, shared by the floating launcher (⌘T) and the `aura://home` page so the two cannot drift apart".
kept.user_impact: The same row names the search engine in one place and not in the other, and the placeholder is also the field's accessibility label, so VoiceOver reads two different names for one control.
kept.fix: Move only the no-match branch of getPlaceholder onto LauncherField as a static helper; the match branch (LauncherMain.swift:91-96) is capsule copy the home page has no use for. Leave URLBarField and the sidebar pill alone — naming the engine inside a small pill is a different call.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed: LauncherMain.swift:88 builds 'Search with <engine> or enter address', HomePageView.swift:165 passes the literal 'Search or enter address' to the same LauncherField, and LauncherTextField.swift:165/208 make the placeholder the accessibility label, so VoiceOver reads two names for the shared control.

kept.title: The launcher panel's corner radius is off the app's radius scale
kept.evidence: `static let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 8` drives both the field and, through `LauncherMain.cornerRadius = LauncherField.cornerRadius`, the whole 740 pt panel. `AuraRadius` (Theme.swift:24-28) defines button 6, row 10, pane 13, and the suggestion rows inside the panel already use `AuraRadius.button`. Nothing else in the app uses 8.
kept.user_impact: The largest floating surface in the browser is the only one that does not sit on the radius scale, and its 8 pt outer corner against the rows' 6 pt inner corner is nearly concentric-wrong.
kept.fix: Fix stands; add that the home page's suggestion panel reads LauncherField.cornerRadius, so it moves to 10 with the field and needs no edit of its own. Check the change against ConditionallyConcentricRectangle first — the rows inside are AuraRadius.button (6), and pane 13 outside a 6 pt row is the nesting the rest of the chrome uses.
kept.verify_reason: Confirmed against the scale's own rule at Theme.swift:22-23 ('a literal radius anywhere else is a bug'), and LauncherField.cornerRadius = 8 drives the field, the 740 pt panel (LauncherMain.swift:20) and the home page's suggestion panel (HomePageView.swift:197, :203). One evidence correction: 8 is not unique to the launcher, PlayerIconButtonStyle.swift:15 uses a literal 8 too.

kept.title: Suggestion list takes a binding it never writes, and the field sets a bezel it never draws
kept.evidence: `@Binding var suggestions: [LauncherSuggestion]` is only read (`ForEach(suggestions)`); nothing in the view or in `LauncherSuggestionItem` writes back, unlike `focusedElement`, which the row does write. Both call sites pass `$viewModel.suggestions` (LauncherMain.swift:58, HomePageView.swift:184). Separately, `makeNSView` sets `textField.bezelStyle = .roundedBezel` and then `isBordered = false` and `drawsBackground = false` on the next two lines (LauncherTextField.swift:153-156), so the bezel is never drawn.
kept.user_impact: A write-capable binding on a read-only list invites a future write from the wrong side, and the dead bezel line reads as leftover stock-AppKit setup in a hand-drawn panel.
kept.fix: `let suggestions: [LauncherSuggestion]` and drop the `$` at both call sites; delete the `bezelStyle` line.
kept.verify_reason: Both halves confirmed. LauncherSuggestionsView.swift:4 binds suggestions and only reads it in ForEach (:13); focusedElement is the one the row genuinely writes. LauncherTextField.swift:153-156 sets bezelStyle and then clears isBordered and drawsBackground, so the bezel never draws.

kept.title: Clicking a suggestion opens the tab before the launcher dismisses, so the panel freezes on screen
kept.evidence: The row tap runs `suggestion.action()` and then wraps the dismissal in `DispatchQueue.main.async { appState.showLauncher = false }` (156-162). Every row action defers its own work by one turn for the stated reason that the panel has to be gone first: `historySuggestions` (LauncherViewModel.swift:413 'One turn later, so the dismissal paints before the web view build stalls the main thread'), `typedURLSuggestion` (:310), `openTabSuggestions` (:266), `createAISuggestion` (:236). FIFO on the main queue means the action's block was queued first, so on a click the openTab/restoreTransientState runs first and the dismissal only lands after it returns. The keyboard path does it correctly: `executeCommand()` calls the action and then `onDismiss?()`, which writes `appState.showLauncher = false` synchronously (LauncherViewModel.swift:170, LauncherView.swift:220-222).
kept.user_impact: Pick a suggestion with the mouse and the panel plus its dimmed backdrop sit frozen over the window while WebKit builds the page, then disappear. The same rows in the URL-bar dropdown and on the home page behave the same way. Pick the same row with Enter and it is instant. This is the exact symptom the four deferral comments say was already fixed.
kept.fix: Drop the async wrapper so the flag write lands before the queued open, matching `executeCommand`: `.onTapGesture { suggestion.action(); appState.showLauncher = false; appState.isURLBarEditing = false }`, with the comment saying the row's action defers its own open by a turn, so this write has to be synchronous or it queues behind it.

kept.title: Emptying the field fast leaves the previous query's rows up, and Enter runs one of them
kept.evidence: `searchHandler`'s empty branch (58-63) calls `invalidateAutoSuggestionRequests()` and replaces the list, but never cancels `localSearchTask`; the cancel only happens on the non-empty path at :69. A keystroke closer than `localSearchDebounce` (0.04 s) to the previous run schedules a task that sleeps and then calls `runLocalSearch(text)` with the old text (:75-80), which overwrites `suggestions` and resets `focusedElement` to row 0. So deleting the last characters with key repeat can land a merged list for 'gh' under an empty field, and `executeCommand()` (:164-171) then runs that row's action on Enter. `reset()` (:135-141) cancels the task, which is why the home page (HomePageView.swift:171-175 calls reset on empty) never shows this and the launcher and URL bar do.
kept.user_impact: Hold backspace to clear the launcher and rows for the text you just deleted stay up under an empty field; Enter navigates to one of them instead of doing nothing.
kept.fix: Move the cancel above the guard so every path through `searchHandler` invalidates the in-flight local search: put `localSearchTask?.cancel()` on the line before `guard !text.trimmingCharacters(...)`, and delete the now-duplicate cancel at :69.

kept.title: Typing an address you have visited shows the same page twice, one row under the other
kept.evidence: `merge` dedupes only `links` (`dedupeByURL(links)` at :217); the `typed` row is prepended afterwards at :225 and never compared. `LauncherScoring.urlKey` (:152-158) strips the scheme and trailing slash, so `constructURL(from: "github.com")` = https://github.com and a history row for https://github.com/ collapse to the same key 'github.com' — the dedupe would catch them if the typed row were in the same pass. `HistoryManager.search` matches on `urlString.localizedStandardContains` (HistoryManager.swift:158), so the root entry is returned for exactly the query that produces the typed row.
kept.user_impact: Type a domain you visit often and row 0 ('github.com') and row 1 ('GitHub — https://github.com') are the same destination, which is the most common thing anyone types into the launcher.
kept.fix: Drop link rows the typed row already covers, in `merge` right after the mix, keeping open-tab rows because 'Switch to tab' is a different action: `if let key = LauncherScoring.urlKey(typed?.url) { sortable.removeAll { $0.type == .suggestedLink && LauncherScoring.urlKey($0.url) == key } }`, with the comment saying row 0 already goes there.

dropped.title: Suggestion rows never highlight on hover: the window is not asking for mouse-moved events
dropped.reason: Could not confirm the monitor is silent. The quoted comment (GlobalMouseTrackingArea.swift:170-175) is about the pointer sitting over a WKWebView, where no view tracks mouse moves; with the launcher up the pointer is over SwiftUI content whose rows carry .onHover tracking areas, and tracking-area mouse-moved events reach local monitors. The same raw-monitor idiom backs three other live surfaces (URLBarField.swift:398, FloatingTabSwitcher.swift:311, HomePageView.swift:311), including the URL-bar dropdown where hover highlighting is used constantly, so a claim that it never fires needs a run of the app, not a read. Refuting or confirming this needs one manual pass with the toolbar pinned; I am dropping it rather than guessing.

dropped.title: The home page's one-shot focus never releases the window's first-responder lock
dropped.reason: The latch is real — LauncherTextField.swift:189 only writes wantsFocus when isEditing is non-nil, so the home page's 0.1 s pulse (HomePageView.swift:168, :334-338) sets it true forever — but the user-visible consequence does not survive checking. FirstResponderLock.lock() requires view.window (AuraWindow.swift:63), and the pulse fires in the same pass that inserts the field, which is exactly the case the pendingFocus branch (:196-199) exists for, so the lock often registers nothing. Where it does register, the launcher's own field locks later and overwrites AuraWindow.lockedFirstResponder, and its didBecomeKey observer is registered later so it runs last. The field also unmounts with the home tab (BrowserWebContentView.swift:96-98 is per active tab), which deallocs the lock. Net: leaked state, no symptom I can name.

dropped.title: The field jumps up under the cursor as rows arrive, twice per query
dropped.reason: The behaviour is exactly as described (LauncherPlacement.swift:22-27 centres the measured panel, LauncherView.swift:100 feeds it the panel height), but it is not a defect: the file's own header says the field-anchored version was tried and abandoned because 'the panel drifted downwards as suggestions arrived', and LauncherPlacementTests.grownPanelRecentres pins it deliberately. Reversing a documented, tested design decision on taste is a call for the owner, not an audit finding. The .animation(nil) at LauncherView.swift:121 shows they already weighed the movement and chose to snap it.
